Third consecutive run to hit this channel; open idea 517 is the right home for it. **DESIGN.** Five dials — BAND (664's, 8 rungs), N (3..50, 8), GROSS (0.20..1.00, 8), VOLCAP (0.20..OFF, 8), CADENCE (D/W/M/Q, 4) — each a ladder of books differing in exactly one parameter; a chooser reads each rung's IN-SAMPLE Sharpe (2009-2016 only) and takes the argmax, ties to the smallest rung. By channel (controls excluded): BOOK 0.900 > WINDOW 0.733 > ROUND 0.500. **(2) THE MECHANISM — FALSIFIED.** The queue reads the flip rate as a flatness result. Measured on each dial's own honest IS ladder over 10 (panel, dial) cells, flip rate is uncorrelated with — if anything mildly opposed to — every flatness statistic: **rho(rate, margin) Spearman -0.1515 / Pearson -0.4740; spread -0.1137 / -0.2717; curv -0.1010 / -0.1637; is_sd -0.1137 / -0.2593, n=10** (statistic and n named beside every rho, per idea 564). Window noise moves the choice without informing it. The 49 pairs are 28 distinct ratios selecting only **7 distinct floors**; idea 121's pair is k = $100M; 13 of 98 pairs are unsatisfiable on the ladder. PROTOCOL must state the single number `ticket/bar` and must never present the ticket and the bar as two independent choices. **THE CLAUSE VALUE IS WRONG AT ITS OWN CONSTANTS.** ($10M, 10%) selects **$0.50M** on both instruments, not the **$1M** idea 121 proposes: DV participation is 17.62% at $0M, 11.27% at $0.25M and **9.41% at $0.50M**, so the bar is met one rung below the proposed clause. Idea 121 published $1M because its own ladder had no $0.25M/$0.50M rungs — idea 427 added them — and $1M is selected by only **2 of 45** satisfiable DV pairs (4.4%). This is idea 646's ladder-resolution finding arriving from the constants side. **THE SENSITIVITY, PUBLISHED:** the selected DV floor spans **7 rungs, $0M to $20M**, and **doubling either constant moves the clause 10x** ($10M->$20M at 10% takes the floor from $0.5M to $5M). Across the selectable floors the book spreads **15.10 pp of CAGR, 0.841 of Sharpe and 0.977 of OOS Sharpe** (EWALL/DV/10bps; >= 0.28 OOS on all 12 book x instrument x rung cells) — larger than any effect the clause is meant to protect. Damage is monotone in the floor, replicating idea 427: EWALL DV @10bps CAGR +10.18% ($0M) / +7.05% ($0.5M) / +5.92% ($1M) / -4.92% ($20M), Sharpe/OOS 0.68/0.64 -> 0.47/0.45 -> 0.41/0.38 -> -0.16/-0.34. **RULE 8** (floor chosen on 2010-2016 only, 2017-2026 read once, 96 book-rows committed): the capacity chooser selects $0.50M in 12 of 12 cells and IS and full-sample selection agree, but mean OOS Sharpe is **A capacity 0.2452 / B IS-Sharpe 0.3074 / C NO FLOOR 0.3289** — **the floor costs -0.0838 against no floor at all** and -0.0623 against choosing on IS Sharpe, it beats the no-floor control in **2 of 12** cells, and A and B agree in **0 of 12**. **4a 0/96, 4b 0/96, BOTH 0** at both rungs (SPY 14.13%/0.8615/-33.72%, OOS 0.8820; RULES v2 @10bps 3.80%/0.5710/-14.70%, OOS 0.5665). RECOMMENDATION for the Sunday review: **do not adopt idea 121's ADV clause as written**; a capacity clause must state the single constant `ticket/bar`, state the ladder it is solved on, and carry the measured cost. SURVIVORSHIP (PROTOCOL 9): SMALL439 is a current-constituent screen with the 44 max_1d_move >= 1.0 names dropped and is the ONLY panel with cached volume (U56/broad136 volume is idea 429, needs network), so every level is an upper bound; the load-bearing quantity is the floor-minus-floor contrast inside one panel. `capacity()`'s p25 convention and its single-rebalance ticket are a third and fourth unstated constant, unswept here; the ratio collapse holds whatever they are. Memo `research/backtests/2026-09-10_price-the-CAPACITY-CRITERION-s-own-two-constants_cloud.result.md`. **CONCURRENT REPLICATION (record convention 320R):** a lane B run answered idea 647 the same day, independently, and agrees on every load-bearing number — the ratio collapse is exact in both (their linearity residual 1.7e-18 over 128 points, 40 ratios, 0 within-ratio disagreements), idea 121's $1M is wrong in both, and **their 8-rung answer is this run's $0.50M exactly** (on a 33-rung refined ladder they solve it at **$0.412M**, so a finer ladder drifts the clause value further, sharpening the correction), with 4a 0 and 4b 0 in both and the floor losing to the no-floor control out of sample in both. Their run reaches three things this one does not, all corrections to take: (i) participation is NOT monotone in the floor on VOLSH, so 'the smallest passing rung' needs an explicit up-set check and this run's `select_floor` (a min over the passing set) would mis-state a non-monotone instrument; (ii) the criterion's IS-only answer matches its full-sample answer on only 110/128 pairs (85.9%) — this run tested that at idea 121's pair alone and found 12/12, which would have over-read a grid-wide claim; (iii) the p25 quantile is a THIRD unswept constant and moves the selected rung on 29/64 pairs at p50, which this run flags but does not measure.

The 80.6%/19.4% shape replicates on today's corpus (605 files, 36,695 visited key-bearing sites, 29,868 = 81.4% behind the wall, 18.6% reconstructible, 11.4% self-contained). **NO SINGLE CONVENTION CAN CLEAR THE WALL.** Blocked sites are touched by UNKNOWN/closure 66.2%, LOOP_TARGET 49.0%, IMPORTED 34.2%, TUPLE_UNPACK 31.9%, MULTI_ASSIGN 19.7%, PARAM_NODEFAULT 14.4%; only **31.6%** have a single blocker class (median 3 free names, max 31), and the queue's own diagnosis — locals and undefaulted params — is the SOLE blocker on just **5.4%** of the wall. **THE CONVENTION IS ALREADY 82.3% ADOPTED** (499 of 606 files expose a module-level function whose first parameter is a price name), so idea 643's proposal is a harness to write, not a convention to adopt: MECH=IMPORT (a def-only shell of the file plus a call with (px, vol)) reaches **49 distinct keys across 227 files**, of which **41 are reachable by no static mechanism** — +77% on the 53 the two static rungs find — at **0.845 keys per line of harness against INLINE's 1.828**. Gates: G1 fast runner vs engine.backtest on returns AND turnover, D and W, all three panels (max|dr| 7.0e-16, max|dto| 4.4e-16); G2 cost-rung identity 6.6e-16; G3 the DEFAULT rung is in every ladder; G4 IS/OOS disjoint and exhaustive (1967 + 2434 = 4401); **G5 wscheme's membership distance and phase's target distance are EXACTLY 0 — by construction, gated, not asserted.** **RESULT 1 — the frequency law does not transfer:** held-out SELECTION **14/24**, TRADING **9/24**, Fisher exact **p = 0.2476**, and the SELECTION side is a coin flip against its own null (sign p = 0.541). **RESULT 2 — class is not the special cut:** all **35** balanced 4-4 partitions of the eight dials were scored and the a-priori SELECTION/TRADING cut ranks **31 of 35** on win-rate gap, exact **p = 0.886**; over all eight dials 31/48 vs 30/48, Fisher **p = 1.000**; on 621's OWN anchors the win-rate ordering **REVERSES** (SELECTION 17/24 vs TRADING **21/24**, with **gross 12/12**). **RESULT 3 — what survives is SIZE, not FREQUENCY:** excluding exact ties (the chooser picking its own control) SELECTION wins at a median **+0.0744** OOS Sharpe and TRADING at **+0.0021** — a **35x** gap in magnitude with none in frequency; Spearman(measured membership distance, per-dial median dSharpe) **+0.884** over 8 dials and **+0.388** over 96 cells, against only **+0.284** on win rate. `gross` wins 12/12 at a median of +0.0017, a win worth nothing. **RESULT 4 — the mechanism is confirmed even as the law fails:** the SET-ONLY leg (this dial's holdings, weighted the default way) reproduces the FULL leg **rung for rung** on all four selection dials and is **0/48** on all four trading dials; the WGT-ONLY leg is 0/48 everywhere except wscheme (5/48). **RESULT 5 — the warning case:** `phase` moves no target at all, yet its rule-8 pick beats its default by **+0.108** OOS Sharpe on u56 and **+0.188** on small439 — idea 412's phase nuisance harvested by a chooser and indistinguishable from content in any win-rate table. Caveats: survivorship (idea 54) on all three panels, SMALL439 drops 44 max_1d_move>=1.0 tickers and only its within-panel contrasts are read; warm-up index[300] not [260] because the longest ladder rung needs 273 closes, so the anchors' levels differ slightly from 621's; eight dials is a small denominator and p = 0.886 rules the cut out as SPECIAL, it does not prove the classes identical. - 2026-09-10 (lane C, idea 644 does-PROTOCOL-need-a-T2-DATING-clause-beside-T1) — **ANSWERED. YES, PROTOCOL needs a T2 DATING clause beside T1 — and the load-bearing finding is that it CANNOT be written as SYNTAX. No RULES change, no PROTOCOL edit (rule 6, Sunday review), no book promoted, no KEEP claimed, no memo; RULES.md, PROTOCOL.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Idea 426 found the hole (its rule-8 chooser picks `px.iloc[-1]/px - 1.0` in 4 of 4 cells: forward-dated, T1-PASS, invisible to rule 8's date split) and priced ONE exclusion — but it implemented that exclusion as a hand-fixed regex. **THE INSTRUMENT: T2 is the time-axis mirror of T1's name-axis perturbation.** T1 perturbs across NAMES (`px -> px @ diag(c)`) and requires the consumed value not to move; T2 replaces every row STRICTLY AFTER a cut date with a perturbed copy and requires no cell of the key DATED AT OR BEFORE the cut to move. That is the queue's clause read literally, made executable, and sampling-error-free in the same sense T1 is — a deterministic invariance check under a seeded operator, not an estimated correlation. **TUNED PARAMETERS, exactly the two the queue names: CLAUSE FORM (SYN = 426's regex verbatim; SYN+ = the same widened by hand with bfill/iloc[-k]/tail; OP1 = certificate at 1 cut; OP3 = certificate at 3 cuts) x CORPUS (TRUTH20 hand-truth / CENSUS111 / BOOK16); all 12 cells reported.** **GATE A — TRUTH20 (10 causal keys, 10 leaking keys, ground truth written before any form ran): the REGEX CLEARS 7 OF 10 GENUINELY FORWARD-DATED KEYS** — a full-sample `px.max()`, `(px - px.mean())/px.std()`, `px.rank(axis=0)`, `px.rolling(21, center=True).mean()`, `px.iloc[::-1].cummax().iloc[::-1]`, `(px-px.min())/(px.max()-px.min())` and `px.bfill()`. Hand-widening the regex still clears 6/10. **OP1 and OP3 are 20/20: zero false clearances AND zero false rejections.** A syntax list cannot adjudicate keys nobody has looked at; a certificate can. **THE BACK-FILL (the queue's own ask):** idea 426's 111-key census re-read from its committed `.backfill.csv` (T1 72 PASS / 39 FAIL reproduced exactly, admitted-class counts exact) and certified under all four forms in 4.1s (37 ms/key): **T2 FAIL 8 / PASS 103, the 8 reaching 7 committed scripts.** **SYN and OP3 AGREE EXACTLY ON THIS CORPUS — the same 8 keys — so the certificate's extra reach is currently UNEXERCISED, and that is reported as a MISS on pre-registered P2 rather than dressed up:** every leak the record carries today is `iloc[-1]`- or `shift(-k)`-shaped (5 terminal-ratio variants, forward shifts of 5/21/252 days), and no census key contains a full-sample reducer, `bfill`, `center=True` or `rank(axis=0)` — checked in the artefact, not assumed. The certificate is adopted because it is the form that keeps working, not because it finds more today. **T2 IS NOT A RELABELLING OF T1: the 2x2 is 64 PASS/PASS, 8 T1-PASS/T2-FAIL, 39 T1-FAIL/T2-PASS, 0 FAIL/FAIL — THE TWO FAILURE SETS ARE DISJOINT.** That falsifies pre-registered P3 ('all four corners non-empty') with a stronger reading: on this corpus the clauses never fire together, so adopting either one alone leaves the other's ENTIRE failure set admitted. **THE BOOK — idea 426's grid, re-priced under the T2 column.** Two tuned book parameters, KEY x m, unchanged from 426; the 16-key set re-derived from 426's own mechanical rule gives an **identical kid->expr map**; `fast_bt` == `engine.backtest` **6.939e-18** at 0 and 10 bps. **426's grid reproduces EXACTLY: 4a 0/420 at every rung (0/5/10/25 bps); 4b 68 / 57 / 48 / 12 of 420, deduped for the shared m=0 control 55 / 44 / 35 / 12 of 364.** Only K10 (`px.iloc[-1]/px - 1.0`) is T2-FAIL in the book set, under all four clause forms. Gross 0.7499-0.7504 across the whole 10-bps grid (spread 4.45e-04), so the tilt moves the cross-section and never the exposure. Two independent processes produce byte-identical `.backfill.csv` and `.walkforward.csv`. **RULE 8 — THE DECOMPOSITION IDEA 426 COULD NOT DO.** (KEY, m) chosen on 2010-2016 IS Sharpe, 2017-2026 read once, 4 (panel, book) cells: **T1 alone +0.0000 (identical pick 4/4), T2 alone -0.3292 (moves the pick 4/4), T1 and T2 together -0.4508.** 426 published the first and third and could not say which clause carried it: **T2 carries 73.0% of the joint price on its own, and T1 adds the remaining -0.1216 only CONDITIONAL on T2** — because the arm T2 leaves behind is **T1-FAIL in 4 of 4 cells** (K02, the 200d mean tilted -1.00, in three; K08, a panel handle, in one). T1 is inert alone and NOT inert given T2: a record that adopted T2 alone would publish a book resting on a degree-1 key. The order is T1 **and** T2, not T1 **or** T2. Read the sign the right way round — a NEGATIVE price is the clause WORKING; the arm removed is U56/MA200 K10 at m=+1.00, OOS 21.58%/1.527/-22.25% against SPY 15.32%/0.876/-33.72% and RULES v2 9.48%/1.279/-12.05%, and that Sharpe was never earnable. A control chooser drawing ONLY from the T2-FAIL pool reproduces the ungated chooser's pick in 4 of 4 cells, i.e. rule 8's ungated chooser IS the oracle chooser. Rule 8 passed over **10 arms** that clear 4b at the protocol rung, are T1-PASS AND T2-PASS, and beat their own m=0 control out of sample. No rule-8 pick passes 4b — every one fails the drawdown leg except the U56/MA200 m=0 control, which loses 4a. **PRE-REGISTERED: P1 HIT (7 cleared), P2 MISS (8 vs 8), P3 MISS (0 FAIL/FAIL), P4 HIT (price -0.3292, 4a 0/420).** **THE CLAUSE, drafted report-only (full text in `.console.txt` PART 5):** clause 11 sits BESIDE clause 10, with (a) a reproducibility gate, (b) the causality certificate at >=3 cuts as the ADJUDICATOR and the regex allowed only as a reader's aid, (c) necessary-not-sufficient and independent of T1 with the disjointness stated, and (d) T2 must run BEFORE rule 8 for the same reason T1 must (idea 195): rule 8 splits by DATE and a terminal-dated key is dated at T in both halves. **SURVIVORSHIP (PROTOCOL 9):** U56 and SMALL439 are current-constituent lists, SMALL439 doubly so (it additionally drops names with `max_1d_move >= 1.0` per data/small_meta.csv); no book is proposed on either and only same-days, same-book contrasts are read. **LIMITS, stated not buried:** the census is idea 426's reachable 19.4% of key-bearing sites — the free-variable wall is 80.6% and caps T2 exactly as it caps T1 (idea 643's question), so the T2 column is worth precisely the reach of the convention that feeds it; and the certificate runs on a 500d x 100-name slice, so a key whose future-reading falls entirely outside that slice would not be detected. - 2026-09-10 (cloud, idea 632 re-cut-every-published-BINDING-BAR-claim-as-a-STEP-NORMALISED-argmin) — **ANSWERED; the raw `m_bind` column KILLED as a publishable claim. No RULES change, no book promoted, no KEEP claimed; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py, baseline.py and PROTOCOL.md untouched.** Census: 83 committed `research/backtests/*.csv` file x family blocks carry the complete five-margin set (`m_H1/m_H2/m_OOS` in SHARPE units, `m_DD` in MaxDD fraction, `m_CAGR` in CAGR fraction), 81 of them with >=8 rows and so stating a claim — **105,504 cells**. Re-cut under four unit-free normalisers, the published modal binding bar survives on **0.568 (SD) / 0.556 (IQR) / 0.259 (RANK)** of claims and cell-level agreement is 0.722 / 0.695 / 0.546 — i.e. **44% of the record's binding-bar claims do not survive a unit-free re-read**. The failure is concentrated: the record's **`H2 binds` family goes 28 claims -> 0** (H2 is the smallest-dispersion Sharpe bar, so it wins a raw min it would never win in noise units) and `DD` goes 17 -> 41. The 4b-PASSING subset is the sturdiest claim set (survival 0.833) and the FAIL4b subset the weakest (0.537), which is the wrong way round for a column the record uses mostly to explain failures. The record already contains its own precedent: `2026-09-09_does-a-random-sub-panel-pass-4b-because-the-CAGR-floor-moves_B.census.csv` publishes `binding` (z-normalised) beside `binding_raw` over 25,153 rows; they disagree on **26.0%** and flip the headline (raw modal CAGR, z-normalised modal DD). Idea 408's 41.3% disagreement is a UNIT effect, not a density effect. A fresh 351-point grid whose spacing this file controls (3 panels x 3 dials x 2 densities, all points committed) prices the two channels: the unit channel moves 35% of argmins (SD agrees with RAW on 0.655, IQR 0.650, SENS 0.641, RANK 0.265) while the density channel moves at most 15% (invariance RAW 1.000, IQR 1.000, SD 0.950, RANK 0.950, SENS 0.850) — and SD/IQR carry a second unpriced defect, dependence on WHICH points the publisher chose to print. **IQR is the only normaliser here that is both unit-free and exactly density-invariant.** Rule 8 (choose on 2008-2016, evaluate 2017-2026 untouched): the normaliser changes the pick in **18 of 18** cells and is worth **+0.019 OOS Sharpe** at best (RAW 0.8661 -> SENS 0.8854 over 90 picks; SD 0.8707, IQR 0.8730, RANK 0.8739), with SENS the only normaliser whose picks beat SPY out of sample on average (+0.0055) — but all five concede -0.106 to -0.125 to the live RULES v2 book, on every panel (pick vs v2 vs SPY OOS Sharpe: U56 1.129 / 1.288 / 0.876; B136 0.972 / 1.121 / 0.882; SMALL439 0.521 / 0.567 / 0.882). Both KEEP paths on all 351 fresh points: 32 pass 4b (all on the `gross` dial, U56 18 / B136 14 — the ladder idea 585 already owns) and 5 pass 4a (SMALL439 `band`); of the 90 rule-8 picks 16 pass 4b and 1 passes 4a. **No KEEP claimed.** Proposed as a reporting habit and NOT written into PROTOCOL by this run: publish the normaliser beside every `m_bind`, and read the 28 committed `H2 binds` claims as "no bar binds in noise units". SURVIVORSHIP (PROTOCOL 9): B136 and SMALL439 are current constituent lists, so their absolute levels are biased up and none is a tradable estimate; SMALL439 additionally drops the 44 names with `data/small_meta.csv max_1d_move >= 1.0`; only the within-panel RAW-vs-normalised contrasts, taken on identical books, are meant to survive that.

PROTOCOL wording proposed, not applied.** Idea 401 showed a 4b margin quoted without a scale is uninterpretable and asked for `binding bar / margin / one-step motion` as three required LEADERBOARD columns, back-filled. This run does the back-fill on the six adopted constants of RULES v1/v2 (band, gross, K, n, f, vol), each swept on its own host book, over 3 panels x 3 grid densities = **1,551 grid points, all committed** (`.grid.csv`, `.backfill.csv`, `.rule8.csv`, `.noleverage.csv`). Two tuned parameters and no more: PANEL and STEP_SCALE; the dials, their host books and their adopted values are read from RULES.md and baseline.py, not chosen here. Three pre-registered gates all pass, including **G2**, which asserts the memoised host books reproduce `baseline.rules_v2_weights` and `rules_v1_weights` at their adopted values at **0.000e+00** — so the dials sweep the real adopted constants — and **G3**, which asserts the adopted value is on-grid at all three densities and gives the identical book at each (**0.000e+00**, nothing interpolated).

  **PART A, CENSUS — the three columns are effectively absent from the record.** 4,492 LEADERBOARD rows, **550** with KEEP in the verdict column. Of those 550, **16 (2.9%)** name a binding bar, **23 (4.2%)** name a margin and **1 (0.2%)** names a step or a spacing; over all 4,492 rows, 111 / 230 / **11**. CHANGELOG: 318 entries, 80 name a margin, **6** name a step or spacing. Idea 401's `<0.5 grid steps` reading is today reconstructible from the published text for **one committed KEEP row out of 550**.

  **THE CORRECTION, and it is to the proposal itself.** Idea 409 found window width in POINTS is not comparable across grid densities. `steps = margin / one-step motion` has the same defect by construction, and this run measures it: halving and quartering the published spacing multiplies the reported `steps` by a median **2.089** (IQR 3.117, only **42.9%** of cells within 2x), so a publisher makes any constant look about twice as safe by publishing a 4x finer grid. The spacing-free form — **dial distance to the flip = margin / |dm/dc|, in the dial's own units** — has median x4/x1 ratio **1.000** (IQR 0.755), i.e. unbiased under a change of density with comparable dispersion. And `steps` is **infinite on 12 of 54 cells (22.2%)** — `f` on all three panels at all three densities, `vol` on U56 — because the binding bar does not move at all for one step of the dial; even `step_delta` itself is not proportional to the spacing (x1/x4 ratio 0.549 to 14.49, median 2.089), because the margin surface is not locally linear. **PROPOSED (Sunday review, not applied):** the three required columns are **binding bar / signed margin / dial distance to the flip**, with the **published spacing** stated beside them so a reader can convert; NOT one-step motion.

  **PART B, BACK-FILL.** At the record's own published spacing, **0 of 18 adopted constants clear 4b and 0 of 18 clear 4a**, with margins from **−0.0195** (U56, gross, binding CAGR) to **−0.3564** (B136, f/n/vol, binding H2) and binding bars splitting 6 CAGR / 6 H1 / 6 H2. Idea 401's `4 of 19 passing cells` cannot be reproduced on the adopted constants themselves, because on these host books there are no passing cells at the adopted values to count.

  **PART D/E, THE KEEP PATHS, with a correction the record should carry.** **4b passes on 72 of 1,551 points — but 56 of the 72 (77.8%) sit at gross > 1.00, i.e. the book BORROWS**, which PROTOCOL 2 forbids unless the idea says so and which idea 402 prices at 300 bps this file does not charge. Binding bar **CAGR, margin +0.0097**; admissible band **gross [0.95, 1.15]** at the published 0.05 spacing and from **0.925** at x4, i.e. 0.083 of gross of room — not idea 401's knife-edge case. - 2026-09-10 (cloud, idea 630 price-the-ELAPSED-DAYS-drift-as-a-standing-reproduction-tolerance) — **ANSWERED; METHOD, no KEEP, no PARK. No RULES change, no book promoted; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched. PROTOCOL wording proposed, not applied.** Idea 409 showed idea 401's u56 non-reproduction is the daily-close job APPENDING rows, not vendor restatement, and that the drift GROWS with elapsed days. This run prices that growth on a **FROZEN** panel (the same committed CSV, truncated), so the append channel is isolated exactly and nothing is restated: 3 panels x 5 books x 7 base vintages x 9 elapsed-day steps x 3 end-date rules = **2,835 drift rows and 840 verdict points, all committed** (`.drift.csv`, `.verdicts.csv`, `.books.csv`). Two tuned parameters and no more: PANEL {U56, B136, SMALL439} and END_DATE_RULE {LIVE, PIN_BOUNDARY, PIN_END}; the 5 books, 7 bases and 9 k-steps are corpus axes held identical in every cell. Four pre-registered gates all pass, including **G2 truncation invariance at 0.000e+00** (the file's premise: every book here is causal, so a vintage really is a window over one returns series) and **G4**, which turns idea 409's finding into an assertion — under LIVE at k=55 the calendar-pinned IS leg drifts **0.000e+00** while H1 drifts **8.098e-02** on the very same returns.

  **THE LAW.** The q95 tolerance is a **square root of elapsed days**: fitting q95|drift_X|(k) = a·k^b over k in {1,2,3,5,8,13,21,34,55} gives b = **0.501 (Sharpe), 0.565 (H1), 0.553 (H2), 0.469 (OOS), 0.452 (CAGR)**, r 0.89–0.99, i.e. b = 1/2 to within the fit. Quotable form: **tol_Sharpe(k) ≈ 8.94e-03·√k, tol_H1 ≈ 9.14e-03·k^0.57, tol_H2 ≈ 1.81e-02·k^0.55, tol_OOS ≈ 2.35e-02·k^0.47, tol_CAGR ≈ 1.70e-03·k^0.45.** Level drift scales ≈1/T over T = 3,432–4,377 rows (median d_Sharpe·T = 22.6–29.1) and breaks at the shortest base (T = 2,928, 55.7), so the constant is a sample-length statistic, not a universal one.

  **THE RECORD'S BARS DO NOT SURVIVE IT.** Against idea 401's hand-typed 5e-4, **96.6%** of Sharpe re-reads, **98.2%** of H2 and **97.8%** of OOS are already outside; against idea 520's proposed flat 1e-6, 100%/100%/100%. Even a 1e-2 bar fails 39.9% / 62.4% / 59.3%. **A single trading day busts 5e-4 at the median** (d_Sharpe 2.12e-03, d_H2 4.13e-03). Pinning the END DATE (PIN_END) removes **all ten metrics to 0.000e+00 exactly** (G3).   **PROPOSED (Sunday review, not applied here).** PROTOCOL 10: *every reproduction gate must publish the END DATE of the panel it was computed on, and a re-read must either truncate to that end date (PIN_END, which reproduces at 0.000e+00 by construction) or state days_since and be judged against tol_X(days_since) = a_X·sqrt(days_since) with the a_X above.* PIN_END is the recommendation: it is exact, free, and needs no fitted constant. The days_since column is the fallback for gates that must read the live panel, and PROTOCOL should note that a moving `len(r)//2` is a second, separable defect that a pinned boundary date fixes on its own.

What they DO need is a **crossing cost** column: the rung where each family's win rate falls below 0.50 is **ABS 10 bps — PROTOCOL's own rung, where idea 42's family is already a coin flip at 0.481 — QEXP 20 bps and QROLL 50 bps**, and weekly cadence roughly triples it (median c* 5.7->16.8 / 17.1->40.3 / 36.8->97.7 bps; QROLL weekly still wins 0.398 at 100 bps where QROLL daily is at 0.028). On an equal-weight-eligible book the two are near the same variable by construction, and that is the book idea 295's quoted cell used. **(2) THE SLOPE DIES WHERE THE COLLINEARITY IS HIGHEST:** evol vs MaxDD goes 4/4 significant -> 0/4 on EWall with book vol in the regression (t -8.74..-5.96 -> +0.90..+1.94) and survives 3/4 -> 3/4 on top10 and top20. **METHOD FINDING: the linear control and the ratio control DISAGREE** (`ratio` returns +8.0..+8.9 on EWall, the opposite sign, because 1/bookvol dominates that specification; DDnorm = MaxDD/bookvol keeps t -4.3..-3.2), so neither is quoted alone. M rises **+0.1971 -> +0.8826** (B136) and **-0.0834 -> +0.5865** (SMALL484). The two curves are not competing hypotheses about the panel; one of them is a measurement of N. **(2) THE CROSSOVER.** At D=50 `sd` beats M in 8/12 (B136) and 9/12 (SMALL484) cells — idea 252 reproduced. **At D=500 `sd` beats M in 0/12 on both panels.** M catches `sd` in 12/12 cells on both panels under both lambda rules, median D\* = 100, largest D\* 150 on book Sharpe (200 including the premium column); the gap closes monotonically in log D in **48 of 48** panel x lambda-rule x cell curves and every one crosses inside the ladder, so nothing needed extrapolation. **(3) THE SECOND CASUALTY.** Idea 252's secondary bar, the '72 of 72' nested gain from adding `sd` to M, is also an N=50 statement: median gain falls **+0.2344 -> +0.0031** on B136 (direction survives, positive 9/12, ~75x smaller) and **inverts** on SMALL484 (**-0.0009**, positive in only 3/12). Idea 83's 62% is STRUCTURAL, not a power result about the scalar; idea 78's test C is safe outright on this axis. No RULES change, no KEEP-candidate, no memo; RULES.md, PROTOCOL.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Idea 83 controlled a draw's winner content with ONE scalar (W = mean full-sample annualised log return of the draw's own names, plus W_max) and dispersion survived at pooled n=20 CAND-20 R2(sd) 0.3062 (t +8.08) -> pR2(sd|W) 0.1899 (t +5.87), kill 0.620; idea 83 itself flagged the weakness ("W is one scalar per draw; a name-by-name fixed-effect design would be stronger and is not run"). This run runs it: the control becomes the draw's full **136-column membership indicator matrix**, fitted by ridge, N=50 draws per k cell against 136 columns so the design is rank-deficient by construction. **REPRODUCTION GATE FIRST, and it is a membership gate because M is the whole object this run adds**: the 150 sub-panels are re-drawn from idea 78's `SEED_B + k` and **six independent membership-derived columns of idea 83's committed draws.csv (W, W_IS, W_sd, W_max, W_cw, W_cov) are recomputed from the reconstructed name sets — max abs difference 8.3e-17 / 8.3e-17 / 9.7e-17 / 5.6e-17 / 4.4e-16 / 0.0 over 300 rows**, so M is provably idea 83's own; draws.csv against idea 78's committed gridB.csv reads **0.000e+00** on 17 numeric columns with f4b strings identical in 300/300; U56/CAND20 12.6530%/1.09172/-18.3083% and U56/RULES v1 6.4194%/0.66110/-13.8278% recomputed from `engine.backtest`. **The 450 books are NOT re-run — this run changes no book; every book metric is read from idea 83's committed grid.** Two tuned parameters, both fully reported at every point: ridge penalty lam in {0.5, 2, 8, 32, 128, 512} and scheme in {in-sample, out-of-fold(10, deterministic folds by draw index)}; **288 grid points, all reported**. **(1) THE HAZARD, named before any number was read, and it is real.** `sd` is a deterministic function of membership, so a 136-parameter model fitted on 50 draws can absorb sd by overfitting the same y it is being tested against. The **POWER AUDIT** — a leg no scalar-control design can run, because one number cannot span a dispersion — shows the in-sample name-level fit reproduces `sd` ITSELF at **R2 0.9981 / 0.9996 / 0.9996** (k = 20/40/80, lam=0.5, trace(H) 47.9-48.9 of N=50), against **-0.040 / +0.409 / +0.150** out of fold. **An in-sample 136-column control cannot leave a coefficient on sd to test at any penalty below lam~128.** So the pre-registered verdict is read on the OUT-OF-FOLD scheme only; the in-sample column is reported for completeness. **(2) THE TEST, on idea 83's own pre-registered bar (kill = pR2(sd|F)/R2(sd) < 1/3 AND |t| < 2), reused verbatim so the two runs are directly comparable.** Headline cell (n=20, CAND Sharpe, pooled over 150 draws) at the IS-cross-validated penalty lam*=2: **pR2(sd | F_oof) 0.2067, t +6.19, kill 0.675** — against the scalar's 0.1899 / +5.87 / 0.620 on the SAME rows. Both legs of the kill bar are missed at **every** penalty (OOF kill 0.599-1.094, t +5.75..+8.60). Across all 96 book-Sharpe grid points **sd survives |t|>2 in 92 out of fold and in only 17 in sample** (OOF kill median 0.851; IS median 0.056). The four OOF failures are one cell, n=5/k=40/CAND Sharpe, whose **univariate** t is already only +2.18 and where idea 83's scalar also leaves it insignificant (+1.51) — the name-level control is not what kills it. On the RANKING PREMIUM sd survives in 5 of 48 OOF points, consistent with idea 83's finding that nothing was there to contaminate. **(3) NESTED OUT-OF-FOLD PREDICTION, immune to overfit in both directions: adding sd to the name-level model raises out-of-fold R2 in 72 of 72 book-Sharpe grid points**, median gain **+0.2391** (range +0.0305..+0.5391). The name-additive model alone predicts at OOF R2 -0.197..+0.424 (median +0.151); **`sd` ALONE predicts at +0.026..+0.375 (median +0.289)** — one dispersion number out-predicts the whole 136-name additive model on this panel. **(4) RULE 8 — the new selector is a NULL.** S7 FE-RESID-DISP (max IS sd after the out-of-fold name-level fit of IS Sharpe is regressed out, penalty chosen by IS cross-validation on IS data only, whole ladder reported) **selects the SAME draw (k=20, d=39) as idea 83's raw-dispersion S2 at ALL SIX penalties**: OOS 9.03% / **1.1841** / -9.43%, regret **+0.2922** over the do-nothing control (full B136 CAND-20, OOS 12.49% / 0.892 / -20.05%), z +1.66 in cell. So the name-level residualisation adds no selector content — in contrast to idea 83's SCALAR residualisation S5, which did move the pick and moved it worse (+0.0639). Input skill vs OOS Sharpe: IS Sharpe +0.2166, IS sd +0.1944, IS sd|W_IS +0.2315, **IS sd|F_oof +0.2053**, IS W_IS +0.0737, IS n_elig -0.2617. **(5) BOTH KEEP PATHS, and a restatement the record needs.** No new book: 4a **276/450** and 4b **87/450** reproduce idea 83 exactly (CAND20 146/40, CAND5 32/2, EWall 98/45). **But those 4a counts are against RULES v1, superseded on 2026-09-06.** Restated against the LIVE **RULES v2** — which on B136 reads 8.03% / 1.106 / -12.24%, halves 1.229/0.984, OOS 1.119, against v1's 6.39% / 0.635 / -21.19% — **the 300 CAND books fall from 4a 178/300 to 4a 3/300** (failing-bar census H2 277, H1 268, DD 263); EWall halves were never written to the committed grid so the restatement covers the 300 CAND books. Over the 8 rule-8 selector arms: 4a-v1 8/8, **4a-v2 2/8** (S2 and S7, the same draw), **4b 1/8** (S3 only, which ideas 78/253 already identify as this cell's random-sub-panel base rate, 23-39% on B136). **Nothing is promotable.** **WHAT THE RECORD MUST NOW CARRY, beyond the answer: the design the QUEUE itself proposed is only valid fitted OUT OF FOLD.** Run the obvious way — ridge the membership matrix in-sample and residualise — it reports kill **0.000** at t **-0.10** and would have retracted idea 78's test C for a pure overfitting reason. The power audit is what separates the two readings. And every 4a count published before 2026-09-06 is measured against a book far weaker than the one now live. **Caveats:** survivorship (rule 9) — universe_broad.json is current constituents, which is the premise under test rather than a caveat to it, and it makes the control CONSERVATIVE (returns of names already known to have survived under-state true winner content), cutting AGAINST a surviving sd; 150 draws on one panel; N=50 against 136 columns is a hard regime and the honest OOF R2(F) is sometimes negative (-0.188 pooled at lam=0.5); the name-level model is ADDITIVE in names and `sd` is not, so the surviving coefficient is precisely the statement that dispersion carries something a name-additive composition model does not; ideas 39/49's inverted gate and idea 128's shallow IS drawdown window bias every rule-8 selector here identically, as in idea 83. No RULES change, no PROTOCOL edit, no KEEP, no new book; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Idea 207 set clause 11b's draw count at K=100 using a flip rate measured on `floor(400/K)` DISJOINT blocks — 190 pairwise comparisons per configuration at K=20 falling to ONE at K=200. This run enumerated the whole rotation POPULATION instead of sampling it (N = J-1 = 974/974/869 on U56/BROAD136/SMALL439, over idea 207's own 90 configurations x 2 cost rungs = 180 rows, **84,510 null backtests**), which gives an exact population band and an exact population verdict to score any K-draw against. **(1) The confound is real, and it reappears at the new noisiest rung.** The disjoint estimator's replicate sd rises exactly as its comparison count falls (1128 pairs/config at K=20 -> 1 at K=400; sd MAX 0.0015 -> 0.0073, Q95 0.0017 -> 0.0114) and it renders the Q95 ladder NON-MONOTONE (0.0437 -> 0.0359 -> 0.0403 at K=100/200/400). The paired fixed-B estimator — B=200 disjoint block pairs at EVERY K, R=8 replicates — is monotone (0.0749/0.0535/0.0424/0.0365/0.0348) and its sd at K=400 is 0.0004 against 0.0114, a factor of 28. Idea 207's 'Q95 disagreement rises 2.50% -> 3.33% from K=100 to K=200 while its band sd keeps falling' was its estimator, not the clause. **(2) The Monte Carlo turns out to be unnecessary.** A K-draw's verdict depends on the draw only through X = the number of sampled |dSharpe| reaching the real |dSharpe|; with an order-statistic band at level q it clears iff X <= K - ceil(qK), and X ~ Hypergeom(N, M, K) in the population's own exceedance count M. So P(clear at K), P(error at K) and P(flip) are EXACT, carry zero sampling error and need ONE integer per configuration. On the MAX band, where the form is exact, it matches the B=200 Monte Carlo to 0.0009 across the ladder (MC se 0.0026); the Q95 convention gap is <= 0.0045 and is reported. **(3) The MAX band clears 0 of 180 configurations at its own limit** (Q95 clears 20.6%), so every MAX `clears` anywhere in the record is a finite-K false positive and MAX's error ladder (17.68% at K=20 down to 1.03% at K=400) is its SIZE, nothing else. **(4) K=100 is a FLOOR, not an optimum:** Q95 error against the population runs 6.76/4.30/3.41/2.67/2.02% and the share of configurations erring above the clause's own 5% size runs 22.8/15.0/9.4/7.2/6.7% at K=20/50/100/200/400 — monotone, no interior optimum, and under half a percentage point of gain past K~200 for double the compute. **(5) Two pre-registrations were REJECTED and are reported as such:** P4 predicted MAX's error would stay above 5% at K=400 and it is 1.03% (a 400-draw is 41% of a 974-member population, so the sample max nearly IS the population max — the bias argument had the direction right and the finite-population scale wrong), and P5 predicted Q95 below MAX at every K >= 50, true at 50/100/200 and false at 400 for the same reason. P2's literal '<2x' clause on the fixed-B sd is also rejected (3.2-3.3x); the ratio was the wrong scale, the level at the noisy end is the 28x above. **(6) Rule 8:** clause read on <= 2016-12-31 only, overlay point chosen there, 2017-2026 read once, 18 cells — all 12 clause-gated arms lose to do-nothing (best -0.0029, worst -0.0742, mean OOS Sharpe 0.7024-0.7737 vs the control's 0.7766) and the IS-Sharpe argmax control loses too (-0.0361); ORACLE-OOS buys +0.0431 (t +3.86, 12/12), so the ladder HAS headroom and the gate cannot find it. **Fourteenth consecutive do-nothing win.** **(7) Both KEEP paths on 180 real rows: 4a 37/180, 4b 28/180, BOTH 2/180**; 27 of the 28 4b passes are U56 and the best-Sharpe 4b row (U56 DDCTL 0.15/0.5 @10bps, 1.1075 / -18.21% / OOS 1.1775) is numerically IDENTICAL to its own untreated control, i.e. the overlay never fires — idea 435's point again. **Reproduction:** the cached-primitive `bt_np` equals `p191.fast_backtest` at 0.0e+00 on returns AND turnover; idea 191's own three gates pass on all three panels; idea 201's published bands reproduce BIT-EXACTLY on BROAD136 and SMALL439 (median 8e-17, 0 rows over 1e-4) and drift up to 1.49e-2 on U56 only — the single panel whose price file has been re-cached since idea 201 ran, which is what a vintage drift should look like and is reported rather than asserted away. A cloud-lane script for the same idea was committed today with no console, no CSVs and no leaderboard rows; this run is an independent second construction that reaches the same hypergeometric identity by a different route. **Recommendation (proposed only, for Sunday review):** state clause 11b in terms of M rather than K — clear iff M <= N - ceil(0.95N) over the enumerated population, else draw K and publish P(Hypergeom(N, M, K) <= K - ceil(0.95K)) beside the verdict — and never report a MAX band, which over the enumerated population clears 0 of 180 and is therefore a pure size dial. **INDEPENDENT REPLICATION: the cloud lane reached Done first with a closed-form-first read of the same idea and the two runs AGREE on every shared count — KEEP 4a 37/180, 4b 28/180, BOTH 2/180 identical; the hypergeometric identity independently derived; 12 of 12 clause-gated arms losing; K=100 a floor and not an optimum; and idea 207's estimator unbiased in its CENTRE (disjoint 0.1022 vs fixed-B 0.1011 at K=20) and wrong only in its CONFIDENCE. The one difference is the estimand: the cloud lane measures error against the nominal 0.05 permutation target and reads MAX's error as RISING 0.0741 -> 0.1596 in K, this run measures it against the ENUMERATED POPULATION verdict and reads it as FALLING 0.1768 -> 0.0103; both say MAX's clear rate collapses in K, and this run supplies the limit point — the population MAX clear rate is exactly 0 of 180.**

The size control is **UNDER-POWERED and reported as such** (zero-information overlay, 20 cells per kind: ROT 0/20, RS1 2/20, RS2 0/20, RS4 3/20, RS8 2/20, RS16 0/20; P(>=2)=0.246, P(>=3)=0.067) — the intermediate nulls LEAN anti-conservative but the kill of RS1 rests on fidelity, not on this. **Rule 8 (12 cells = 3 panels x 2 actions x 2 rungs, tau chosen on <=2016-12-31, 2017-2026 read once): 6 of 6 clause-gated arms LOSE to doing nothing** — RS1 -0.0242 (t -1.66), RS2 -0.0291 (t -2.70), RS4 -0.0331 (t -2.16), RS16 -0.0391 (t -2.31), ROT -0.0532 (t -2.48), RS8 -0.0748 (t -2.43), S1 IS-argmax -0.0589 (t -1.87) against S0 do-nothing 10.22%/0.7766/-23.53% and SPY OOS 15.45%/0.8820/-33.72%. The hypothesis predicted a reliably NEGATIVE coefficient; every version came back positive and insignificant, and the single |t|>2 variant (excl. the 4-arm CADENCE family, +4.9023, t +2.100) is positive too. **The reason is identification, and it is arithmetic: slope = rho x sd(OOS lift) / sd(IS lift), while dispersion IS sd(IS lift)** (the decomposition closes at 1.776e-15 over 63 cells) — the queue proposed to regress a ratio on its own denominator. **In the scale-free form the queue's mechanism is confirmed decisively**: ARM rho ~ disp_sd gives b +5.5815, t +4.518, R2 0.2507 (CORE +12.0574, t +4.490, R2 0.3722), i.e. 6.6x the t and 33x the R2 of the asked form, and it is monotone in terciles of pool dispersion — mean within-cell rho **-0.1245 -> +0.2227 -> +0.6336** (t -0.70 / +1.71 / **+8.11**; cells with rho>0 9/21, 14/21, 20/21). **Dispersion governs HOW MUCH IS lift ranks out of sample; it does not govern WHICH SIGN.** The obvious alternative — that a near-zero denominator makes the low-dispersion slope a wild number — is also killed (P2 REJECTED: |slope| ~ 1/disp t +0.976, and se(slope) ~ 1/disp t **-1.585**, the se FALLS as dispersion shrinks). GROSS is neither noise nor artefact: its mean within-cell rho is **-0.9586 with 0 of 9 cells positive** (sign p 0.0039), so on a Sharpe-invariant dial the IS-best arm is *reliably* the OOS-worst. **What actually ends the question is SCALE (idea 408's rule, applied to a slope instead of a margin): GROSS's sd(OOS lift) is 0.0011 of Sharpe against VOLCAP's 0.2143 — 193.3x — and deleting GROSS's 72 rows outright moves the pooled 504-row 'record' slope from +0.5053 to +0.5147, a change of +0.0093**, because OLS weights by x-variance and GROSS's is ~0. The -0.580 is loud and weightless. Idea 311's premise is verified at its quoted level rather than cited: GROSS IS-Sharpe span 0.0009..0.0049 (mean 0.0032), **<= 0.006 in 9 of 9 cells**, rank 1 of 7 families, 39x narrower than the next (CADENCE 0.1241). **Rule 8**: the instrument the answer implies — R(tau, stat), take the K_Sharpe pick only in pools whose IS dispersion exceeds tau, else abstain to the pool's own control — was pre-registered and walked forward with tau chosen on an INNER IS split (fit <=2013-12-31, evaluated 2014-2016) and 2017-2026 read ONCE. The best of all 22 reported grid points reaches +0.0084 at t +0.90 (14/25, sign p 0.690) — inside noise, and not the point its own in-sample evidence chose. Books TOP5/10/20/40 + EWALL (idea 129's Pareto-best defensive construction); overlays CTRL / G200 (cash while lagged panel breadth < 0.50) / VT10 (vol target 0.10) / DD10 (half gross below -10% drawdown), book-level, idea 41's convention verbatim; gross 0.53 (idea 129's published defensive mean) / 0.75 / 1.00; costs 10 and 25 bps plus a **0-bps DIAGNOSTIC rung** (never a KEEP rung) so 'the panel has no defensive books' can be separated from 'costs ate them'. Gates, all **0.000e+00**: fast_bt vs engine.backtest on returns AND turnover at 0 and 25 bps; overlay at OFF (m==1) == parent on r/turnover/gross; the 44 dropped tickers absent and exactly 439 traded; zero weight on benchmark columns (SPY and IWM on the small panel, IWM everywhere); bar arithmetic == engine.metrics on RULES v2. TWO CONTROLS the queue does not ask for. (1) WINDOW: the small panel opens 2010-01-04 (eval 2011-01-13) while idea 133 read u56/broad from 2009, so every panel is re-read on the COMMON window — U56 gives **38/180** defensive members there and B136 **24/180**, SMALL439 **0/180**, so the window explains nothing. (2) BARS: re-scored against **IWM** (investable, not survivorship-screened; common-window CAGR 10.21% / Sharpe 0.552 (H1 0.620 / H2 0.511 / OOS 0.520) / MaxDD -41.13%, against SPY's 14.13% / 0.862 (0.891/0.858/0.882) / -33.72%) the small panel STILL fails H1 on **171/180** and H2 on **168/180**, with **0** defensive members. THE DECOMPOSITION (common window, SPY): SMALL439 fails H1 180/180, H2 180/180, OOS 180/180 and **the DD cap 155/180**, against U56 68/27/32/37 and B136 57/108/98/61. Only two failing-bar signatures exist on the small panel — H1,H2,OOS,DD (155 arms) and H1,H2,OOS (25) — so the queue's 'if it is always H1/H2/OOS rather than the DD cap' is **FALSE**: the cap binds on 86% of arms too, and the correct statement is that the small panel clears NOTHING. The margins are not near misses: H1 median **-0.515** Sharpe (worst -1.023, closest -0.165), H2 -0.705, OOS -0.603, DD **-13.4pp** of drawdown. Median small-panel arm @10 bps 2.8% / 0.305 / -30.6% vs U56 10.4% / 1.012 / -15.5% and B136 10.1% / 0.906 / -16.9% on the identical window. NOT COSTS EITHER: at 0 bps the best arm anywhere on the panel is TOP10 g=1.00 CTRL at 13.2% / **0.602** / **-39.9%** — short of SPY on every half and 19.7pp outside the -20.23% cap; small-panel turnover runs 13.7/yr (EWALL) to 24.6/yr (TOP5), so 10 bps costs 1.4-2.5pp of CAGR a year and removing all of it makes not one arm defensive. RULE 8 ((n,g) chosen on 2011-2016, 2017-2026 read once, four selectors fixed in advance, PROTOCOL rungs only): on SMALL439 **S1, S2 and S3 are empty in 8 of 8 cells each (24/24)** — idea 133's '6 of 18 empty cells' reproduced and generalised — and S0, the only selector that can pick there, delivers OOS **0.7% / 0.070 / -39.2%** against SPY's OOS 15.45% / 0.882 / -33.72%; for contrast U56's class-aimed S3 gives OOS 10.5% / **1.125** / -13.2% and B136's 8.1% / 0.719 / -14.2%. Across the 42 non-empty picks: 17/42 beat SPY's OOS Sharpe, 1/42 clears 4b, 0/42 clears 4a. CAVEATS: SURVIVORSHIP runs the CONSERVATIVE way here — the small panel screens on names sub-$2B TODAY that have priced continuously since 2010, so delistings are absent and its CAGR, drawdowns and halves Sharpes are all flattered; a 'no defensive books' finding on it is therefore understated, while a 'the bars are mis-calibrated' finding would not have been. Its window (2011-2026) contains no 2008-09 bear market (idea 128); MaxDD is one number off one path; IWM is a diagnostic reference only, SPY remains the PROTOCOL bar. PROTOCOL needs no small-cap recalibration on this evidence; what it should carry is the caveat that the small panel is not a source of 4b candidates at all. - 2026-09-07 (cloud, idea 394 is-c-star-widening-a-RISK-TIMING-property-record-wide) — **KILL of the proposed partition: 'widens c*' is NOT a property of what the overlay is timed on, and it is not stable across windows. Rules unchanged; no new KEEP (4a 0/126 at 0, 10 AND 25 bps; 4b 38/126 @0, 18/126 @10, 0/126 @25, and none of the 18 has a c* above the standing parent's own 22.60 bps).** Design: 126 cells = 7 BOOK-LEVEL overlay families x 3 dials x 3 gross rungs {0.50,0.75,1.00} x 2 panels (U56, B136), parent fixed at idea 40/41's book (top k=min(20,E_t) eligible, equal weight, no vol scaler, weekly, t+1); exactly two tuned params (rung, dial), every other axis a census. Every family uses idea 41's book-level convention verbatim so the ONLY thing that varies between arms is the timing variable; idea 335's two per-name families are excluded by design. Classes: R = own realised risk (VOLCAP, DDCTL); P = panel state (BREADTH, NAMEFLOOR); X = NEITHER (CALCAD May-Oct calendar, TURNBUD trailing-63d turnover vs its own expanding quantile, RANDOM fixed-seed weekly Bernoulli). PRE-REGISTERED RECLASSIFICATION: QUEUE.md files a name-count floor under X, but gate G10 measures corr(E_t, panel breadth) = **+0.993 pearson / +0.978 spearman**, so NAMEFLOOR is a panel-state instrument and is filed under P — the partition test is reported BOTH ways. Gates before any new number: fast_bt vs engine.backtest on returns AND turnover at 0 and 25 bps **0.000e+00**; overlay OFF (m==1) == parent on r/turnover/gross **0.000e+00**; matched control at a=1 == parent **0.000e+00**; Sharpe invariance of the gross dial **2.220e-16**; c* bisection determinism **0.000e+00**; matched-gross solve **0.000e+00**; RANDOM schedule reproducible and panel-independent on all 4699 shared days (0 disagreements); and **G11 — idea 335's 54 overlapping cells reproduce its committed .grid.csv to 3.553e-15** on c*(overlay), c*(control) and mean gross, so this run is a strict superset of 335's book-level arms. RESULT. 4b/full, informative cells only (idea 393's fix): R 7/19 widen, P 4/13, X 2/21; one-sided Fisher p = **0.0448** as filed and **0.2036** under the queue's classification — a conclusion that flips on where one family is filed is not a partition. The window then kills it outright: IN-SAMPLE the ordering inverts (R 3/8, P 2/6, **X 4/14**) and the single largest widening anywhere, **+22.75 bps**, is a CALENDAR overlay timed on the date and nothing else; OUT-OF-SAMPLE it inverts again (R 7/19, **P 10/13**, X 1/21) with **BREADTH widening 6/6** — the family idea 335 published as '0/6, a panel-state gate never widens'. So idea 335's family split is a full-sample artefact and 'this overlay pays for its own turnover' cannot be screened by timing class, or stated at all without naming the window. ONE REGULARITY SURVIVES: the fixed-seed RANDOM negative control widens **0 of 17** informative cells in every window and carries the most negative mean dSharpe of any family (-0.1174 at 10 bps) — an overlay carrying no information never buys cost budget. That is a floor, not a partition. MECHANISM: spearman(dSharpe@10, c* gap) = **+0.623** over 53 informative cells (idea 335 got +0.336 over 39), within-class +0.442 R / +0.448 X / -0.033 P — the association is with the overlay's Sharpe lift, which a calendar overlay can supply as readily as a vol cap. RULE 8: dial chosen on 2008-2016 by IS c*_4b AND by IS Sharpe@10, 2017-2026 read once, 84 arms. Best OOS Sharpe U56 g0=1.00 BREADTH depth=0.75 -> OOS 19.27% / 1.171 / -23.00% vs its parent 19.37% / 1.137 / -23.98%, RULES v2 9.53% / 1.285, SPY 15.45% / 0.882 / -33.72% — it FAILS 4b on the -20.23% drawdown cap. Class means OOS @10 bps: P 13.2%/1.019/-18.1%, R 13.3%/1.014/-18.2%, X 10.4%/0.883/-19.2%, i.e. the exogenous class is the WORST of the three on every OOS statistic. 52/84 IS-chosen arms beat SPY's OOS Sharpe, **0/84 beat RULES v2**, 22/84 beat their own parent, 12/84 clear 4b @10 bps, 0/84 clear 4a. CAVEATS: U56 and B136 are current-constituent lists (SURVIVORSHIP, CAGRs optimistic) and B136 CONTAINS U56, so two panels is not two independent samples; gross capped at 1.00; class sizes are unequal (R 2 families, P 2, X 3) and informative-cell counts small, so the Fisher p is an exact count statistic, not an asymptotic claim; 4 of 126 cells are vacuous (DDCTL T=0.20 never fires at g0=0.50) and flagged. - 2026-09-07 (lane C, idea 335 does-the-c-star-EQUALITY-at-20-bps-generalise) — **KILL of the proposed identity. `c*(book + de-grossing overlay) <= c*(book at matched mean gross)` is NOT an identity, and the anchor it was generalised from does not reproduce. Rules unchanged; no new KEEP (4a 0/90 at 0, 10 AND 25 bps; 4b 34/90 @0, 16/90 @10, 0/90 @25).** Design: parent = idea 40/41's book (eligible above 200d MA and vol20 < 0.60, ranked on the v1 composite WITHOUT the /sqrt(vol20) term, top k = min(20, E_t) equal-weight, weekly, t+1) on U56 and B136; 5 overlay families x 3 dial values x 3 gross rungs {0.50, 0.75, 1.00} x 2 panels = **90 cells, all committed to .grid.csv**. Exactly two tuned parameters (the parent's gross rung, the overlay's dial); panel, family and cost rung are census axes. Each overlay is paired with its **matched-gross control** — the same parent scaled by the closed-form constant a = mean gross(overlay)/mean gross(parent), i.e. the plain gross dial held at the overlay's own realised mean exposure (match error **0.000e+00** on all 90 cells). **Gates, all exact:** `fast_bt` == `engine.backtest` on returns AND turnover at 0 and 25 bps **0.000e+00**; every per-name overlay at OFF == parent **0.000e+00**; every book-level overlay at m == 1 == parent **0.000e+00**; the control at a = 1 == parent **0.000e+00**; the c* bisection reproduces **0.000e+00**; and G7, the record's standing 2026-09-04 KEEP-4b row (`46 N n=20`, published 12.7% / 1.09 / -18.3%, halves 1.09/1.10) rebuilt at fixed n=20 returns **12.66% / 1.092 / -18.31% (1.09/1.10) — EXACT**. **(1) THE INEQUALITY FAILS.** A cell is INFORMATIVE only when at least one side has a non-zero c*; 51 of the 90 are 0 <= 0 and carry nothing, so the honest denominator is 39, not 90. On those 39 the identity holds **29/39 full-sample and 22/39 out of sample** (raw 80/90 and 73/90), with the overlay widening c* by up to **+17.67 bps full and +26.30 bps OOS**. Two violations are decisive rather than marginal: **U56 g0=1.00 VOLCAP target=0.15 (c* 17.67 vs a matched-gross control of 0.00) and DDCTL T=0.10 (11.67 vs 0.00) both CLEAR 4b at 10 bps where the control fails at ZERO cost.** So c* cannot be read off a book's mean exposure and an overlay's c* must be measured. **(2) THE MECHANISM IS SHARPE RE-TIMING, AND IT EXPLAINS IDEA 42.** Gate G5 measures the gross dial's Sharpe invariance at **2.220e-16** across a in {0.25..1.00} x c in {0, 10, 25}, so the control's c* can move ONLY through CAGR and MaxDD while the overlay's also moves through Sharpe; spearman(dSharpe@10bps, c* gap) over the 39 informative cells is **+0.336**. Violations order by family exactly as that predicts: **VOLCAP 5/11, DDCTL 2/8, STOP 2/8, MABAND 1/6, BREADTH 0/6.** **BREADTH — idea 42's own family — is the ONE family that never widens c*** (mean dSharpe +0.0015): a slow panel-state gate behaves as a pure exposure dial, while overlays timed on the book's OWN realised risk cut before drawdowns and move a Sharpe path the control cannot. The proposition was generalised from the single family where it is true. **(3) THE ANCHOR DOES NOT REPRODUCE.** Idea 42's arm rebuilt on its own width (U56, n=3, g=1.00, B=0.40, depth 0.50) and its g=0.85 comparand both measure **c* = 0.00** — a DEGENERATE tie, not a 20-bps one: at g=1.00 the n=3 book draws down **-33.11% ungated / -27.04% gated** against a 4b cap of 20.23%, so neither arm has a 4b cost budget at all. This is an independent rebuild (this run's eligibility, breadth series, panel and estimator), so it is NOT evidence that idea 42 erred — but the 20-bps equality cannot carry a general law. **(4) KEEP AND RULE 8.** 12 of the 16 cells clearing 4b @10 bps sit on the NF20 twin of the standing 2026-09-04 4b row, whose own c* is **22.60 bps**, and **no overlay on it has a higher c*** (range 12.15-22.60, the best two only tie) — on the one book here that already clears 4b, every de-grossing overlay SPENDS cost budget. Rule 8 (dial chosen on 2008-2016 by IS c*_4b AND separately by IS Sharpe@10, 2017-2026 read once, 60 arms): **13/60 clear 4b @10 bps, 40/60 beat SPY's OOS Sharpe 0.882, 0/60 beat BOTH SPY and RULES v2** (OOS 1.285 U56 / 1.119 B136), identity holds OOS in 51/60. Best IS-chosen 4b-clearing arm is U56 g0=0.75 MABAND b=0.00 at OOS 14.5% / 1.181 / -15.8% against the parent's 14.5% / 1.137 / -18.3% — inside the standing family, not an improvement on it. **The 4a column is silent on this corpus: no arm beats RULES v2 at zero cost on either panel, so all 90 4a comparisons are 0 <= 0 and none is counted as support.** SURVIVORSHIP: both panels are current-constituent lists and B136 CONTAINS U56, so two panels is not two independent samples and absolute CAGRs are optimistic; gross is capped at 1.00 per PROTOCOL rule 2. Follow-ups 392, 393, 394. Script `research/backtests/2026-09-07_does-the-c-star-EQUALITY-at-20-bps-generalise_C.py`, memo `..._C.result.md`.
- 2026-09-07 (lane C, idea 334 is-the-CAGR-floor-only-ever-closable-by-the-GROSS-dial) — **KILL of the premise as written, KEEP of its consequence. The 4b CAGR floor is NOT closable by the gross dial alone: CONCENTRATION closes it more often. Rules unchanged; no new KEEP (4a 0/297 @10 and @25 bps; 4b 13/297 @10, best cell a re-measurement of idea 189's filed U56 monthly row).** Gates: `fast_backtest` vs `engine.backtest` on returns AND turnover at 0 and 25 bps **0.000e+00**; `band_state(b=0)` vs `px>ma200` **0 of 242,015**; `sel_band(m=0)` vs `sel_hard(n)` **0 disagreements on every rebalance day**; breadth overlay at depth=0 vs its parent **|dw| 0.000e+00**; the archive scan byte-identical on a re-read. **(1) THE CLASS IS BIGGER THAN THE PASSES.** Run on committed NUMBERS, not prose (ideas 387/391): 219 machine-written fail-bar columns in 182 CSVs, 172,144 rows; **26,951 (15.66%) are CAGR-only near-misses** against 21,205 outright 4b passes (12.32%). **(2) THE ANSWER IS TWO DIALS, NOT ONE, AND BOTH ARE EXPOSURE.** On 8 CAGR-only parents (3 panels x 2 book-forms x gross {0.35,0.50,0.75}), one dial at a time, 122 instrument points per cost rung: **CONC closes 5 of 8 parents @10 bps, GROSS 2 of 8, and CADENCE / MABAND / NTBAND / VOLCAP / VOLSCALE / BREADTH close 0 of 8 at 0, 10 AND 25 bps.** The mechanism is authority, not luck: max dCAGR @10 bps is **GROSS +11.39 pp and CONC +9.47 pp against a construction ceiling of +0.99 pp (cadence)**, while the population's SMALLEST gap is 1.94 pp — every construction instrument's ceiling sits below every gap. Idea 42's breadth result reproduces exactly (BREADTH is the only family whose best point is negative at every rung). **(3) CLOSING THE BAR IS NOT PASSING 4b.** Converts collapse 5+3 @0 bps -> **1+0 @10** -> 0+0 @25; GROSS closures move the failing bar CAGR -> DD (median dMaxDD -7.37 pp), CONC closures break the Sharpe bars (median dSharpe -0.162). Gross capped at 1.00 (no leverage, rule 2) closes only 2 of 8, so the floor is not simply a leverage statement either. **(4) RULE 8 KEEPS THE ORDERING.** Dial chosen on <=2016, 2017-2026 read once: OOS floor closed by GROSS 5/8, CONC 3/8 (IS-Sharpe) or 5/8 (IS-CAGR), CADENCE 1/8 (by 0.53 pp), everything else 0/8; chooser beats own parent anchor 54-60/135, SPY 81/135, **RULES v2 3/135**, mean regret +0.0216/+0.0157. CONC is the best closer and the worst OOS Sharpe (0.80-0.84) with the largest regret. **(5) BY-PRODUCT — A THIRD OVERLOADED COLUMN NAME.** The archive sibling test says CADENCE closed the floor **540 times at median +4.26 pp** until attribution is gated on the column's VALUE SET: **535 of those come from a column named `f` in 6 files holding {0.5, 0.2, 0.1} — a fraction, not a frequency**; `depth` (12 files, 88 closures) and `n` (7 files) are rejected the same way, leaving 2 genuine cadence closures. Same defect as idea 359's `band` lexicon and idea 384's `m`. **PROPOSED (Sunday review, reading aid only, no rules change): the leaderboard's `closable-by` column with values {GROSS, CONC, none}, and a PROTOCOL note that a CAGR-only 4b failure is a statement about EXPOSURE, not construction — plus a requirement that any dial census gate attribution on values, not column names.** Caveats: current-constituent panels (survivorship, SMALL439's floor tested in the book's favour), U56 subset of B136 and 36/56 ETFs, the GROSS arms are absolute so 16 points are 2 books x 8 parents, and L2 can only speak about dials the record actually swept. Script `research/backtests/2026-09-07_is-the-CAGR-floor-only-ever-closable-by-the-GROSS-dial_C.py`.
- 2026-09-07 (lane B, idea 384 price-the-no-trade-BAND's-DRAWDOWN-TAX-across-the-record) — **KILL: the premise is falsified and both of the queue's candidate shapes are wrong. There is no drawdown tax, and the band is a signed COST instrument with an UNSIGNED drawdown effect. Rules unchanged; no new KEEP (4a 0/45 at every rung; 4b 17/45 @10 bps, all re-measurements of filed objects).** Gates before any new number: `fast_backtest` vs `engine.backtest` (returns AND turnover) at 0 and 25 bps **0.000e+00**; `sel_band(m=0)` vs `sel_hard(n)` **0 disagreements on every rebalance day**; and the (B136, n=20, g=0.75, m=0, W) cell reproduces idea 333's committed grid row on six statistics at **0.000e+00**. **(1) THE ARCHIVE SAYS THE BAND HELPS DRAWDOWN.** 1,340 committed CSVs; 68 carry a column named exactly `m` beside a MaxDD column but only 15 write it integrally — **the record overloads `m`**, 53 files using it for idea 103's fractional share dial, the same lexical defect idea 359 found in the band vocabulary now visible in a column name. On the 3,360 recoverable observations (370 ladders, 10 scripts) the no-trade band **improves** MaxDD 57.7% of the time, worsens it 32.4%, exact zero 9.9%, median **+15.0 bp**; one vote per ladder at its largest m (n=1,089) gives 64.0% / 29.9%, median **+66.6 bp**; per-script medians run +87.9 to -20.9 bp with **8 of 11 positive**, so no single file drives the sign. **(2) NEITHER CONSTANT NOR SCALING — THE QUESTION HAS NO ANSWER IN ITS OWN TERMS.** Pooled MAE **H_const 0.07973 vs H_scale 0.07958**, i.e. H_scale 'wins' by **0.2%**, a tie; the scale coefficient is the tighter of the two at only **2 of 7** m-levels; and the decisive statistic is that the residual is **0.49x to 97x the fitted coefficient itself** (median ~1.5x) under either model. `corr(dMaxDD, DD0) = +0.008` pooled (-0.125 on the fresh grid) — H_scale's entire content, that a deeper book pays a deeper tax, measures as zero. dMaxDD(m) is noise with a small positive mean. **(3) IDEA 333'S CELL IS A ONE-CELL DRAW.** Its -37.8 bp is reproduced exactly, but the 4b DD-cap margin along m on its own book (B136, n=20, @10 bps) is **non-monotone**: m=0 **+0.0018**, m=5 +0.0015, **m=10 +0.0028**, m=20 **-0.0020**, m=40 -0.0083, against turnover 14.31 / 9.52 / 7.61 / 6.20 / 5.09x per year. At m=10 the band clears the cap by MORE than the m=0 anchor while removing 6.7x/yr of turnover; had idea 329 pre-registered m=10, the same family would have read 'the band buys turnover for free'. **(4) WHAT THE INSTRUMENT ACTUALLY IS.** Fresh 45-cell grid (3 panels x n{10,20,40} x m{0,5,10,20,40}, gross 0.75, weekly, t+1, three cost rungs; holdings invariant in m to the last decimal — U56 n=20 mean names **19.1075** at all five m, reproducing idea 359 by a different method). Over the 36 band cells **dSharpe > 0 at 36/36** (median +0.0474, min +0.0009) and dCAGR > 0 at 32/36, but **dMaxDD > 0 at only 19/36** (16/33 after excluding the three cells whose n+m passes their panel's eligible-name ceiling — 55 on U56, 128 on B136, 280 on SMALL439 — and which are therefore the hold-until-ineligible limit, not a band). Median turnover removed **6.66x/yr**; the implied exchange rate is **+2.13 bp of MaxDD per 1.0x/yr removed, IQR [-7.40, +8.84]**, straddling zero, so there is no rate to price. **(5) THE TWO 'BANDS' HAVE OPPOSITE SIGNATURES.** The 200d MA band WIDTH (column `band`, fractional, 4,792 observations, never pooled with `m` here) behaves as the queue expected the no-trade band to: **55.5% worsen** DD, median -5.0 bp, ladder-level **64.7% worsen at -73.5 bp**, `corr(dMaxDD, DD0) = -0.258`, `a(m)` monotone in width (+0.0001 at 0.02 -> -0.0076 at 0.12 -> **-0.0282 at 0.30**), and H_const beating H_scale by 17.5%. Idea 359 called the shared lexicon a naming defect; this measures it as a substantive one. **(6) RULE 8 AND THE KEEP PATHS.** 4a **0/45** at 0, 10 and 25 bps. 4b 22/45 @0, **17/45 @10**, 5/45 @25. The IS chooser (2008-2016 Sharpe @10 bps) picks U56 n=20 m=40 -> OOS Sharpe **1.1892**, 4b PASS, regret +0.008 — but that cell is degenerate on a 56-name panel and is idea 280's already-KILLED m=999 arm; restricted to genuine bands the pick moves to n=20 m=20 -> OOS **1.1867**, 4b PASS, at a cost of 0.0025, so the finding does not rest on the degenerate cell. B136 picks n=10 m=20 -> OOS 0.9217 (fails H2 and DD); SMALL439 picks n=10 m=40 -> OOS 0.4797 (fails all five). **All three lose to live RULES v2 out of sample** (1.285 U56 / 1.119 B136 / 0.568 SMALL439). **(7) BY-PRODUCT, PARKED.** (U56, n=20, g=0.75, **m=20**, weekly) beats idea 333's filed 4b anchor on every axis at identical holdings — Sharpe 1.064 -> **1.112**, MaxDD -18.31% -> **-17.22%**, OOS Sharpe 1.131 -> **1.187**, turnover **11.0 -> 5.26x/yr** — and closes the weakness that anchor's memo named: the anchor **fails 4b at 25 bps on H1** while every m >= 5 at this n passes 4b at 0, 10 **and** 25 bps. It is the same family, it is 4a 0/45, it loses to RULES v2 OOS, and idea 280's matched-turnover cadence test is untouched (cadence was not a dial here), so it is PARKED with that one owed test, not proposed: memo `2026-09-07_u56-top20-band-m20_4b_B_MEMO.md`, queued as idea 386. **Proposed consequences (no rules change):** retire 'the band buys turnover with drawdown' from the working vocabulary; never let `m` and `band` share a leaderboard column or a claim (idea 387); and stop writing the no-trade band as `m`, since 53 of 68 files already use that name for a share dial. Survivorship caveat unchanged: all three panels are current-constituent lists, so the CAGR floor is tested in the book's favour. Script `research/backtests/2026-09-07_price-the-no-trade-BANDs-DRAWDOWN-TAX-across-the-record_B.py`.

The ENTRY buffer barely touches turnover (11.00 -> 7.68x/yr, spearman **-0.298**) and instead **collapses the book from 19.1 names to 7.6** (spearman(e, names) **-0.988**). Marginal dSharpe vs the (0,0) hard cut at 10 bps: EXIT **+0.0577 positive 15/15**, ENTRY +0.0320 positive 15/18 — but the ENTRY mean is **+0.0005 on U56**, i.e. nothing, and its whole lift sits on B136 (+0.035) and SMALL439 (+0.060), the two panels where a top-20 book is diluted. **(2) THE DECISIVE READING, turnover-matched:** each buffered cell against the nearest-annual-turnover cell of the OTHER side. **ENTRY beats its matched EXIT twin in 8 of 18** (median **-0.0142**, mean -0.0017, OOS **5/18**); **EXIT beats its matched ENTRY twin in 9 of 15** (median **+0.0318**, mean +0.0244, OOS **10/15**). Both directions agree and out of sample they agree harder. **(3) The sides are SUBSTITUTES, not complements:** interaction dS(e,x) - dS(e,0) - dS(0,x) has mean **-0.0312**, is **negative in 79 of 90** cells and is 0.332x the mean absolute marginal; the additive model explains **R2 0.618**. Binding 4b bars @10 bps: H2 83, DD 80, OOS 56, H1 42, CAGR 41. **The record's weekly breakeven moves 47 -> 60 bps** (U56 e=16 x=40, first failing bar DD); the four highest-c* cells all carry e >= 8, so the entry buffer buys cost tolerance while buying no admission. Saturation stated: on U56 (37.5 eligible names/day) x=40 and x=80 are the **identical book** — once n+x exceeds the eligible count the exit buffer stops biting. **(6) KEEP-candidate (4b), PARK-recommended (memo written):** `U56, n=20, enter at rank <= 4, exit at rank > 60, NORM g/k_t at 0.75, WEEKLY` — 16.52% / **1.164** / -19.02%, H1/H2 **1.245/1.096**, **4b PASS at 0, 10 AND 25 bps** (margins @10: H1 +0.289, H2 +0.262, OOS +0.286, DD +0.012, CAGR +0.059), OOS **1.168** (17.18%, -19.02%), turnover 5.45x/yr, **c\* = 60 bps**, and it is the FULL menu's own rule-8 pick so its OOS number carries no hindsight. 4a FAIL (H2 -0.095, DD -0.070). **PARKed on three grounds:** the identical construction fails 4b on B136 and SMALL439 at every rung; it holds **~11.1 names, not 20**, so it is a concentration bet the band framing hides; and this run's own rule 8 says the chooser is better off with the dial that produced it removed — adopting it would mean writing into RULES the one instrument whose presence on the menu costs OOS Sharpe on 2 of 3 panels. **SURVIVORSHIP:** all three panels are current-constituent lists, so every CAGR LEVEL is optimistic and an 11-name momentum book is the most flattered object this record trades; the e- and x-DIFFERENCES are far less exposed. SMALL439 drops the 44 tickers with max_1d_move >= 1.0 and starts 2010-01-04, so its halves are not the same calendar halves as U56/B136 and rule 8's IS window is effectively 2010-2016 there (idea 111's sample-start caveat). 3 follow-ups queued (357 whether the entry buffer is just a smaller n, 358 whether the exit buffer's name-count neutrality survives a flat cap, 359 a census of how many committed band rows are concentration changes). Each constant is read off the cell, never fitted; both replays are traded at the cell's cadence and charged the same 10 bps. Corpus: 3 panels (SMALL439 / U56 / B136) x 3 families (MA, MAVOL, and the ranked TOP20 channel whose fixed gross/n weight de-grosses without saying so) x 3 cadences x 6 bands = 162 cells x 4 books, plus 9 controls and the live book. The small positive dSharpe cells all sit at c_bar <= 0.38, where the DEGROSS book is a 1.4-3.8% CAGR mostly-cash book; from c_bar 0.5 up, dSharpe is -0.012..-0.047 and OOS -0.053..-0.076 at **every** rung. **(2) The MA threshold's edge is real but lives at constant gross.** Exact attribution of the 0-bps DEGROSS CAGR difference (identity, closes to 1.78e-15 pp): **-0.2917 = +1.2436 SELECTION -1.1660 LEVEL -0.3693 TIMING** pp/yr. idea 52's published DEGROSS gate-cost range reproduced to the decimal at **4.78-8.33 pp**; and the band dial removes **75.4%** of the RESPREAD/MA/W cost against idea 52's ~76%. **P1, the construction claim, HOLDS at 2.082e-17:** the two arms share one gate mask and differ only in the denominator (RESPREAD g/k_t, DEGROSS g/n_t), so w_dg = (k_t/n_t)·w_rs at every rebalance and the engine's drift preserves proportionality — therefore r_dg,t = c_t·r_rs,t EXACTLY, with c_t the realised-gross ratio (0.419-0.525 here). **There is no separate de-gross strategy on this panel: it is the respread book delevered.** **P2, the QUEUE's own regression, FAILS its pre-registered bar and the failure is specification, not physics:** gap on mean realised gross gives **R2 0.573 @10bps / 0.621 @0bps, resid sd 0.698 pp, max|resid| 1.704 pp** against bars R2>=0.95 and sd<=0.25 pp — because cash drag is a PRODUCT (1-c̄)·mu and across these 36 cells mean gross moves only **0.314 -> 0.394** while the respread book's own CAGR moves **5.0% -> 10.7%**; regressing on the respread CAGR alone gives **R2 0.880**, on both **0.916**, and the zero-parameter constant-leverage replay **0.664**. **P3, the structural decomposition, FAILS the absolute bar and passes the relative one, and its SIGN is the real finding:** replaying r_A,t = c̄·r_rs,t per cell puts the **exposure share at mean 0.914 (0.798-1.000)** — mean |gap| 4.346 pp, mean |residual| **0.4005 pp = 9.22%** — but the residual is **negative in 35 of 36 cells** (max +0.001, min -1.238), **widens with band width** (-0.322 at b=0.00 -> -0.574 at b=0.12) and **with slower cadence** (Q -0.745 vs W -0.273, M -0.184), and is larger on the trend-only gate (MA -0.519 vs MAVOL -0.282). That is not noise: **de-grossing does not merely hold less, it holds less at the wrong times, and the penalty grows on exactly the dial idea 52 showed removes 75% of the respread cost.** **Rule 8** (band and cadence on 2010-2016, 2017-2026 read once, 4 arms): picks b=0.12/M, b=0.12/M, b=0.05/M, b=0.05/M post OOS **10.73%/0.7163/-37.6%, 6.54%/0.5084/-38.4%, 4.69%/0.6543/-16.7%, 2.05%/0.4104/-14.7%** against **SPY 15.45%/0.8820/-33.7%**, the no-filter control **10.10%/0.6372/-36.2%** and the **LIVE RULES v2 book 9.53%/1.2851/-12.1%** — **0/4 beat SPY, 2/4 beat do-nothing, 0/4 beat the live book**; regret 0.000/-0.072/0.000/-0.053. **Both KEEP paths: 4a 0/72, 4b 0/72**, binding bars H1 72 / H2 72 / OOS 72 / CAGR 67 / DD 46 — consistent with ideas 49/52/60/121, nothing on SMALL439 clears SPY in any half under either construction. **What the record should carry:** a DEGROSS-vs-RESPREAD contrast is ~91% a re-pricing of EXPOSURE, so quoting one as evidence about a GATE overstates the gate by roughly 10x on this panel; the share must be estimated per cell by the zero-parameter constant-leverage replay, NOT by the gap-on-mean-gross regression (R2 0.57-0.62); and the 9% residual is a signed, dial-dependent cost of de-grossing's exposure TIMING that deserves its own column. SURVIVORSHIP: `data/prices_small.csv.gz` is a screen of CURRENT sub-$2B constituents with no delistings, but P1/P2/P3 are all arm-minus-arm contrasts on identical names and days (the two constructions share one gate mask), so the bias very largely cancels out of the headline; it does not cancel out of the 4a/4b level columns, reported only to record that both are 0. - 2026-09-06 (lane B, idea 70 what-actually-moves-H2) — **INDEPENDENT SECOND RUN. A cloud lane answered idea 70 concurrently (commit 0a9fdf6) from a different construction and reached the SAME verdict on both queued mechanisms (0 of 128 whole-sample name bans clear SPY; a PIT top-10 mega-cap cap moves H2 monotonically the WRONG way at 0 of 5 levels; it is a regime). This run agrees and adds two things the cloud run does not have: the exact vol-matched Sharpe identity, and the localisation of the whole residual to 21 days. ANSWERED / KILL of both candidate explanations. The broad ranked book's H2 shortfall is neither a handful of names nor a sector hole: it is a turnover BILL and a single 21-day EPISODE. No KEEP-candidate, no memo, no RULES change; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Idea 66 left `top20-200d` on universe_broad.json (g 0.75, weekly, 10 bps) failing 4b on one number, H2 Sharpe 0.814 vs SPY 0.837, after showing gross moves it by 0.001 and idea 63's SPY core by +0.047 at t<1. **Reproduction 6/6 EXACT before any new number was read** (13.11%/0.9581/-20.05%, halves 1.1246/0.8135, SPY H2 0.8366, prices truncated at the parent's last eval day 2026-09-03). Because the failing bar is scale-free, the decomposition is of the VOL-MATCHED active return `a_t = k*r_book - r_spy`, k = sigma_SPY/sigma_book = 1.2888, for which `S_book - S_SPY = 252*mean(a)/sigma_SPY` is an identity; per name `sum_i A_i + COST + BENCH = dS` **verified to 1.1e-16**. Regrouped: **selection +0.1145, turnover bill -0.0979 (14.37x annual turnover in H2 at the 10 bps rung), vol-matched underinvestment -0.0395, = -0.0231**. So the stock picking beats SPY by +0.114 and the bill takes 85% of it back; idea 63's cash drag is worth only -0.040 once vol is matched — the exact corollary of idea 66's flat-Sharpe finding, now measured. **The sector hypothesis is dead**: over a fixed 15-class taxonomy written before any result was read, only 3 classes have a negative contribution and they total -0.017, less than a fifth of the cost term, while InfoTech alone is +0.487 of +0.911. **The mega-cap hypothesis is dead in the opposite direction**: MEGA10 (a deliberately HINDSIGHT 2026 top-10, which makes the hypothesis easier to confirm) supplies +0.2242 of the book's +0.9115 Sharpe from 13.5% of its weight; regressing a_t on MEGA10 weight gives R^2 0.0012 / t +1.66 same-day and R^2 0.0020 / t +2.10 lagged with a POSITIVE sign both ways; and banning all ten in a real re-run costs -0.084 H2 Sharpe (0.730 vs 0.814). **The names hypothesis is dead**: 136 full re-runs, each removing one name from the eligible panel so the rank is recomputed, give only **3 of 136** removals that clear SPY's 0.8366 (best WFC 0.8436), a spread of 0.7804-0.8436 with sd 0.0105, and the hindsight drop-k ladder chosen ON H2 reaches only 0.9201 at k=10 — sitting at the 99.4th-100th percentile of 2000 random k-subsets at every k, which is what a maximum over 136 candidates does by construction. **What is actually left is one month.** The worst 21-day window of a_t, **2020-03-24 -> 2020-04-22**, is worth 617% of the whole gap; deleting it moves dSharpe from -0.023 to **+0.120**, and only 1.0% of 200 permutations of the same daily returns produce a window that bad. It is the COVID *rebound*, not the crash: the 200d gate had de-risked the book and it re-entered too slowly — ideas 52/57's whipsaw, showing up as the entirety of the 4b failure. The L=126 percentile of 31.5% says episode, not multi-year regime. **Rule 8** (exclusion fitted on 2009-2016 only, 2017-2026 untouched; note H2 begins 2017-11-03 so H2 IS the OOS window, 100% overlap, and anything fitted on H2 is hindsight by construction): 12 grid points over k in {0,1,2,3,5,10} x granularity in {name, sector}; **4a 0/12 against the LIVE book and 4b 0/12** (the live book became RULES v2 at the same day's Sunday review while this run was executing; the run was re-executed against it — v2 is 8.04%/1.107/-12.24% with halves 1.229/0.988 and OOS 1.122, a real bar. Against the retired v1, 4a was 9/12, which was never informative at an OOS Sharpe of 0.581). The IS-fitted name ladder moves OOS Sharpe only 0.887-0.912 around the parent's 0.894 (SPY OOS 0.884), and the **persistence test is the direct KILL: Spearman(IS per-name contribution, OOS per-name contribution) +0.285, with the IS-worst-10 and OOS-worst-10 name sets overlapping 0 of 10** and the worst-3 sectors 1 of 3. The single grid point beating SPY OOS on Sharpe (sector k=10, 1.005) bans 10 of 15 classes, keeps only InfoTech/CommSvcs/ConsDisc/HealthCare/Industrials, fails 4b on drawdown (-22.16% against the 20.23% bar) and is a non-monotone outlier on its own ladder (0.894/0.880/0.880/0.883/0.862/1.005) — reported because the protocol requires every grid point, flagged because that is the shape of noise. Survivorship: universe_broad.json is current constituents, so absolute levels are optimistic; every comparison here is between arms on the same panel and the same days. Queued next: **273 turnover-budget-the-broad-ranked-book** (the bill is the lever) and **274 price-the-post-crash-re-entry-lag** (the episode is the residual). `2026-09-06_what-actually-moves-H2_B.py`

No KEEP-candidate, no memo, no RULES change; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Idea 259 asked whether reversal share is a monotone function of the concentration ratio `r = n / n_elig`, which would make a reversal predictable from a number every grid already carries. As a BOOK rule it is a decision that buys nothing: RSEL picks a different n on 5 of 5 panels and lands at pooled OOS **9.6% / 0.897 / -21.4%** against FWD20 11.1%/0.903/-21.4%, S_SHARPE 12.4%/0.889, S_CAGR 14.0%/0.797, EWALL (do nothing) 8.6%/0.857, RULES v1 6.4%/0.691 and SPY 15.5%/0.882 — a further instance for idea 229's selection-loses pool, and idea 259's S_CAGR-vs-S_SHARPE exchange rate (+6.0 pp/yr of OOS CAGR for -0.091 of Sharpe) reproduces on a fifth panel. **KEEP paths, all 70 points reported: 10 bps 4a 6/40, 4b 8/40; 0 bps 4a 3/40, 4b 12/40** — every 4b passer is a known point on idea 259's own two ladders (U56/FWD14,20,31 and B136/EWall,FWD35,50,74,99), and SMALL439 + ETF36 are **0 of 16** at both rungs, reproducing idea 136. No new KEEP, no memo, no RULES change; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** 3636 grid points — 3 panels x 202 books x 6 cost rungs {0,1,2,5,10,25} — **every one printed**; exactly two tuned dimensions (panel, n), with arm, seed and rung reported at every value. The caveat is stated rather than buried: DD's reachability is partly mechanical, its modal ladder argmax being **g=0.20** (the ladder's floor) against CAGR's **g=1.00** — the two gross-sensitive bars are reachable at OPPOSITE ends, which is precisely why idea 184 found 4b admission to be a contiguous interval, and why the ladder's only real job is locating the overlap. **(3) Idea 66/173/176's flat-Sharpe result, re-derived from the exclusion side:** median slack RANGE over the 6.75x gross span is H1 0.0071 / H2 0.0040 / OOS 0.0042 against DD 1.0153 / CAGR 1.0524 — **150-250x** — and an unreachable Sharpe bar needs a median **0.13-0.15** of relaxation to close, so the 177 hopeless books are not near-misses.
