A dial where coin-flipping wins is a dial whose grid slopes, not a dial where fitting has skill. **CADENCE is the only survivor**: paired +0.0642 OOS Sharpe (t +4.54, 40 win / 11 loss, sign p 0.0001), capture **67.1%** of the oracle against RANDOM's **-33.0%**, oracle at an INTERIOR point in 96.2% of books, selector agreeing with it 75.5% (picks M in 44/53, oracle M in 48/53) — an interior optimum driven by a mechanism (turnover cost) that transfers. **GROSS reproduces idea 166 on a fresh corpus exactly as pre-registered (P2 HIT):** mean OOS Sharpe is flat to 0.001 across the entire 0.20-1.00 ladder — gross is a near-pure SCALE lever, so its Sharpe argmax is noise — the selector consequently picks g=1.00 in 50/53 books and LOSES (mean d -0.0006, sign p 0.0008), while the 4b-margin ladder is NOT flat and peaks at g=0.80 (-0.158) with 0.75 at -0.161 and 0.70 at -0.179, i.e. idea 166's 0.70-0.80 plateau, reproduced. N loses (capture -23.9% of a +0.0900 oracle gain); BAND is not significant on a ladder whose whole mean spread is 0.018 Sharpe. **The mechanism behind the Sharpe-vs-4b sign flip:** every arm that raises mean OOS Sharpe lowers the OOS 4b pass count, because Sharpe is bought by surrendering CAGR (SLEEVE: mean OOS CAGR 9.96% -> 8.82%, Sharpe 0.964 -> 1.144, MaxDD -17.2% -> -12.6%), and the CAGR floor is 4b's most-violated bar (**1223 of 1908 rows**, vs H2 689, DD 447, OOS 405, H1 312). - 2026-09-05 (lane B, idea 159 the-share-at-which-ranking-stops-paying) — **ANSWERED, and it is a KILL of the question rather than an answer to it: there is no book share at which ranking stops paying, because the VALUE of a cross-sectional tilt and the COST of running it are the same function of share. No RULES change, no new book, no KEEP-candidate.** The reproduction gate passed **8 of 8** before any new number was read — ideas 81/153's INV-vs-NONE name overlap at n=20 (u56 69.4%, broad 42.5%), idea 153's matched-share dCAGR(POS-NONE) at m=0.20 (u56 +2.83%/yr, broad +2.75%/yr), its mean weekly eligible counts (37.5 / 91.5 / 141.2), and the cost-derivation identity `r_c = r_0 - turnover*c/1e4` against a fresh 10 bps engine run at **0.00e+00**, which is what makes the gross and net legs of every comparison below the *same book* rather than two runs. **180 books** (3 panels x 10 book shares x 3 tilts x 2 weighting constructions), each run once at 0 bps with the 10 and 25 bps rungs derived exactly, weekly, t+1, no shorting, no leverage; two tuned parameters (the share m and the tilt), every grid point reported. The idea asked for the share m* at which the tilt's realised magnitude g(m) = |dCAGR at 0 bps| falls below the 10 bps cost c(m) of running it, with a bootstrap interval. Three cost bars were pre-registered and all three reported: the exact incremental cost of holding the tilted book over its own no-tilt control (primary), the cost of *expressing* the tilt (10 bps x annualised sum |w_tilt - w_NONE| over rebalances, an upper bound), and a flat 0.10 pp/yr floor. **Only 10 of 36 (panel, construction, tilt, bar) cells produce a finite empirical m* at all, and 6 of those 10 sit at the grid's lower endpoint m = 0.05** — 'already noise at the smallest share tested', not a threshold. The fitted (log-linear) estimator returns -16.72, +15.82 and +86.90, which is the numerical signature of two near-parallel lines rather than a crossing. The bootstrap (circular block, block 21 d, 2000 replicates, seed 159, tilt and control resampled on the *same* block index) censors **27.5% to 83.2%** of replicates on the large-cap panels, and every interval that is not censored spans essentially the whole share axis (u56 INV [0.050, 0.934] at 83.2% censored; broad POS [0.050, 0.977] at 56.0%). Prediction P4 — that the interval would be at least 0.25 wide — held for the wrong reason: the interval is wide because the parameter does not exist, not because it is imprecisely estimated. **The diagnosis, added post-hoc after P3 failed and labelled as such throughout:** a crossing exists only if g decays in share *faster* than c does, i.e. only if d = slope(log g) - slope(log c) < 0. Bootstrapped on the same scheme, **d straddles zero in 6 of 6 (panel, tilt) cells** — u56 INV **+0.032** [-1.186, +1.097] with P(d<0) = 47.4%, broad INV +0.173 [-0.781, +1.274] at 38.5%, broad POS -0.590 [-2.116, +0.688] at 80.0%. The mechanism is arithmetic and follows directly from idea 153: both the value and the cost of a tilt are proportional to how many names it moves, and how many names it moves is exactly what book share governs, so share scales numerator and denominator alike. The ratio is flat — **g/c = 1.95 / 1.83 / 2.20 at m = 0.05 / 0.53 / 1.00 on u56** (Spearman(m, ratio) -0.224) and 1.50 / 1.47 / 1.58 on broad (+0.358). **On the honest cost bar the tilt is never expensive at all**: g/c runs **16 to 4254 on u56 and 9 to 193 on broad, at every share including the endpoints.** At the incumbent's own share (u56, m = 0.53, n = 20) the live INV tilt has **2.68 pp/yr** of gross magnitude available against **0.083 pp/yr** of true incremental cost and 1.46 pp/yr on the upper-bound bar — affordable by a factor of 32 — and it spends that magnitude as **-2.68 pp/yr**. INV's signed dCAGR is **negative at all 10 shares on u56 (-13.49 to -0.61 pp/yr) and all 10 on broad (-9.57 to -0.36)**, while POS is positive at 19 of those 20 points. **So the live vol scaler is not too expensive to run; it is wrong-signed everywhere.** That is the fifth independent delete-the-scaler finding (after ideas 72, 82, 141, 160 and 162) and the first that separates the two candidate reasons — cost and direction — and finds the cost reason absent. It also sharpens idea 82: ranking does not subtract value by costing too much, it subtracts value by pointing the wrong way; and it removes this axis as a source for idea 124's book-size floor, which must now come from a different argument. **Rule 8 (12 panel x construction x cost cells, m* re-estimated on 2009-2016 only, picks read once on 2017->):** the m*-gated selector returns mean OOS Sharpe **0.7212** against **0.8044** for doing nothing (NONE at m = 0.53), winning **1 of 12**; it beats the plain IS-Sharpe chooser by only +0.021 (4 of 12), and RULES v1 returns 0.4514. **All four selectors lose to SPY's 0.882.** The IS gate is itself unstable — 1.01 (gate nothing) in every 10 bps cell and 0.05 (gate everything) in every 25 bps cell — which is the non-existence of m* reappearing inside the selector. **Both KEEP paths, all 180 books:** 4a 22/90 literal and 22/90 gross-normalised; 4b **17/90 literal and 24/90 gross-normalised at 10 bps** and **0/90 at 25 bps under both constructions** (idea 137's wall, confirmed again). No new book: the passes are idea 153's already-published set re-measured on a finer share grid (u56 and broad, m in [0.30, 1.00], tilt NONE or POS; the incumbent u56 m=0.53/NONE/n=20 at 12.66%/1.092/-18.31%, halves 1.088/1.102, OOS 1.168), with 19 cross-universe arms all inside idea 153's interval. **INV — the live tilt — passes 4b 2 of 60 times**, both at m >= 0.85 where all three tilts hold nearly the same names. Nothing is proposed to the Sunday review. **3 of 6 predictions held.** P1 (reproduction) and P5 held; P2 failed (g is monotone in share for INV, Spearman -0.988 on u56 and -1.000 on broad, but not for POS at -0.515, nor on the small panel); **P3 is the informative failure** (no crossing strictly inside [0.15, 0.85] on either large-cap panel); P4 held for the wrong reason; P6 half-failed (the gate loses to doing nothing as predicted but edges plain IS-Sharpe by +0.021). One PROTOCOL rule-9 *reporting* clause is offered in the memo and nothing else: a claim that an instrument stops paying above some level must report the ratio of its realised magnitude to its cost across that level rather than the two curves separately, and a ratio whose log-slope difference straddles zero has no threshold and none may be quoted from it. Caveats carried: survivorship on all three current-constituent panels (idea 54); the eligibility gate is inverted on the small panel (ideas 39/49) so its numbers describe a gate that does not work there; ideas 38 and 126 carry over; idea 128 (the IS window's SPY drawdown is shallower than the OOS window's); the m -> 1.00 endpoint forces all three tilts onto the same eligible set so g -> 0 mechanically, which is why the fitted estimator is also reported on m <= 0.70 and a crossing at 1.00 is treated as no crossing; a block bootstrap on one realised path measures sampling error around that path, not uncertainty across worlds; m is a sample-average share and idea 157 (open) tests the time-varying n_t. - 2026-09-05 (cloud, idea 156 the-CAGR-floor-is-what-kills-small-pools) — **ANSWERED, KILL of the artefact hypothesis as posed: 4b's CAGR floor IS gross-sensitive, but it is NOT separable from the drawdown cap, and removing it by re-grossing simply relocates every failure onto the cap. No RULES change, no new book, no KEEP-candidate.** Idea 78's 300 sub-panel books (B136, k in {20,40,80} x 50 seeded draws x n in {5,20}) were re-run from the same `default_rng(78_500 + k)` stream and reproduce its committed `gridB.csv` **EXACTLY** (max abs diff 2.2e-16 on every metric; failing-bar string identical in 100.0% of 300 books; k=20/n=20 fails on CAGR in 50 of 50, k=80/n=20 passes 46.0%). Scaling each book to SPY's 17.72% realised vol lands within **0.14%** of target and leaves mean Sharpe unchanged to four decimals (0.8996 -> 0.9000 -> 0.8994 across a 0.75 -> 1.13 mean-gross move), so the test is clean. **The mechanical half of the premise is confirmed: uncapped vol matching removes 106 of the 119 CAGR-bar failures.** The conclusion does not follow: **DD-bar failures rise 146 -> 297 of 300 and corpus 4b passes fall 42 -> 2**, with **0** of the 38 books whose ONLY failure was the CAGR floor becoming a pass and **37 of 38 becoming DD-only failures**. The reason is structural and belongs to 4b rather than to these books: 4b demands 100% of SPY's Sharpe in both halves and out of sample but only **60%** of its drawdown, so a book run at SPY's volatility cannot clear the cap. **Idea 148's no-leverage ceiling is confirmed and strengthened**: 55.0% of the 300 books need g > 1.00 to reach SPY's vol, the driver is the book's cash weight rather than the pool size (k=20/n=20 runs 6.94% vol and needs a median **1.82x**, 100% of its draws levered; k=80/n=5 needs 0.77x), and `g = min(g_req, 1.00)` is the ONLY setting under which the small-pool cell passes 4b at all (0.00 -> 0.12 -> 0.00 as the ceiling is applied then lifted). Rule 8 makes it concrete: idea 78's own k=20 pick, which failed 4b on the CAGR floor, **passes** re-grossed to the ceiling (OOS 11.16%/1.103/-13.93% vs SPY OOS 15.45%/0.882/-33.72% and RULES v1 B136 OOS 5.94%/0.576/-21.19%) and **fails again on drawdown at g = 1.66** — its 4b verdict is a statement about where g = 1.00 sits, not about the signal. Across all 1500 book-arm rows, 4b passes requiring leverage: **0**. Predictions scored 3.5 of 6, with P3 ("most CAGR-only failures flip to a pass uncapped") a clean miss recorded as one. Three clauses proposed to the Sunday review: state 4b's CAGR floor and DD cap as ONE joint risk-budget constraint; record each book's required vol-matching gross beside its 4b verdict; strengthen idea 148's ceiling clause.
- 2026-09-05 (cloud, idea 152 price-the-broad-POS-near-miss) — **ANSWERED: the near-miss is real, is priced exactly, and is NOT capital-worthy. PARK the broad-only book; KILL the cross-universe KEEP claim. No RULES change, no new live book.** Idea 81 left two books one bar short on `universe_broad.json` @10bps, n=20: `POS` (composite x sqrt(vol20)) failing 4b on the DRAWDOWN cap alone by 1.14pp, and `NONE` failing on H2 alone by 0.023. Those two failures are not the same kind of failure, and that is what this run establishes on one harness. Both premises **reproduce exactly** (POS 16.0%/1.052/-21.4%, halves 1.197/0.927, OOS 1.005, to published precision; `INV/n=5/w=0.15` equals `baseline.rules_v1_weights` to 0.000e+00 on all three panels). Ideas 39/49's "the ranking is worth nothing" was a property of the v1 composite (rank-blend plus vol20 gate plus vol scaler), not of momentum. **(3) The gate damage localises to the vol20 filter, not the 200d MA.** Holding the ranking and n=40 fixed: none 14.6%/0.797, 200d only 11.4%/0.693, **vol20 only 7.4%/0.524**, both 5.6%/0.441 — the vol20<0.60 gate alone costs 0.27 of Sharpe against the 200d gate's 0.10, and they compound. Ideas 39/49 only ever measured the two together. **(4) The 200d gate's sign is not stable**: +0.053 Sharpe at n=10, +0.015 at n=20, -0.105 at n=40, -0.117 at n=60 — it helps a concentrated book and hurts a broad one, so neither idea 39's "inverted" nor RULES v1's "the gate is the edge" generalises here. **(5) The decisive counter-evidence against trading any of it, stated against our own finding (2):** compounded EW decile portfolios by 12-1 momentum (daily, 0 bps) are U-shaped, not monotone — D1 21.5%/0.865, D2-D9 flat in an 8.0-12.4% band, and **D10 (worst momentum) 29.2%/0.937, higher CAGR and Sharpe than D1**; the arithmetic D1-D10 spread is -8.11%/yr, t -1.15. D10 is precisely the beaten-down cohort the survivorship bias flatters most, so it is not tradeable — but with both tails beating the middle and only one of them survivorship-clean, finding (2) cannot be read as a demonstrated cross-sectional premium. **(6) Cost-fragile.** At 0 bps the best point reads 15.9%/0.856 — it merely ties SPY frictionless; 10 bps 0.797, 25 bps 0.709, 50 bps 0.561. An 11.5x-turnover sub-$2B book would realistically pay more than 10 bps. **(7) Rule-8 walk-forward** (IS 2011-01-13..2017-01-03, two selection rules fixed in advance): plain-Sharpe picks `no-gate/n=40`, OOS 16.3%/0.818/-33.9% vs SPY 15.5%/0.884/-33.7% and RULES v1 live 7.8%/0.751/-13.8% — beats SPY on CAGR, loses on Sharpe, beats the live book on both at 2.5x its drawdown; the OOS Sharpe *exceeded* the IS Sharpe (0.818 vs 0.785), so this is not an overfitting signature, the book is simply not better than SPY risk-adjusted. The **4b-aware rule picks NOTHING** — no in-sample point met the -11.2% in-sample drawdown cap (shallowest -20.1%) — the same structural outcome as ideas 39, 46 and 49. Survivorship (current constituents of a sub-$2B screen as of 2026-09-03) is one-directional and strengthens the KILL; benchmark caveat stated not adjusted (no IWM in the cache). **For the Sunday review:** nothing to adopt, and one live-book item — the `vol20 < 0.60` gate is the larger of RULES v1's two eligibility filters by damage here and has never been tested in isolation on universe.json, where it is assumed to be part of the edge. Queued as idea 56. Result memo: `research/backtests/2026-09-04_small-cap-momentum-clean_cloud.result.md`.
- 2026-09-04 (cloud, idea 55 trend-gate-lookback-primary) — **KILL for the 200d trend gate as a source of edge on the universe it was fitted to, plus a 4b KEEP-candidate that strictly dominates idea 2's.** The 200d-MA gate is the load-bearing assumption of RULES v1 and of the project's first KEEP-candidate; ideas 39 and 27 measured it at -1.7pp CAGR on small caps and -6.4pp on QQQ, but nobody had varied the LOOKBACK on `universe.json`, where it is supposed to be the edge. Idea 2's construction held fixed (top-n by the v1 composite without `/sqrt(vol20)`, EW at 0.75/n, 75% gross, weekly, t+1, 10 bps, cash when E_t<n), two tuned parameters — K in {200d,100d,50d,none} x n in {5,10,20,30} — all 16 points reported, `vol20<0.60` held at v1's value throughout. Harness check: **K=200d n=20 reproduces idea 2's KEEP row to the decimal** (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103). **(1) K=none beats K=200d at every n on universe.json**, on CAGR and Sharpe both: n=20 reads 13.7%/1.123/-18.5% (halves 1.154/1.101) against the incumbent's 12.7%/1.093/-18.3% at the same 9.5x/yr turnover, and n=5/10/30 all show the same sign. 6 of 16 points pass 4b, 1 passes 4a. **(2) The gate's own contribution is statistically indistinguishable from zero.** Paired daily t-tests on the same names and days: dropping 200d is worth +0.35 to +1.47%/yr on universe.json (**t +1.42 to +1.76** — positive at every n, significant at none) and -0.22 to +0.19%/yr on universe_broad.json (t -0.50 to +0.68). So "the gate is the edge" is not supported on the primary universe; equally, "the gate destroys value here" is NOT established — the honest statement is that it does nothing measurable, and its sign is unstable between two heavily-overlapping large-cap lists, which is itself evidence it is noise rather than structure. **(3) Faster IS decisively worse, and that is the only significant effect in the lookback dimension.** The 50d gate costs 3.0-5.5%/yr on BOTH universes at every n (t +2.59 to +3.85), monotone in K. Whipsaw is real; it has simply stopped mattering by 200d. If a gate is kept at all, keep a 200d-class lookback. **(4) The cleanest number, consistent in sign on both universes: for the un-ranked book (equal-weight every eligible name, no ranking) the 200d gate costs ~1.8-2.2pp of CAGR and ~0.09 of Sharpe (t +1.47 primary, t +2.13 broad) and adds 6.4x/yr of turnover, to buy 2.5-3.1pp of drawdown.** That is drawdown insurance, not alpha, and the Sunday review should describe it that way in RULES. Pricing that trade properly is queued as idea 57. Calendar-year check at n=20 agrees: the gate helped only in 2020 (+1.6pp) and was a dead heat in 2022 (-9.0% vs -8.9% with SPY -18.2%). **(5) Rule-8 walk-forward: on universe.json BOTH pre-registered selection rules pick K=none n=20** (IS Sharpe 1.071, IS MaxDD -11.9%), OOS **14.9%/1.164/-18.5%** vs SPY 15.5%/0.884/-33.7% and RULES v1 7.8%/0.751/-13.8%, clearing every OOS 4b bar; OOS Sharpe exceeds IS Sharpe, so this is not an overfitting signature. The two universes pick opposite arms — the candidate inherits idea 2's universe fragility exactly and must not be promoted as a general rule. **(6) One diagnostic worth recording and not trading:** the K=none un-ranked control passes 4b outright on universe.json (12.2%/1.127/-18.4%, halves 1.141/1.116, OOS 1.183) at **1.9x/yr turnover** and misses on the broad list by 0.6pp of drawdown alone. - 2026-09-04 (lane B, idea 66 gross-exposure-is-the-error) — **KILL for "raise gross" as the fix for the standing 4b failure, and a correction to idea 63's diagnosis.** Idea 63 attributed the books' second-half shortfall to 75%-gross cash drag and repaired it with a 25% passive core; the queue asked whether simply being fully invested does the same thing, in which case the sleeve is a detour. 36 arms (3 pre-chosen books x gross in {0.75,0.80,0.85,0.90,0.95,1.00} x core fraction in {0,0.25}) x 6 cost levels x 2 universes, weekly, t+1, long-only, no leverage; two tuned parameters (gross, core fraction), all points reported; analytic cost identity asserted against a real `cost_bps=10` engine run. **(1) Gross is an exact lever, now verified rather than assumed:** against the same book at g=1.00 every arm shows **corr 1.0000, beta = g to three decimals, and dSharpe = 0.000**; the Sharpe slope d(Sharpe)/d(gross) is -0.001 to +0.008 across all three books and both lists. CAGR, MaxDD and turnover all scale linearly (universe.json `ew-band3`: 11.3%/-15.1%/4.9x at g=0.75 -> 15.1%/-19.9%/6.4x at g=1.00, Sharpe 1.136 at every point). **(2) Therefore gross cannot fix an H2 Sharpe bar, and the cash-drag story does not explain the failure it was invoked for.** The bar idea 63 targeted is the broad ranked book's H2 of 0.814 against SPY's 0.837; across the whole gross sweep it reads 0.814/0.814/0.814/0.815/0.815/0.815 while MaxDD deepens 6.1pp. Cash drag is a real CAGR cost and undoing it does raise CAGR — but at exactly the drawdown you would predict, so no risk-adjusted bar moves. **(3) The sleeve is NOT a detour — it is the only one of the two that touches a Sharpe bar,** because it changes the composition of the return stream rather than its scale: the same broad arm with the 25% SPY core reads H2 0.861-0.862 at *every* gross (+0.047). But the effect is not significant (paired daily t < 1 in every book) and it still fails 4b on drawdown there; and at matched total investment (g=1.00) the core is strictly **worse** on universe.json — 1.106/-21.7% against all-active's 1.136/-19.9%, paired +0.23%/yr t +0.44. **(4) Rule-8 walk-forward: all four picks FAIL out-of-sample on drawdown,** by 0.4-1.9pp (universe.json R1 `g=1.00 b=0.25` OOS 16.7%/1.174/-21.7%, R2 `g=0.95 b=0.25` OOS 15.8%/1.174/-20.6%; broad R1 `g=1.00 b=0` OOS 14.9%/1.073/-22.1%, R2 `g=0.95 b=0` OOS 14.2%/1.073/-21.1%; OOS cap -20.2%). The mechanism is worth carrying forward: **gross is not a selectable parameter.** No Sharpe-based rule can choose it (Sharpe is flat, so R1's pick is decided in the 4th decimal), and the drawdown-aware rule still overshoots because 2009-2016 contains no 2020 or 2022, making its -13.2% in-sample cap loose against the -20.2% the OOS period enforces. Gross is a risk-budget decision, and in-sample drawdown is not a safe way to set it. **(5) One PARK:** `ew-band3, g=0.90, core=0` clears all five 4b tests on **both** universes at **5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 bps** and clears the OOS 4b bars on both (13.5%/1.136/-18.0%, halves 1.113/1.160, OOS 1.234, 5.8x; broad 13.4%/1.064/-20.0%, halves 1.164/0.971, OOS 1.073, 6.2x) — a wider cost survival than idea 63's QQQ-core arm with one fewer moving part. PARK not KEEP: rule 8 does not and cannot select it, and g=0.90 is merely the largest gross whose linearly-scaled drawdown still fits under the broad list's cap, not evidence of an edge — its Sharpe is identical to g=0.75's. **For the Sunday review:** (a) stop treating gross as something a backtest can choose — state it in RULES as a drawdown budget with the number derived from the budget; (b) idea 63's core sleeve survives this test on its own terms but its H2 repair is t < 1 and costs drawdown, so it should not be adopted on the cash-drag argument as stated. Rules unchanged. Ideas 69-70 queued. Result memo: `research/backtests/2026-09-04_gross-exposure-is-the-error_B.result.md`.
- 2026-09-04 (lane C, idea 10 sector-only-universe) — **KILL for the ETF-only book, and the complement control is the finding.** 30 points (6 panels x [RULES v1 + EW-all-eligible + top-n EQW n in {5,10,20}]), all reported; harness reproduces idea 2's published KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103) and the live v1 row to the decimal. **(1) 0 of 10 ETF-only points pass 4a or 4b.** Best ETF arm `ETF36/CAND-n20` 6.8%/0.817/-15.2% (halves 0.754/0.878, OOS 8.1%/0.943) fails 4b on **H1 and CAGR** — the floor is 10.68% and it earns 6.8%; the literal queued arm `ETF24` (broad + sector ETFs, no bonds/commodities) 6.7%/0.779/-15.2% fails H1, H2 and CAGR. **(2) Half the hypothesis is right and it does not help.** Matched construction, same days, same gross, vs the full-list control: ETF36 has **lower vol in 10 of 10 pairs** and ETF24 in 6 of 10 — the idiosyncratic-risk claim is real on volatility — but MaxDD is shallower in only 4/10 and 2/10, and **Sharpe is worse in 20 of 20**, because the return loss dwarfs the risk saved: **-6.15%/yr (t to -5.31)** for ETF36 and **-5.02%/yr (t to -4.11)** for ETF24. Risk came down; return came down more. **(3) The complement carries the entire edge.** The same 56-name list stripped to its 20 mega-cap single stocks gives the run's only 4a pass — `STK20/CAND-n20` **12.1%/1.338/-12.1%, halves 1.341/1.344**, MaxDD shallower than v1's -13.8% — which also passes 4b; `STK20/CAND-n10` reads 19.0%/1.305/-17.3%; running v1's *own* construction on stocks only is worth **+11.6pp CAGR and +0.468 Sharpe (t +4.07)**. **Both rule-8 selections pick a STK20 arm and both clear every OOS 4b bar** (S1 -> n=10, OOS 21.2%/1.366/-17.3%; S2 4b-aware -> n=20, OOS 14.0%/1.449/-12.1%), with **Spearman(IS, OOS Sharpe) = +0.608** over the 18 ranked points — the project's best IS/OOS rank agreement (idea 8 measured +0.000 on this list). **(4) It is a PARK, not a KEEP, and the run's own control is why.** universe.json's megacap group is 20 tickers selected as 2026 constituents (NVDA, AVGO, PLTR, META, TSLA...) — the most survivorship-exposed panel in the repo. The stock-leg advantage is +5.19%/yr (t to +4.45) on those 20 names but only **+0.92%/yr (t max +2.04)** on universe_broad.json's 100 single stocks, which **fail 4b on drawdown at every n**. Memo written recommending **rejection**, with the exact RULES wording it would require so the Sunday review rejects a written rule rather than a vibe; note that at n=20 on a 20-name panel the ranking is inert (mean 13.2 eligible, 49% gross) so the rule is EW-all-eligible with a gate. **(5) Universe invariance is not a substitute for return.** The 36 ETFs are bit-identical in universe.json and universe_broad.json (symmetric difference `[]`), so an ETF-only book passes idea 53's cross-universe composition test **by construction** — and still fails 4b outright. **(6) Two side results for the Sunday comparison:** `B136/EWall` — equal-weight every eligible name in the broad list, no ranking, no vol scaler, 8.3x turnover — **passes 4b** at 10.7%/1.027/-17.7% (halves 1.146/0.917, OOS 1.021), the simplest 4b-passing book the project has; and ranking helps *more* on the low-dispersion ETF panel (+0.186 Sharpe over EWall) than on the full list (+0.043), which does not rescue it. - 2026-09-04 (lane B, idea 73 asset-class-dispersion) — **KILL for cross-sectional dispersion as a universe clause, and idea 10's ETF KILL is re-explained.** 35 points (7 panels x {EWall, RULES v1, CAND-5/10/20}) on a common 2011-01-13→2026-09-03 window so every panel is judged on identical days, 10 bps, weekly, t+1, 75% gross; two tuned parameters (panel, n), all points reported; the harness reproduces idea 2's KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103) and the live v1 row (6.5%/0.666/-13.8%) to the decimal before any new number is read. **(1) The premise is true as a fact about the panels.** Mean cross-sectional sd of 12-1 momentum over the eligible set orders exactly as idea 10 assumed: ETF24 0.129 < ETF36 0.145 < B136 0.257 < BSTK100 0.278 < U56 0.281 < STK20 0.378 < SMALL484 0.682, stable across halves — the ETF panels really do have 2.6x less to sort than the mega-cap stock panel and 4.7x less than small caps. **(2) The inference drawn from it is false.** The net ranking premium (CAND-n Sharpe minus the SAME panel's equal-weight-all-eligible book, same days, same gate, same gross) has Spearman **-0.107 / -0.071 / -0.071** with dispersion at n=5/10/20. The largest premium in the entire run is **ETF36/CAND20 at +0.228 Sharpe (t +2.41)** — on the second-*lowest*-dispersion panel — while the widest panel, SMALL484, has the worst net Sharpe of all 21 CAND points (0.493). Ranking works best where there is least to sort. **(3) What the cross-panel pattern is actually made of.** The gross selection spread (forward 1-week return of the top-n eligible minus the equal-weighted eligible set, no costs) does rise with dispersion (Spearman +0.429/+0.679/+0.357) but rises *more* with the number of eligible candidates (**+0.571/+0.857/+0.964**), and the two are confounded across panels because the widest panel is also the largest. n=7 panels; treated as suggestive, not evidence. **(4) The test with power is flat.** Within each panel, weeks classified into dispersion terciles by an EXPANDING quantile of that panel's own history (no look-ahead): high-dispersion weeks beat low-dispersion weeks in only **2 / 2 / 3 of 7 panels**. Pooled with panel fixed effects over **4,877 panel-weeks**, corr(dispersion percentile, weekly selection spread) = **-0.006 / -0.015 / +0.001 (|t| ≤ 1.01)**. Holding the panel, its names and its survivorship exposure fixed, dispersion predicts nothing. **(5) Rule 8 rejects it outright.** The pre-registered dispersion rule S3 (highest 2009-16 mean dispersion at n=20) picks **SMALL484 → OOS 7.6%/0.506/-26.3%, failing every OOS 4b bar** and finishing last of the seven panels; S1 (highest IS Sharpe) picks STK20/CAND10 → **21.2%/1.366/-17.3% PASS** and S2 (4b-aware) picks STK20/CAND20 → **14.0%/1.449/-12.1% PASS**. Spearman(IS dispersion, OOS Sharpe) = **+0.134** over the 21 points (+0.143 over the 7 panels at n=20) against Spearman(IS Sharpe, OOS Sharpe) = **+0.710**. The panel choice *is* selectable out of sample; dispersion is simply not what selects it — and used as a rule it picks the worst panel available. **(6) Idea 10's ETF KILL survives with a different mechanism.** The ETF book fails on the LEVEL of return, not on the ranking: ETF36/CAND20 earns 6.6% CAGR against this window's 9.91% 4b floor while carrying the best ranking premium in the run. 'Too few things to sort' is not why ETFs failed; 'not enough expected return in the panel' is. **(7) Nothing is upgraded.** The only 4b passes are already-known books — U56/EWall, U56/CAND10, U56/CAND20 (idea 2's candidate) and all four STK20 books (idea 10's PARK, which idea 71 attributes to selection). No new KEEP-candidate. **Survivorship** is one-directional on all three lists and falls hardest on STK20/BSTK100/SMALL484, the high-dispersion panels, so the run is biased *toward* the hypothesis it rejects. **For the Sunday review: recommended RULES wording is none** — do not add a dispersion clause. If a universe clause is wanted, the supported form is about return level and candidate count, not spread: *'The ranked book may be run on any panel of at least 20 eligible names; a panel is disqualified by its own realised CAGR against the 4b floor, not by its cross-sectional dispersion.'* Rules unchanged. Ideas 77-78 queued. Memo: `research/backtests/2026-09-04_asset-class-dispersion_B.result.md`.

- 2026-09-04 (cloud, lane C) — **Idea 13 `52w-high-proximity`: KILL.** 28 points (2 universes × [live-v1 + EW-all-eligible control + 3 signals × n∈{5,10,20,30}]), all reported; harness reproduces idea 2's KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103) and idea 10's `B136/EWall` (10.7%/1.027/-17.7%) to the decimal. **(1) The literal idea loses everywhere.** Replacing RULES v1's return composite with George & Hwang's nearness-to-52-week-high `P_t / max(P_{t-251..t})`, holding names/days/gate/gross fixed, is worse in **8 of 8 matched-n pairs**: dSharpe **-0.045..-0.754**, paired daily **t -3.07..-4.16**, every sign negative, mean **-7.2%/yr** on universe.json and **-9.9%/yr** on broad; the pre-registered 50/50 BLEND arm loses in 7 of 8. **0 of 16 PROX/BLEND points pass 4b anywhere; 0 of 28 points pass 4b on both lists.** **(2) The signal is negatively informative inside the eligibility gate.** Weekly rank IC vs the following week's return over 905/914 weeks: PROX **-0.0208 (t -2.13)** on universe.json and **-0.0252 (t -3.34)** on broad, negative in BOTH halves of BOTH lists, against the incumbent composite's +0.0427 (t +4.16) and +0.0242 (t +3.22). The mechanism is that the 200d gate has already spent the signal — mean PROX of *eligible* names is 0.953 vs 0.902 across all names — so what is left is a level statistic only +0.192/+0.324 Spearman-correlated with the composite, and the part that differs is the part that loses. It is **de-risking, not signal**: vol falls in 8/8 pairs and MaxDD is shallower in 6/8 while CAGR falls further every time — idea 10's ETF shape exactly (risk fell, return fell more). **(3) It loses to no ranking at all**: against EW-all-eligible, dSharpe -0.900..+0.004 with t -4.10..-1.98 at every n on both lists, while the incumbent composite beats that same control on return in 8/8. **(4) The project's own whipsaw prior pointed at this idea and the measurement points the other way — the run's most transferable finding.** A *level* key bounded near 1.0 is FASTER, not slower: at matched n on universe.json turnover is 40.2/31.1/14.8/7.8×/yr for PROX vs **17.6/13.9/9.6/7.0×** for the composite, and flips per ticker per year 4.8/7.4/7.0/5.4 vs 2.1/3.2/4.4/4.7, because eligible names cluster within a few percent of their highs and tiny moves reshuffle the top of the book. "Slower signal" is a property to be measured, not inferred from the signal's form. **(5) Rule 8 rejects it unanimously and with power.** Spearman(IS Sharpe, OOS Sharpe) over the 12 CAND points is **+0.888** (universe.json) and **+0.930** (broad) — against idea 8's +0.000, this is a choice the walk-forward *can* make — and it picks the incumbent every time: S1 and S2 both select COMP-n20 (OOS 14.4%/1.170/-18.3%, clears every OOS 4b bar) and COMP-n30 (OOS 11.6%/0.904/-20.3%, misses OOS DD by 0.1pp), with the composite winning 7 of 8 within-n signal audits. **(6) Nothing is upgraded.** The run's three 4b passes are reproductions of ideas 2, 8 and 10's published rows; 0 of 14 points pass 4a on universe.json (the six 4a passes are all on broad, where RULES v1 itself draws down -21.2% and 4a is not a bar). **Survivorship** is one-directional and flatters PROX — names that spent years far below a 52-week high and then delisted are absent, which favours a signal that avoids them — and it loses anyway, so the KILL is conservative. **For the Sunday review: recommended RULES wording is none.** Rules unchanged. Ideas 79-80 queued. Memo: `research/backtests/2026-09-04_52w-high-proximity_C.result.md`.

Read in one direction: raising gross buys return ~3x more efficiently (0.68 vs ~0.22 pp/pp) and Sharpe-neutrally, so the budget is dominated on its own axis. 0 of 48 broad budget points pass 4b at 10 bps; no arm passes 4b on both universes. Rule 8: B is not selectable (Spearman IS/OOS +0.14/-0.07 on universe.json; the IS pick loses to its own control OOS in 2 of 4 cases). Two findings carried to QUEUE: (a) which 4b bar BINDS decides which lever can help — gross is strictly counterproductive on a CAGR-bound book (32/32 gross arms fail on CAGR) and the budget is the only lever that helps there, lifting `EWall`'s u56 breakeven 7.0 -> 20.0 bps (does not replicate on broad); (b) truncating a trade list is not self-financing, so the QUEUE's literal `largest-changes-first` budget is partly a disguised gross lever (realised gross 0.815 vs control 0.717), the mirror of idea 73's de-grossing artefact. Rules unchanged.

- 2026-09-04 (lane C, idea 15 crypto-sleeve) — **PARK: the largest and most consistent improvement the repo has produced, rejected by rule 8 four times out of four.** `baseline.load_universe` has excluded BTC-USD/ETH-USD from every backtest the project has run, yet both are cached and both are trend instruments of the kind the 200d gate is built for. 78 points (2 universes x 3 books [live v1 / idea 2's CAND20 / EWall] x [control + 2 funding modes x 2 gates x 3 caps]), all reported; harness reproduces idea 2's KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%) and the live v1 row to the decimal and c=0 equivalence against the crypto-free panel is 1.4e-17. Two tuned params only: cap c in {0,5,10,15}% per name and gate in {`same` = v1's own 200d AND vol20<0.60 applied to crypto, `trend` = vol cap waived}; funding (`matched` = sleeve funded by scaling the equity leg down, gross unchanged; `add` = gross rises) is a reported structural variant, gross-matched pre-registered as primary because ideas 66/73/81 showed an unmatched gross change is an exact return lever. **(1) The effect is real and one-directional: 36 of 36 sleeve arms beat their own crypto-free control on full-sample Sharpe on BOTH lists** (paired daily t +1.71..+2.81 matched, +2.70..+3.21 additive), and **5 of 39 points pass cross-universe 4b at 10 bps** — `CAND20/matched/same/c5`, `EWall/matched/same/c5`, `EWall/matched/same/c10`, `EWall/matched/trend/c5`, `EWall/add/same/c5`. Both controls fail that test (CAND20 on broad H2 0.814 vs 0.837, EWall on u56 CAGR 10.4% vs the 10.68% floor — the two near-misses ideas 28/44 have been circling) and **the sleeve repairs exactly the bar each was missing**. The literal queued arm on universe.json, `CAND20/matched/same/c10`, reads 14.3%/1.178/-19.1% (halves 1.254/1.127, OOS 1.237) against 12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, at 10.3x turnover, and its advantage WIDENS with cost (dSharpe +0.154 at 10 bps -> +0.276 at 100) because the sleeve adds return without adding turnover. **(2) Why it is a PARK: the passing arms are unreachable.** In-sample Sharpe is monotone in the cap and higher for the loose gate in nearly every cell, so both pre-registered selection rules buy c=15/`trend` in 4 of 4 walk-forwards and **every one fails the OOS drawdown bar** (rule 8's window: u56 28.4%/1.315/**-31.1%** and broad 24.3%/1.226/**-30.4%** against a -20.2% cap; a crypto-era window IS<=2021: -19.4% and -24.1% against -14.7%); within-book audits pick c=15 in **11 of 12** cells and **not one** of the 5 cross-universe passers is ever selected. Spearman(IS,OOS Sharpe) is +0.771/+0.855 on rule 8's window but **+0.362/+0.252** on the crypto era — the stable ordering is the equity book's, not the sleeve's. **This is idea 66's failure shape exactly** (`ew-band3 g=0.90` also passes cross-universe 4b and is also unselectable), and two instances make it a pattern: on this repo a 4b pass sitting at an INTERIOR parameter value has twice been unreachable by any rule maximising in-sample Sharpe. **(3) Rule 8 cannot validate this idea on the data that exists.** BTC is tradeable from 2015-07-02 and ETH from 2018-08-27, so rule 8's in-sample window holds ~1.5 yr of BTC and ZERO ETH; the crypto-era walk-forward was added for that reason and rejects it too on 3.3 yr of in-sample. **(4) The t-stat is one calendar year.** 2017 (BTC +1425%, ETH +135%) sits inside H1 — which is why sleeve H1 Sharpes look spectacular (1.088 -> 1.408) even though only 13.1% (`same`) / 24.0% (`trend`) of H1 days hold any crypto at all. Restricted to 2018-09+ the effect shrinks by a third and loses significance (t_cry +0.66..+2.06; dSharpe negative in 4 of 18 gross-matched arms on universe.json), and 2018 is the counter-year the full sample hides: BTC -74%, ETH -82%, `CAND20/matched/trend/c10` **-0.4% against the control's +5.9%**. **(5) Survivorship is worse here than anywhere in the repo:** BTC and ETH are the two survivors of the crypto field and LUNA/FTT/the 2014-18 altcoin cohort went to zero rather than to an acquirer, so every figure is an upper bound on a two-ticker sleeve chosen with ten years of hindsight. Secondary: crypto trades 24/7 but the index is equity trading days, so weekend moves land in the Monday bar and a Friday rebalance cannot react — this understates realised drawdown; and 10 bps is an equity cost assumption. **(6) Transferable finding for RULES: the vol20<0.60 cap is a drawdown instrument whose value is conditional on the instrument's own vol distribution.** BTC's median vol20 is 0.532 and ETH's 0.714, so the cap is near-binding by construction: it cuts BTC's eligible days 43.3% -> 24.9% and ETH's 24.2% -> 7.8%. `trend` earns more standalone (BTC gated-only 38.8%/0.966 vs `same`'s 21.0%/0.855) but **every 4b failure among the sleeve arms is `DD`**, and `same` vs `trend` is the only lever in the run that changes which side of the cap a book lands on (mean dMaxDD -2.9% vs -7.0%). That is the mirror image of idea 56's small-cap result, where the same cap destroys value. **Recommendation to the Sunday review: do not adopt.** The exact RULES wording that would be required is recorded in the memo and recommended against; revisit only when a delisting-aware crypto panel exists (cf. idea 54) and ETH has >=8 further years. Memo: `research/backtests/2026-09-04_crypto-sleeve_C.result.md`. Ideas 87-89 queued (margin-aware selection for interior 4b passes, the vol cap as an explicit satellite clause, and a leave-one-year-out audit of every standing candidate).

- 2026-09-04 — Research cloud (idea 14, rsi2-sleeve): **KILL**, decisively. A Connors RSI(2)<thr-in-uptrend mean-reversion sleeve on the 16 sector/industry ETFs, funded by scaling the trend book down, was tested at f in {0.25, 0.50} and thr in {5, 10, 20} against three pre-chosen cores (live v1, idea 2's top20 KEEP, ew-all) on both large-cap lists at 5/10/25/50 bps — 42 leaderboard points, every grid cell printed. **The sleeve loses in 36 of 36 (universe, core, f, thr) cells at 10 bps** (mean dSharpe -0.412, median -0.371, paired daily t between -2.5 and -9.5 vs each arm's own control), and rule 8 selects f=0 (no sleeve) in 5 of 6 walk-forwards; the single arm a selection rule does buy (broad/top20 under the IS-drawdown-capped rule) fails OOS on Sharpe and CAGR. **The mechanism is turnover, not signal.** The signal is real and correctly signed — entry-day forward returns 0.209%/0.087%/0.049% at thr=5/10/20 vs 0.063% unconditional over 1026/2088/3830 entries, gross sleeve Sharpe 0.461/0.550/0.747 — but the sleeve holds 2.2-3.6 names for a mean 2.8 days and turns over **65x/113x/165x per year**, i.e. 6.5/11.3/16.5 pp of annual cost at PROTOCOL's 10 bps, which converts every positive gross book into a negative net one (-1.6%/-4.2%/-5.3% CAGR standalone). This is idea 76's holding-period finding at its extreme: the fastest instrument the project has tested is also the only one whose entire gross edge is consumed by its own trading. Two controls rule out the obvious alternatives: adding a one-day execution lag changes the standalone Sharpe by only -0.08/+0.04/-0.05 (the h=0..4 forward-return profile is flat, so there is no one-day pop being forfeited), and buying one day EARLY loses 45-72% CAGR, confirming the signal is a genuine dip-buy rather than an artefact. The only variant that comes close to breaking even is `div4` (never more than 25% of the sleeve in one name), which halves turnover to 28x and lifts standalone Sharpe to +0.26 at thr=5 — still dSharpe -0.003 to -0.057 on the blended books, i.e. at best free. **Transferable finding for RULES: a sleeve's admissible turnover is bounded by its gross Sharpe, not by its correlation with the core.** The sleeve's correlation with the trend books is only 0.37-0.49, so the diversification premise held; it simply cannot pay for itself. No RULES change proposed. Script: research/backtests/2026-09-04_rsi2-sleeve_cloud.py.

- 2026-09-04 — Research cloud (idea 89, one-year-leverage-audit): **infrastructure delivered, and it changes how two standing candidates should be read.** A generic leave-one-year-out harness (delete a calendar year, chain-link the remainder, recompute every statistic AND every 4b bar on the retained days so the benchmark moves with the sample) was run over 13 (book, universe) cells x 18 years at 10 bps, with zero tuned parameters; it reproduces idea 2's KEEP (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%) and idea 72's `B136/EWall` (10.7%/1.027/-17.7%) to the decimal. **(1) Only 2 of the 7 published 4b passes survive deletion of every single year:** idea 2's `top20` and idea 46's `frac085`, both 18/18 on universe.json. `ew-band3` (idea 57) is 17/18 on both lists, `frac085` 17/18 on broad, and idea 72's `B136/EWall` **10/18** — the weakest standing candidate by a wide margin. **(2) The far more important finding is that 12 of the 14 verdict flips are the BAR moving, not the book weakening.** Deleting 2020 raises SPY's 60%-of-MaxDD cap by 5.53pp (the COVID crash is most of SPY's -33.7%) and deleting 2022 raises the 70%-of-CAGR floor by 1.68pp, while the candidate books barely move — so PROTOCOL 4b's two absolute bars are themselves one-year-levered, and a LOYO 'failure' on DD or CAGR is usually a statement about SPY, not about the candidate. **(3) No equity candidate is unusually year-dependent:** worst-drop Sharpe deltas are SPY -0.059, v1 -0.065, `ew-band3` -0.071, `frac085` -0.074, `top20` -0.077 on u56 (1.10-1.30x the benchmark's own; 1.22-1.56x on broad). Nothing here resembles idea 15's shape. **(4) Every candidate's single best year is 2022** (excess over SPY +7.3 to +14.0pp) except `top20`/u56 (2018, +10.5pp): the 4b edge over SPY is, in the main, one bear market avoided, and that is the exposure to price — not per-parameter fragility. **(5) Harness validation:** applied to idea 15's PARKed crypto arm as a PAIRED DIFFERENCE (`EWall+c10` minus its own control), t is +2.04 full-sample and falls below 2.0 when any of 2016, 2017, 2020 or 2024 is deleted (worst 2020, t +1.48) — the harness flags it, and finds the dependence broader than the single year idea 15 named. LOYO on the same book's own Sharpe does NOT flag it, so **the audit must be run on the statistic the idea is argued on**, which is the one methodological rule this run would add. **(6) Rule 8 says LOYO-robustness is a disqualifier, not a selector:** on the broad list max-IS-Sharpe picks `ew-band3` (OOS 11.2%/1.074/-16.8%, 4b PASS) while max-IS-worst-case-LOYO picks `top20` (OOS 12.5%/0.894/-20.1%) — robustness-aware selection did strictly worse out of sample, so it must not be used to choose books or parameters. Proposed PROTOCOL rule 10 with exact wording is in the memo, recommended as a PARK-trigger only; PROTOCOL.md not modified (Sunday review decides). Caveat carried into the memo: a spliced equity curve's MaxDD is not a realisable path, so DD-based LOYO verdicts are optimistic. Memo: research/backtests/2026-09-04_one-year-leverage-audit_cloud.result.md. Script: research/backtests/2026-09-04_one-year-leverage-audit_cloud.py.

- 2026-09-04 — Research cloud (idea 16, monthly-seasonality): **KILL**, and the reason generalises. 144 grid points (2 universes x 3 books [live v1 / idea 2's `top20` 4b KEEP / `EWall`] x 6 month-masks x f in {0.00,0.25,0.50,0.75}), all printed, plus 6 controls; 2 tuned params (mask, f); harness reproduces idea 2's KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103) and the live v1 row (6.5%/0.666/-13.8%) to the decimal. **(1) The conditioning variable is not persistent.** Spearman between each series' H1 mean-daily-return-by-month ranking and its H2 ranking is **+0.000 / -0.182 / -0.364 / -0.021** on universe.json and **+0.000 / -0.049 / -0.322 / +0.028** on broad — 6 of 8 negative, max +0.028. Corroboration: September is the worst full-sample month in all four series yet appears in **0 of 6** in-sample-fitted `worst1` masks (in-sample worst-1 is Jan or Aug everywhere) and 1 of 24 `worst-k` masks overall, i.e. it is hindsight, not signal. Month t-stats agree: SPY's Sep is t -0.22 and the only |t|>2 months are the positive ones (Jul +3.54, Nov +3.05). **(2) The literal idea loses.** Only 24 of 144 arms beat their own control on full-sample Sharpe (mean dSharpe -0.080; best anywhere +0.063 on the weakest book, +0.003 on the standing KEEP), monotone in f — the more exposure the mask removes the worse it gets — and the removed exposure is bought back more cheaply by the plain gross lever (ideas 66/83). The KEEP candidate is the book it hurts most (mean -0.113). **(3) Rule 8 is anti-predictive 6 of 6.** The IS-Sharpe selector picks `worst6` (the freest mask) in every single case and loses **-0.292 to -0.570** of OOS Sharpe against its own control. **(4) The two cross-universe 4b passes are not results:** `top20`/`sep` at f=0.00/0.25 clear 4b only by lifting broad H2 from 0.814 past SPY's 0.837 while *lowering* full-sample Sharpe, on the one mask rule 8 never selects. **Carry-forward for PROTOCOL:** report the cross-half rank correlation of the conditioning variable BEFORE building any book — it is one line, and where it is ~0 no grid can rescue the idea. Applies to every queued regime/breadth/VIX/day-of-week conditioning idea. Rules unchanged; standing candidates unaffected.

- 2026-09-04 — Research cloud (idea 87, interior-4b-passes-are-unselectable): **KILL for the proposed rule-8 amendment; the two ideas it was meant to rescue were parked correctly.** 66 grid points across six 1-parameter risk grids re-run from scratch (GROSS/top20, GROSS/EWall, BAND/ew-all, N/ranked, CRYPTO/CAND20, CRYPTO/EWall) x 2 universes, 48 selections, all printed; 2 tuned params (grid parameter, margin m); harness reproduces idea 2's KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103), idea 72's `B136/EWall` (10.7%/1.027/-17.7%) and idea 57's broad `ew-band3` (11.1%/1.064/-16.8%) to the decimal. **(1) Rm(m) = argmax IS Sharpe s.t. the IS 4b drawdown cap met with margin m does not beat rule 8 on anything that matters:** OOS Sharpe vs the default arm +0.027/+0.029/+0.033 at m=0/1/2pp against R0's +0.031, it reaches the grid's OOS-best in 0 of 10 / 0 of 9 / 0 of 4 cells against R0's 2 of 12, and **13 of 48 selections are infeasible** (8 of 12 at m=2pp), so the amended rule is not even well-defined without a fallback. Its one incremental recovery, `GROSS/EWall` g=0.80 on broad, differs from R0's pick by **+0.0009** OOS Sharpe — 4b compliance, not performance. **(2) The premise's fatal half: the grids that produced the interior passes have no selectable content.** A 2x change in gross moves IS Sharpe by **0.0002-0.0046** and OOS Sharpe by 0.0001-0.0038 while moving IS MaxDD by 7-9pp (R0's pick there is fourth-decimal noise, landing on g=1.00 in 3 of 4 cells), and the crypto cap grid's IS MaxDD spread is **exactly 0.0000** on both universes because the in-sample max-drawdown episode predates the sleeve's tradeable window — a constraint blind to the parameter it constrains. **Rm recovers idea 15's c=0.05 in 0 of 8 (rule, universe) cells**, picking c=0.15 whenever feasible, which fails 4b on DD both full-sample and OOS on both lists. **(3) The margin is a second tuned parameter wearing a safety label:** `GROSS/top20` broad picks 1.00 -> 0.70 -> 0.60 -> 0.60 across R0/m=0/1/2 and four of six grids give a different pick per universe under at least one rule. **(4) Confirmed without any amendment:** 8 arms pass full-sample 4b on both universes, and idea 57's band book is the most robust object in the run (all four non-zero bands pass cross-universe; every feasible rule picks band=0.08), while idea 2's n=20 is picked on u56 and n=30 on broad, independently reproducing ideas 44/53's universe-specificity warning. **Proposed for the Sunday review — PROTOCOL 8a, a pre-test rather than a new selection rule:** report each grid's IS objective spread and the spread in each binding 4b bar; where IS Sharpe spread across the whole grid is under 0.02, or a binding constraint's spread is 0.00, the parameter is a policy dial, not an estimate — rule 8 does not apply and it must be set by a stated risk budget (idea 69). Rules unchanged; PROTOCOL rule 8 unchanged pending review.
- 2026-09-04 (lane C) — Idea 89 is-window-has-no-crash: **KILL**, rule 8's split stays at 2016. Moving it changes 8/12 (S13) and 5/12 (S21) published selections but <=0.034 realised 2022+ Sharpe on the selectable cells. Idea 87's premise refuted: S13/S16 share the same IS MaxDD (-22.1%) yet picks move, and a crash in the IS window makes 4b's DD cap LOOSER (it is relative to SPY on the same window). The binding in-sample 4b constraint is the CAGR floor, not the drawdown cap. Also: rule-8 selection is degenerate on grids whose parameter has no data in the IS window (crypto under S13). No RULES change.

- 2026-09-04 (cloud, idea 88 selectability-pre-test-across-the-leaderboard) — **KILL for PROTOCOL 8a as idea 87 worded it; a narrower replacement is recommended.** 11 one-parameter grids (N, fraction, gross x2, band, lookback, cost x2, cadence x2, hysteresis) x 2 universes = 22 cells / 122 arms, all reported; 2 tuned params (grid parameter, selection rule R0/R2); weekly, t+1, 10 bps except in the cost grids. Harness reproduces idea 2's KEEP row (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103) and idea 10's `B136/EWall` (10.7%/1.027/-17.7%) exactly, and the cost-free simulator matches `engine.backtest` to 0.00e+00. **(1) The retrospective the queue asked for comes back empty.** 8a fires on 4 of 22 cells and all four are the gross grids idea 87 proposed it from; every published n / fraction / band / lookback / cost / cadence / hysteresis sweep passes with IS Sharpe spread 0.040-0.502 against the 0.02 floor (nearest: `HYST/top20` u56 at 0.0398, where the pick is also the grid's OOS-best). **No walk-forward conclusion on the leaderboard outside idea 66's rested on a grid with no selectable content**, and the classification is unchanged for any threshold in 0.005-0.02. **(2) The clause's stated rationale is refuted, with the sign reversed.** 8a is worded as a safeguard on selection; mean REGRET (pick's OOS Sharpe minus the grid's OOS-best) is **-0.001 on flagged cells against -0.061 on unflagged**, Spearman(IS Sharpe spread, REGRET) over the 22 cells is **+0.256** where 8a predicts negative, and **the four worst selections in the run all PASS 8a**: broad `F/fraction` -0.310, u56 `F/fraction` -0.232, u56 `CADENCE/EWall` -0.182, broad `CADENCE/EWall` -0.105. The fraction cells reproduce idea 46 exactly — rule 8 picks f=0.15 and takes OOS 16.8%/0.941/**-27.8%** (u56) and 11.0%/0.715/**-29.9%** (broad) while the grid's OOS-best reads 1.173 and 1.026, and the 4b-aware rule R2 is *infeasible* on u56. This is structural, not bad luck: a flagged grid's arms differ in OOS Sharpe by 0.001-0.004, so the pre-test can only ever flag grids where the choice is costless on the objective. Mean SKILL (pick minus grid mean) is +0.039 (t +1.49) on PASS cells and +0.000 (t +0.37) on FAIL cells — the separation exists but it is the flagged grids being *inert*, not the unflagged ones being safe. **(3) What the flag does track is risk.** Flagged cells' OOS MaxDD spread is **11.3%** against 4.8% unflagged: u56 `GROSS/top20` has an IS Sharpe spread of **0.0002** (identical to 3 dp at every g) while OOS MaxDD runs -12.4% to -24.0%, and the fourth-decimal pick lands on g=0.80 on u56 and g=1.00 on broad. That is a genuine defect worth a clause — a risk-disclosure one. **Recommended wording for the Sunday review: `8a. Risk-consequence disclosure` — report every walk-forward grid's IS objective spread AND its OOS MaxDD spread; where the IS objective spread is under 0.02 Sharpe while the parameter moves MaxDD by more than 5pp, the parameter is a policy dial: record that rule 8's pick is not an estimate and set it from a stated drawdown budget (idea 69). Explicitly reject the draft's second half** ("only parameters that pass the pre-test are walk-forward selected") — on this evidence it would license exactly the selections that go wrong and forbid only the ones that cost nothing, and passing 8a must not be reported as evidence that rule 8 selected well. **(4) By-products, all reproductions:** `N/ranked` u56 picks n=20 under both rules (OOS 14.4%/1.170/-18.3%, idea 2 confirmed) and n=30 on broad (4b fail on DD — ideas 44/53 again); `CADENCE/top20` picks monthly on both lists with zero regret and monthly fails 4b on broad drawdown at -26.1% (idea 64's trade-off, walked into by the selection rule); `HYST/top20` u56 picks k=2.00, 12.7%/1.145/-17.2% at 3.9x/yr turnover, 4b PASS full and OOS (idea 86 confirmed). Both KEEP paths on all 122 arms: 4b full-sample 32/61 (u56) and 16/61 (broad), 4b OOS 43/61 and 19/61; **4a 3/61 on u56 and all three are g<=0.60 arms** that clear v1's -13.8% drawdown by de-grossing and then fail 4b's CAGR floor (idea 20/66's lever), 46/61 on broad where v1 itself draws down -21.2%. No new candidate. Survivorship: both lists are current constituents, so absolute CAGRs are optimistic; the run compares selection rules on common grids, so the bias falls on every arm alike. Rules unchanged; PROTOCOL rule 8 unchanged. Result memo: `research/backtests/2026-09-04_selectability-pre-test_cloud.result.md`.

- 2026-09-04 (cloud, idea 85 exit-schedule-vs-entry-schedule) — **Idea 83's mechanism claim is HALF REFUTED, and the remedy it implies works exactly where the claim is true and nowhere else: PARK on the unranked book, KILL on the ranked one.** 44 arms plus a 16-point gross ladder across 2 books x 2 universes, all reported; 2 tuned parameters (budget B in {inf,0.30,0.20,0.15,0.10,0.05}, mode in {entry-only, idea 83's pro-rata total}); weekly, t+1, 10 bps with 25 bps also reported; harness reproduces idea 2's `CAND20` (12.7%/1.093/-18.3%, halves 1.088/1.103) and idea 10/72's `B136/EWall` (10.7%/1.027/-17.7%, halves 1.146/0.917) exactly. **(1) The decomposition.** The entry and exit legs are 50.0-50.1% and 49.9-50.0% of Sigma|dw| on all four books — a self-financing long-only book that resets to a fixed gross cannot be otherwise, so "which leg is bigger" was never the question. The informative split is what the exit leg is made of: **gate exits are 24.8% (u56 CAND20) and 11.1% (broad CAND20) against rank displacement of 67.8% and 82.7%**, versus **56.6%/57.0% gate on EWall** (rank 0%, drift trims 43%). Idea 83's "book turnover is mostly the 200d gate's EXITS" is therefore **false on the ranked book its budget was tested on** — on the broad list 8 of every 9 dollars of selling is rank rotation — and true on the unranked one. **(2) The remedy, priced against the lever.** An entry-only budget (every exit honoured in full, buy leg capped at B, unspent proceeds to cash) on `EWall`: u56 B=0.10 reads **10.0%/1.100/-12.9% at 6.3x turnover** against the control's 10.4%/1.050/-15.9% at 8.2x, and broad B=0.20 reads **10.9%/1.077/-16.4% at 7.8x** against 10.7%/1.027/-17.7% at 8.3x. Exchange rate **-0.14 and -0.01 pp of CAGR per pp of MaxDD, against the gross lever's -0.63..-0.73 measured on the same days** (the ladder reproduces ideas 66/83 to 0.01 and confirms dSharpe = 0.000 across it). It is **not** the lever in disguise: at u56 B=0.10 gross falls only 5.5%, which at the lever's rate buys 0.9pp of drawdown, and the observed improvement is 3.0pp. The advantage widens with cost (u56 EWall Sharpe at 25 bps: 0.925 control -> 1.012 at B=0.05). **On `CAND20` the same instrument does nothing**: dSharpe +0.001..+0.007 on u56 until the budget begins de-grossing (0.717 -> 0.538 at B=0.05, where its exchange rate converges on the lever's own -0.68), and **negative at every budget on broad** (-0.002..-0.016, t -1.08..-3.68). The exit attribution predicts which book responds. **(3) Idea 83's total budget reproduces, sign and size:** gross untouched (0.739-0.750 at every B), turnover cut up to 70%, and **MaxDD deepens in 19 of 20 arms, mean -3.0pp** (idea 83 reported -2.4pp pro-rata), with dSharpe positive but never significant (t +0.17..+1.89). **(4) PARK, not KEEP.** No cross-universe 4b pass at a common budget: broad `EWall` B=0.20 turns the control's OOS 4b CAGR miss into a PASS (4b full PASS, 4b OOS PASS) while the same B on u56 `EWall` still fails 4b's CAGR floor as its control does; over all 44 arms 4b full is 16/44, 4b OOS 24/44 and 4a 17/44 (all the 4a passes are on broad, where v1 itself draws down -21.2%). And **rule 8 picks the wrong end of the grid — a textbook case of idea 88's finding**: on u56 `EWall` in-sample Sharpe is monotone DOWN in the budget (0.970 -> 0.934) while OOS Sharpe is monotone UP (1.114 -> 1.224), so R0 selects the weakest arm B=0.30 (OOS 1.124 against the grid's 1.224) and R2 is infeasible; on broad `EWall` R0 picks B=0.20 (OOS 1.097 vs best 1.113). The IS Sharpe spread there is 0.036 — just above idea 88's 0.02 floor, i.e. a grid that passes the selectability pre-test and is still selected backwards. Note the paired daily return t-test has no power on this instrument (CAGR moves -0.4pp/+0.2pp; the whole effect is in drawdown and vol), so t -0.23..+0.58 at the favourable arms is not evidence against it. Survivorship: both lists are current constituents, absolute CAGRs optimistic; every arm shares the panel and the days, so the control-vs-arm comparisons are far less exposed than the levels. **For the Sunday review: if a turnover instrument is ever adopted it must be entry-only and only on an unranked book** — the ranked book's selling is rank rotation, and constraining it either does nothing or silently de-grosses. Only the absorbing k=0 arms improve 2022, by being in permanent cash. **(6) Two results recorded against our own KILL:** turnover FALLS under the rule (u56 CAND20 9.6x -> median 7.8x/yr), so none of the loss is a trading-cost story — it is missing exposure during recoveries; and 36 of 288 arms are NOT dominated on the CAGR/drawdown axis, 24 of them in the single cell `broad/V1`, the worst book in the run (0.640 Sharpe, -21.2% MaxDD, failing all five 4b bars) — a drawdown rule is cheapest exactly where the book is not worth running. **(7) The 4a pathology again:** 4a passes RISE with cost (10 and 62 at 10 bps, 30 and 74 at 25 bps across the two lists) while 4b passes fall to **0 of 294 at 25 bps** — cutting exposure clears 4a only because RULES v1 is weak. **For the Sunday review: recommended RULES wording is none.** Idea 22 is now answered twice (idea 40 on the growth book, this run on the live book) and should be closed rather than re-parameterised; if drawdown is to be reduced, the supported instrument is the gross number itself, stated as a budget. So a whole-window MaxDD denominator is a crisis depth in disguise times a tier coefficient. Tier by tier: book-level DD control **+0.320** (t 11.6, R2 0.31 — the steepest, and the direct mechanism behind open idea 118), per-name gate +0.179 (t 12.4), entry budget +0.062, **per-name trailing stop +0.012 (t +1.46): its protection does not respond to crisis depth at all**. Harness sanity: both state-machine controls reproduce `engine.backtest` at max|diff| **0.0e+00** in all 12 cells and reproduce the live book and idea 2's standing candidate to the decimal. **(1) The absorbing state is exact, not a tendency:** at k=0.00 with equity-conditioned re-entry (`high` or `recover`), **140 of 140 arms that ever armed never released**, mean capture **724 rebalances** (max 919 = the entire remaining sample) — the cut is what freezes the equity the release condition reads, so the rule fires once and the book is in cash for life. The 4 exceptions never armed. At k>0 episode length scales as ~1/k (`high` 724/218/109/69 at k=0.00/0.25/0.50/0.75). **(2) The diagnosis in idea 22's wording is WRONG and this run says so on its own pre-registered prediction.** I predicted a per-name stop reading the NAME's price would be safe because the name keeps trading; it is not. Release rate / mean block: `free` 0.999 / 2.6 days, `spy200` 0.999 / 35.3, **`nhigh` 0.951 / 250.9** (8.4 names permanently out), **`bookhigh` 0.863 / 285.4**. Both **high-water-mark** arms are near-absorbing and one non-HWM arm is endogenous — so the operative property is *a re-entry condition demanding a state variable regain a running maximum*, not "a function of the book's own equity". PROTOCOL rule 4b's CAGR floor and drawdown cap ARE jointly satisfiable on this data and the incumbent (0.70, 0.60) sits comfortably inside the non-empty region: 4b is a screen, not a wall. Rules unchanged; no new KEEP; one REPORT-ONLY PROTOCOL clause proposed.** Reproduction was asserted before any new number was read: `fast_backtest` vs `products/backtester/engine.backtest` at **2.776e-17**, idea 171's **530 of 530** committed GROSS-dial ladder rows re-derived at **2.220e-16**, and idea 171's headline premise re-counted on its own committed file (**CAGR 1223 of 1908, exact**). The two swept parameters are the idea itself — PHI (16 points) x DELTA (20 points) = **320 grid cells, all reported** — and the sweep costs zero extra backtests because pass/fail at any cell is a pure function of `c = CAGR/CAGR_SPY` and `d = |MaxDD|/|MaxDD_SPY|`, computed once per point on a 1590-point corpus (idea 171's 53 books x 10 gross x 3 sleeve, 10 bps, t+1, weekly). **At the incumbent: 173 points clear both coefficients (31 of 53 distinct books) and 151 clear all five bars of 4b; `phi_max(0.60) = 0.9569`, i.e. +0.2569 of headroom before the pair empties.** The three Sharpe bars close only 13 of the 320 cells that the two coefficients leave open. **The pair reduces to ONE number:** because `c` and `d` scale together on the gross ladder, a point satisfies both iff its efficiency ratio `k = c/d >= phi/delta = 1.1667`; median k is 1.376 and **51 of 53 books** clear it. Idea 164 (cloud, same day) derived the identical constant from the other side — "non-empty iff `rho/s <= delta/gamma = 0.857`", and 1/1.1667 = 0.8571 — two independent derivations agreeing to 4 decimals. **Idea 171's premise reproduces and is re-read, which is the run's real content:** the CAGR floor IS the most-violated bar here too (1280 of 1590 violations, sole binding for 1021, against H2 243 / DD 153 / H1 127 / OOS 116), but that is a fact about the LADDER the project sweeps, not about the bar — mean `c ~= 0.856 x gross`, so the floor mechanically needs `g >~ 0.82` and 8 of the 10 gross rungs sit below it (4b pass rate **0.0% at every g <= 0.60**, 10.7-23.9% at g >= 0.70). `Spearman(c, d) = +0.9340` full sample and +0.9166 OOS: return and drawdown are bought together, which is the measured mechanism behind idea 171's Sharpe-vs-margin sign flip. Rule 8, both forms: the region is a **stable object** (IS-window and OOS-window maps agree on emptiness in 306 of 320 cells, `Spearman(n_IS, n_OOS) = +0.9942`), but the (phi, delta) screen **is not a selector** — the IS-chosen pick returns OOS 8.03%/0.9804/-12.93% against a do-nothing control's 5.36%/**1.0553**/-8.96% (**-0.0749**), beating the control in only **3 of 240** non-empty cells; that is the fifth consecutive instance after ideas 110/132/151/166/171 and the screen must not be added to rule 8. Both KEEP paths at the incumbent, all 1590 points: 4a 1430, 4b 151, both 142, passers B136 141 / U56 10 / **SMALL484 zero** (consistent with idea 170); 4a's near-universal pass is de-grossing beating the low-return live book's drawdown, which is PROTOCOL's own stated reason for adding 4b. Per idea 144 every 4b passer is an idea-171 book re-grossed, so **no new KEEP candidate is proposed**. The memo proposes REPORT-ONLY PROTOCOL clause 11 (publish `k` alongside every 4b CAGR-floor or DD-cap failure, and state whether `k >= 1.167`) so that "fails at the gross it was priced at" stops being reported as "fails the bar". Pre-registered predictions scored 6 hits and **1 miss** — P3 predicted a Sharpe bar would bind at the incumbent; the CAGR floor binds, 1280 to 243. Caveat carried, not buried: survivorship (idea 54) biases every `c` up and every `d` down, so the region looks MORE reachable than it is — "satisfiable" is the conservative direction and "a wall" would have been the strong claim. PROTOCOL clause 11 extends to overlays as a REPORT-ONLY column carrying a stated turnover caveat; as a SELECTION GATE it is a KILL. Rules unchanged; no new book; no KEEP candidate.** Idea 181 built clause 11's null for a KEYED TILT and explicitly left the sleeve, entry-budget and drawdown-control constructions un-priced. **The definition this run supplies:** an overlay is a pair (s, A) — an ON indicator evaluated at the book's rebalance dates plus an action applied while on — and its matched null is the SAME action on a **circular rotation** of s. Rotation is the right null because it preserves the on-share and the episode structure exactly and destroys only *when* the overlay fires; a permutation shatters episodes and a re-drawn state variable changes the construction rather than the timing. Corpus: 3 panels (U56, BROAD136, SMALL439 — the 483-name sub-$2B panel with the 44 `max_1d_move >= 1.0` tickers dropped) x 3 families (DDCTL drawdown control, BUDGET entry/turnover budget, SLEEVE conditional TLT/GLD/UUP) x 3 thresholds x 2 depths x 2 cost rungs x (1 real + 20 rotations) = **2268 rows, 108 real**; base book fixed at idea 2's top-20 EW composite, no vol scaler, gross 0.75, weekly, t+1; both cost rungs derived exactly from a single 0 bps run via the engine's own turnover series. Four reproduction controls asserted before any new number: `fast_backtest` == `engine.backtest` (2.8e-17), the cost identity (2.8e-17), CAND-20 weights == idea 78/171's `weights_cand` (**0.0e+00**), and the null itself validated — **on-share preserved in 2160 of 2160 draws and the circular switch count in 2160 of 2160**. DDCTL uses a TRAILING 252-day high rather than a running high-water mark, because idea 93 established that HWM re-entry is absorbing. **(1) The null is exact where it matters and NOT exact everywhere, and the run says which.** Realised turnover matches to **1.25% mean (DDCTL) and 0.82% (SLEEVE)** but only **25.4% mean and 213.8% max for BUDGET-skip**, because suppressing a rebalance genuinely changes trading. Idea 186's phrasing — "the same on-share AND turnover" — is therefore achievable for overlays that scale or reallocate weights and **not** for one that suppresses a trade, and the proposed clause publishes the gap instead of hiding it. **(2) As a REPORTING column it is informative rather than bookkeeping: 17 of 108 real overlays clear (15.7% on Sharpe, 9.3% on drawdown), about half idea 181's 32.8% for keyed tilts, and it separates the three constructions cleanly — DDCTL 15/36 (42%), BUDGET 2/36 (6%), SLEEVE 0 of 36 (0%).** The reading is sharper than the count: **all 15 clearing DDCTL points have NEGATIVE dSharpe, -0.19 to -0.52** — the drawdown control's effect is distinguishable from random timing and reliably harmful, an independent confirmation of idea 93 on a different construction — while **the conditional sleeve's entire effect (dSharpe -0.188..+0.032) sits inside a null band whose max averages 0.176**, i.e. an equally-frequent randomly-timed sleeve delivers the same thing, including the drawdown improvement that makes the sleeve attractive (u56 ma=200/f=0.5: MaxDD -14.07% against the base's -18.21% and OOS Sharpe 1.2333 against 1.1775, and it does not clear). **527 of the committed LEADERBOARD's 3330 data rows mention a sleeve**; 54 mention a drawdown control or trailing stop and 11 an entry/turnover budget. **(3) The clause moves no verdicts** — idea 181's Q2, asked of overlays: the 4b verdict is identical in **91.5%** of the 2160 real-vs-null swaps and 4a in 83.4%, and a **randomly-timed overlay clears 4b MORE often than the real one (20.7% of null rows against 16.7% of real rows; 4a 25.5% vs 22.2%)**, the same direction idea 181 found for tilts. **Every one of the 18 real overlay rows that clears 4b is inside its own null band** (17 on u56, 1 on broad), so the clause would flag 18 of 18 overlay-based 4b passes as noise while changing none of them. **(4) Rule 8, the overlay point chosen on <= 2016-12-31 and 2017-2026 read once, 18 cells: a KILL of the fit and of the gate.** S0 do-nothing 0.7766 mean OOS Sharpe; S1 IS-Sharpe argmax 0.7334, paired **-0.0432 (t -2.00), winning 6 of 18**; S2 the same argmax gated on the clause read on the IS window 0.7405, paired **-0.0361 (t -2.62), winning 0 of 18**, abstaining in 11 cells and agreeing with S1 in only 3. Per idea 144 an overlaid book is the same book with an instrument on it, so nothing here is proposed. 4 of 108 cells are inert by construction — u56 DDCTL at D=0.15 never fires and its dSharpe is exactly 0.0 — and are reported as such rather than counted as evidence. **(6) All 7 pre-registered predictions HIT**, including P3 (SLEEVE clears least) and P4 (DDCTL clears most), which were written before the sign of DDCTL's effect was known. - 2026-09-05 (cloud, idea 194 abstention-is-the-only-thing-that-ever-helps) — **ANSWERED, and idea 194's hypothesis is HALF RIGHT IN THE STRONGEST POSSIBLE WAY: abstention is EXACTLY a dilution toward doing nothing and NEVER a source of gain. As a KEEP path or a rule-8 arm every gate is a KILL. Report-only rule-8 clause 8b proposed; no new book; RULES untouched.** 378-book corpus (3 panels x 7 keys x 9 shares x 2 cost rungs, weekly, t+1, gross 0.75 `norm`) rebuilt by IMPORTING idea 177's `build_panels()`/`build_base()`, so the corpus under test is literally the code that produced the corpus in the run beside it. CELL = (panel, cost rung, share) = **54 cells**; MENU = the 7 keys; CONTROL = NONE (the composite with no cross-sectional tilt — the natural 'apply no key'); CANDIDATES = the other 6 including idea 159's RND scramble. Exactly 2 tuned params (abstention threshold τ ∈ {−inf, 0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20} on the gate's IS-Sharpe margin over the control, and the IS selector ∈ {IS_SHARPE, IS_CALMAR, IS_MAXDD, IS_CAGR, IS_4B}) = **25 gates, every grid point printed**, plus S0 do-nothing and RANDOM as controls. **Reproduction 2/2 EXACT:** corpus vs idea 165's published .grid.csv (n 0.0, CAGR 9.71e-17, Sharpe/H1/H2/OOS_Sharpe 2.22e-16, MaxDD 8.33e-17), and **[c] the ABSTAIN-ALWAYS identity at 0.000e+00** over all 54 cells. **(1) THE FIRST ANSWER IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT.** In this project's own convention a gate that admits nothing HOLDS the cell's control book, and S0 IS that control book, so on an abstained cell the paired difference is identically zero: a pure abstain-always arm is not an approximation of do-nothing, **it IS do-nothing**. Hence `gain(G) = a·0 + (1−a)·c` where a is the abstention rate and c the mean choice effect on picked cells — **and the identity holds to 3.47e-18 across all 25 gates**. 'How much of the gate's gain is explained by its abstention rate alone' therefore has an exact answer: **none of it as a source, all of it as a scaling.** **(2) Abstention is pure dilution — 5 of 5.** Per selector, sign(slope of gain in a) = −sign(c₀) in every one: IS_MAXDD c₀ −0.1258 → slope **+0.1450, R² 0.961**; IS_CAGR c₀ +0.0145 → slope −0.0277, R² 0.810; IS_SHARPE c₀ +0.0099 → slope −0.0191, R² 0.599; IS_CALMAR and IS_4B the same sign at low R². **But POOLED across the 25 gates the R² of gain on a alone is 0.002** — the rate explains nothing across gates because c is not constant, so idea 194's literal wording is FALSE and the identity is what is true. **(3) Is the abstention CHOICE skilful? Matched-rate random-abstention null (abstain in the same NUMBER of cells, chosen at random, 2000 draws): 5 of 19 testable gates escape — and the DIRECTION is the finding.** All three ABOVE-band gates are IS_MAXDD, the worst selector in the run: its gate claws −0.1258 up to −0.0087 (p 0.000 / 0.008 / 0.017) and **never above zero**. Both BELOW-band gates are the DECENT selectors at τ=0.20 — IS_SHARPE gain −0.0104 vs null [−0.0084,+0.0116] p 0.020, IS_CAGR −0.0119 vs [−0.0078,+0.0133] p 0.005 — i.e. at a high threshold the gate declines in exactly the cells its selector would have won. **A gate never manufactures a gain; at best it undoes its own selector's damage, approaching do-nothing from below.** **(4) Rule 8 (everything fitted ≤2016-12-31, 2017–2026 read ONCE, 54 cells, 27 arms): the NINTH consecutive do-nothing win.** S0 mean OOS Sharpe **0.7195** (10.31% CAGR, −25.71% MaxDD); best of all 27 arms IS_CAGR ungated 0.7340 (**+0.0145, t +1.09**, 33W/21L) — insignificant; worst IS_MAXDD ungated 0.5937 (−0.1258, t −6.67, 9W/45L); RANDOM 0.6812 (−0.0383, t −1.91). Every one of the 25 gates lies within [−0.0219, +0.0145] of S0. Both KEEP paths on the OOS window: **S0 4a 17/54 and 4b 12/54**, max over all arms 4b 15/54 — **no arm is promoted**. Benchmarks: SPY OOS 15.45%/0.8820/−33.72%; RULES v1 @10bps u56 7.73%/0.7471/−13.83%, broad 5.94%/0.5763/−21.19%, small 7.92%/0.5807/−32.84%. **(5) The record back-fill** (idea 194's 'for every published selector in the record'): 74 `*.walkforward.csv` scanned, **only 18 carry a recoverable abstention schema**, 74 published selector arms recovered — mean abstention rate 0.364, 50 abstain at all and 3 abstain always; OOS gain vs each file's own control mean +0.0349 but **median −0.0294 with only 24 of 74 positive**, and among the 50 abstainers `gain = +0.0669 − 0.0451·a` at **R² 0.005** — the same null as the fresh experiment. That 56 of 74 files record no abstention signal at all is itself the argument for the column. **Predictions P1 HIT, P2 HIT, P3 MISS (informatively — the escapes point the other way), P4 MISS, P5 HIT, P6 HIT.** Proposed report-only rule-8 wording **8b**: a rule-8 arm that declines to pick holds the control, so abstain-always is identically do-nothing; report every gate's ABSTENTION RATE beside its OOS gain and read the gain as (1−a)·c; a gate may only be claimed to add value if it beats a MATCHED-RATE RANDOM-ABSTENTION null at the same a. Survivorship carried (current-constituent panels; small = sub-$2B screen less the 44 `max_1d_move ≥ 1.0` tickers, joined never-selectable SPY) and the 54 cells share three price panels so every t-stat is optimistic — the permutation null is the inference this run leans on.
