- 2026-09-05 (lane C, idea 208 audit-every-committed-null-for-a-salted-seed) — **ANSWERED, and the answer is worse than the question.** The census is small and the fix is one line: an AST audit of all 166 committed `.py` (165 parse) finds **5 `hash()` sites, 4 of them seeds, in 2 scripts** — idea 191's `the-on-share-column_cloud.py` (lines 435, 580) and `the-share-at-which-ranking-stops-paying_B.py` (536, 581). The site that matters reaches the RNG through a **locally defined helper's `seed` parameter** (`rotations(J, N_NULL, SEED + hash((pan.name, fam, thr)) % 10_000)`), so a `default_rng(` grep misses the corpus's single largest exposure; a two-child-process probe confirms a str-bearing hash differs per process while `hash(3)` and `hash((1,2,3))` do not. **Exposure: 612 of 10,472 published draw-derived cells (5.8%) and 540 of 4,628 clause verdicts (11.7%).** By-product: 0 of 34 randomness-using scripts draw unseeded, so this is the only hole of its kind. **The re-draw is exact, not sampled:** idea 191 draws 20 of the J−1 = 974 circular rotations, so enumerating the WHOLE population (30 U56 configs × 975 × 2 cost rungs = **29,250 genuine backtests**) makes the draw law closed-form, `P(clears) = C(K,20)/C(974,20)`. Idea 191's 60 U56 real rows reproduce first at **max |Δ| 1.4e-15** through its own code. Then: **0 of 60 published cells clear with probability 1, 10 with probability 0, and 50/60 = 83.3% are UNDETERMINED**; E[# clearing] 12.04 ± 1.61 against 10 published; **expected verdict flips vs the published draw 6.00/60 = 10.0%**, worst cell P(flip) 0.864; two independent 20-draw seeds disagree on **8.7%** of cells — the exact counterpart of idea 201's sampled 17.8%. The band's own 5–95% draw range is **98.5% of the median band**, and the undetermined zone is 0.3070 wide on a mean |dSharpe| of 0.0862 — **356% of the effect being tested**; only 10 of 60 cells have P outside [0.1, 0.9]. **So a correct seed buys reproducibility, not a verdict: the 20-draw band is the disease and the salt is the symptom.** Rule 8 prices it: pick on ≤2016 within family by largest IS margin, read 2017→ once, under 200 independent seed regimes — **23.7% of (cell, seed) draws pick a different overlay**, within-cell OOS Sharpe range up to **0.3832**, best seed 1.177 / worst **0.826** (OOS CAGR 14.7% vs **7.2%**) against the do-nothing control **1.177 / 14.5% / −18.2%**, SPY 0.882 / 15.5% / −33.7%, RULES v1 0.399 / 3.8% / −14.2%. **0 of 6 cells beat do-nothing (best cell mean dOOS −0.0026, pooled −0.0738, best single seed +0.0000) — the twelfth consecutive do-nothing win.** KEEP paths on the 60 real rows: 4a 7/60, 4b 27/60, of which **0 clear their own null with probability 1**, 18 undetermined, 9 never, and **8 are the inert control book** (on-share 0, idea 200's defect reproduced from an independent direction) — no 4b pass on this grid is defensible as an overlay effect. No new book proposed; PROTOCOL.md and RULES.md untouched (rule 6). **Proposals: (5) forbid `hash()` of a str or of a tuple containing one as a seed — use an int literal, `zlib.crc32(key.encode())` or an int-built `SeedSequence`, and print seeds; (11b) publish `clears` only beside `P(clears)` or as UNDETERMINED, and where the null population is enumerable, enumerate it (975 backtests per configuration here) instead of drawing a band.** 5 of 5 pre-registered predictions hit. Caveats carried: survivorship (U56 current constituents, levels biased upward), correlated neighbouring rotations (the enumeration is exact for the draw law, not for the clause's power), BROAD136/SMALL439 not re-drawn, the MaxDD mean range ratio is a divide-by-zero artefact of the 8 inert cells (median 67.9% is the usable figure).

Rules unchanged; no book; no KEEP.** Reproduction before any new number: `fast_backtest` == `engine.backtest` at 1.4e-17/2.1e-17/2.8e-17, CAND-20 weights **0.000e+00** on all three panels, RULES v1 on U56 0.66418 exact, idea 191's **180 of 180** published real rows at **9.7e-17**, and idea 208's 60 U56 cells identical on 176 of 180 (K,N) pairs — the 4 disputes being cells whose real effect is 0 to machine precision with 169-352 tied rotations and a largest disputed gap of **2.220e-16**, a tie-breaking convention rather than a different population. **(1)** Using every rotation in turn as a pseudo-real (169,020 per row), the incumbent max-of-n rule's measured size is **1/(n+1) EXACTLY** — 0.04762 / 0.01961 / 0.00990 / 0.00498 to five decimals — so the sibling run's inference from band drift is confirmed in closed form: n is the test's alpha, not its precision. **(2) Under the incumbent form more draws are strictly WORSE**: expected disagreement with the enumerated truth rises **0.0742 -> 0.1009 -> 0.1392 -> 0.1739** on Sharpe and the undetermined zone WIDENS (0.1031 -> 0.1574 at eps = 0.10). **(3) At a fixed level** — the permutation p-value `(#{|d_null| >= |d_real|} + 1)/(n+1) <= alpha`, the exact-inference form of the sibling's Q95 proposal and identical to the incumbent max-of-20 at alpha = 0.05 — flip vs truth falls **0.0742 -> 0.0516 -> 0.0312 -> 0.0238**, two-seed disagreement 0.1003 -> 0.0313, and the zone falls from **104.0% to 20.6% of the mean |dSharpe| (0.0991)**. **(4) Two corrections to the sibling run, both in the direction of MORE draws.** Its caveat states J ~ 670/600; the enumeration counts **J-1 = 974 / 974 / 869**, so a 400-draw pool is 41-46% of the population, not 60-67%. And its 'K=200 doubles the cost for no measured gain' rests on ONE disjoint block pair per configuration (its own P5 miss): under the exact law n=200 is 24% better than n=100 on flip rate and 36% better on zone width, so **100 is a floor, not an optimum**, and the complete population — 2.4x a 400-draw pool, 4.9x a 200-draw band — is exact. A single 20-draw realisation misses its own clause's expectation by 2-6pp (sibling's realised 15.6%/6.1% against the exact 17.7%/11.9%), which is the instability both runs were commissioned to measure showing up in the measurement itself. **(5) Independent cross-checks that agree exactly: 4a 37/180, 4b 28/180, SMALL439 0/60, S0 do-nothing 10.22%/0.7766/-23.53%, and 0 of 8 clause-gated rule-8 settings beating do-nothing** (best MAXN/200 -0.0131 t -14.0, level-alpha/200 -0.0946, ungated -0.0560; SPY OOS 15.45%/0.8820/-33.72%) — the **thirteenth consecutive do-nothing win**, with MAXN's apparent improvement in n exposed as idea 194's dilution identity: its abstention rate climbs 0.531 -> 0.851, so it improves only by acting less. - 2026-09-06 (cloud, idea 188 COMPANION RUN — can-a-panel-property-choose-the-cadence) — **A sibling cloud lane answered idea 188 on 2026-09-05 while this run was in flight (the queue read as open when this lane claimed it at 00:00 UTC). This is the companion, not a replacement: it measures the same two properties independently, agrees with both, and then takes the step idea 77's clause actually requires — turning each property into a rule-8 SELECTOR. That step is a KILL. Rules unchanged; no book; neither KEEP path claimed.** Idea 175's corpus, cadence mask, backtest and KEEP evaluators imported verbatim; **its published 805-row ladder reproduces 805/805 at 2.2e-16** and its 28-cell constants table at 8.3e-17, including the split under test (SMALL M +0.0978 / 6W +0.0163; U56 6W +0.1640; ETF 6W +0.1600). **(1) Signal decay is not merely absent as a mechanism, it points the other way.** Cross-sectional rank IC of the composite against forward return, eligible names only, sampled every 21 bars so windows do not overlap: on U56 the IC RISES monotonically **+0.0639@21d -> +0.1481@126d (t 2.76 -> 6.59)** and on ETF +0.0470 -> +0.1291, while on SMALL it is **+0.0045 at h=21 with |t| <= 1.55 at every horizon on the grid**. The large-cap signal does not decay over any horizon tested; the small panel has no cross-sectional signal to decay. The IR-optimal horizon `argmax IC(h)/sqrt(h)` lands at h=5d on all three fixed panels, so the statistic that ought to select the cadence selects the ladder's fastest point everywhere and cannot produce the split. **(2) Holding-episode length (idea 76's measure, made cadence-free on daily top-20 membership) orders the families the right way — SMALL 18.8d < U56 31.3d < ETF 38.8d (fixed panels 9.0 / 17.2 / 22.9) — but is not a clause:** alone it explains R2 0.173 of the M-minus-6W gap, with h* 0.204, against **0.445 for the family dummies alone**, and adding the dummy on top of both properties still lifts R2 to 0.452. Spearman(gap, episode_days) is -0.386 pooled but +0.072 / +0.141 / -0.008 within ETF / SMALL / U56 — the correlation is entirely between-family, the signature of a re-labelling. No RULES change, no book promoted, no KEEP candidate; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Reproduction first: idea 71's published membership cell re-derives **to the digit — STK20 overlaps the ex-post best-20 of BSTK100 by 10 of 20 against 4.0 expected, hypergeometric P = 6.475e-4** — but only once the ranking window starts at the frame's 260th bar, the same post-warm-up start every book in this project is evaluated from; started at the raw first bar the same cell reads 8/20 at p 0.018, because 13 rather than 11 of the 100 superset names had not listed yet. **That is the first finding: a published overlap p-value is a function of the window start and of how late-listing names are counted, and neither has ever been stated beside one.** Both conventions are therefore run for every cell — **PUB** (idea 71's: unrankable names count in N but cannot enter the top-k) and **COV** (dropped from both N and k) — crossed with 2 ex-post metrics (TOTRET, SHARPE) and 3 windows (FULL, IS <= 2016-12-31, OOS >= 2017), all with EXACT integer hypergeometric tails, no normal approximation and no scipy; 200 seeded uniform draws confirm the null (mean overlap 3.99 against the hypergeometric 4.00). **THE CENSUS the queue asked for, 7 panels x 2 conventions x 6 cells:** `STK20` **5 of 6 COV cells significant, min p 1.1e-4**; `BSTK100` vs the pooled large+small superset 6 of 6 (min p 2.7e-36) but **size-confounded and flagged, never read as clean**; `SMALL439`'s own `max_1d_move >= 1.0` screen **3 of 6 on TOTRET (p 1.6e-3 FULL, 7.5e-7 OOS) and 0 of 6 on SHARPE** — the screen is return-loaded but not risk-adjusted-loaded, and its verdict **INVERTS between the conventions** (PUB p = 1.00 with 216 of 483 names unrankable, COV p = 1.6e-3); and **`BROAD8` 0/6, `SECT16` 0/6, `BFC12` 0/6**, with BFC12 ANTI-loaded (0 of its 12 names in the ex-post top-12, p = 1.00, as a diversifier sleeve should be). So the ETF sleeves of universe.json are clean and the megacap list is not. **`ETF36` has no offline superset at all — it IS the cached ETF list — and is printed as untestable rather than scored**, which is the honest answer to 43 of the leaderboard's rows. **THE BOOK EVIDENCE.** One pre-registered book (RULES v1's composite ranked WITHIN the panel, n=10, gross 0.75, NORM, weekly, t+1) on 9 panels x 3 rungs, cost identity 0.000e+00, plus the two counterfactual panels the overlap test implies on STK20's own superset: **`HIND20_IS`** (top 20 of BSTK100 by 2009-2016 return — knowable on 2017-01-01, hence a REAL ex-ante rule) and **`HIND20_OOS`** (top 20 by 2017-2026 return — pure look-ahead). OOS Sharpe at 10 bps: **STK20 1.386 > HIND20_OOS 1.309 > HIND20_IS 1.052 > U56 0.890 > SPY 0.882 > BSTK100 0.607 > SMALL439 0.413**, and OOS CAGR 22.7% / 24.7% / 14.6% / 9.4% / 15.5%. **The hand-picked panel beats the look-ahead ceiling for the very window it was supposed to be tested on, and beats the honest ex-ante rule by +0.334 of Sharpe and +8.1 pp of CAGR.** Its OOS-window overlap is 8/20 with HIND20_OOS (p 0.018) against 7/20 with HIND20_IS. **The decay column says the same thing in one number:** the real ex-ante rule decays as an honest selection must (IS 1.484 -> OOS 1.052, **+0.433**) while the hand-curated panel IMPROVES out of sample (0.995 -> 1.386, **-0.391**), as does the look-ahead ceiling (-0.306); the un-curated panels decay normally (B136 +0.261, BSTK100 +0.307, SMALL439 +0.210). **Negative IS->OOS decay on a hand-curated panel is the fingerprint, and it costs one column.** **RULE 8 IS WHERE THE IDEA'S OWN PROPOSAL DIES:** used as a pre-registration FILTER on IS information alone, the test flags **all three testable panels at p < 0.05** (STK20 0.036, SMALL439 1.6e-3, BSTK100 3.9e-4), so it has nothing to choose between; ranked by that p-value it calls **STK20 the CLEANEST** and STK20 is exactly the panel the full-window test flags hardest. `CLEAN_PICK` = STK20 (OOS 1.386), `LOADED_PICK` = BSTK100 (0.607), `IS_SHARPE_PICK` = HIND20_IS (1.052), `ANCHOR` = do nothing on U56 (0.890). The mechanism is not subtle: a list written in 2026 is loaded on EVERY window, so restricting the test to the IS window does not measure how much hindsight the list carries — **the test is diagnostic only when run against the window under evaluation**, which is a reporting requirement, not a selection rule. **KEEP paths:** 4b **1 of 27** book-rung points (U56 at 0 bps alone), **0 at 10 and 25 bps**; 4a 6/27. Nothing promoted. **What PROTOCOL should carry (for Sunday review, not applied here):** beside every panel a result quotes, publish the overlap count, its expectation, the exact hypergeometric p, the number of unrankable names, the convention, and the window — and where no offline superset exists, print that instead of a number. On this record that column would flag 53 leaderboard rows naming STK20 and 42 naming SMALL439, clear the 43 ETF-sleeve rows, and leave 43 ETF36 rows explicitly unscored. CAVEATS: every superset is itself current constituents, so delisted names are absent from panel and superset alike and all counts are LOWER bounds on the true selection; the two ALLSTK rows mix size with hindsight and are flagged; the hypergeometric null is a uniform k-of-N draw, which no curator performs, so a small p means 'not uniform' and it is the EX-POST ordering that makes it a hindsight finding; only 3 panels have a superset, so the link between overlap and performance is printed as a table and not fitted.

Tested on every committed (CAGR,Sharpe,Vol) triple in the corpus — **10061 rows from 16 CSVs, median relative error 3.96e-4, p90 8.45e-4, 98.63% within 1%, 92.59% within 0.1%**; all 138 failures sit at positive Sharpe and are the dropped third-moment term, not the sign ambiguity. Both pre-registered bars (>=95% within 1%; R^2>0.90 IS and OOS) cleared. **(3) The reach is the constraint.** `LEADERBOARD.md` has 3753 data rows of which **1515 are byte-identical duplicates** (2238 distinct — a pre-existing rebase artefact, so any count quoted off that file without de-duplication is inflated). - 2026-09-06 (cloud, idea 277 how-many-published-gate-claims-are-flat-in-gross) — **ANSWERED: the flatness idea 274 measured is an IDENTITY, not a finding, so NO published Sharpe verdict can be a gross artefact through this channel; the exposure channel lands on CAGR and MaxDD, and the record's real weakness is that only 9.3% of its gate/overlay grids can be audited for it at all. The reportable statistic is therefore the SHARE, not the sign: on `dg` arms the gross channel alone carries a mean **59.4%** of the published dCAGR and **54.0%** of the published dMaxDD, a majority of the difference in **54/72** cells each; on `rw` arms it carries **0.000**. Realised gross runs within **0.0003** of nominal under `rw` and **-0.17** (large caps) / **-0.34** (small) below it under `dg`. The CONVENTION, not the instrument, is what manufactures the gap. **(4) THE CENSUS.** 853 committed grid CSVs (this run's own excluded) -> 541 carrying a Sharpe-like column -> **323 with gate/overlay vocabulary**, of which only **30 (9.3%)** commit a REALISED gross column; **90** are nominal-gross-only and **203** carry no gross column at all. Two more (`gross-as-the-missing-third-bar`, `gross-dispersion-not-gross-level`) carry an `m_GROSS` ranging to **-0.22**, which is not a gross level and is flagged rather than scored. Scoring **5033 within-group comparisons** (grouped on whatever of panel/universe/cost/book/family/conv/kind the parent committed, so no comparison crosses a panel or a rung): **3851 (76.5%)** are made across a gross gap wider than the ladder's own Sharpe span and **2879 (57.2%)** across a gap wider than 0.05 of realised gross. But the consequence splits by axis: **only 299/5033 (5.9%)** of published dSharpe differences are inside what the ladder buys — the flatness that motivated the worry is exactly what makes a Sharpe verdict immune to it — against **947/4849 (19.5%)** of dCAGR and **935/4849 (19.3%)** of dMaxDD differences ENTIRELY inside it. Among differences larger than 1pp the gross-channel share is median **+0.353** for CAGR (majority-exposure in 40.1%) and **+0.401** for MaxDD (43.7%). **(5) RULE 8:** the pre-registered IS-Sharpe chooser (IS <= 2016-12-31, OOS >= 2017-01-01 read once) beats do-nothing in **2 of 6** cells, mean OOS Sharpe **0.876 vs the live book's 0.967** (SPY 0.882) — the **12th** selection-loses instance in the record. It does beat its own gross-matched ungated ladder point in **4 of 6** (mean 0.951), so the gates carry OOS information the ladder does not; just less than doing nothing carries. Spearman(IS, OOS) +0.14..+0.95. **(6) KEEP census: 4a 0/144; 4b 17/144** (U56 10, B136 7, SMALL439 0) — and **9 of the 17 are beaten by their own gross-matched un-gated ladder point**, including **7 of the 9** `rw` passes. The best 4b arm, `band3/dg/g1.00` on U56 @10bps (11.59% / 1.2054 / -15.91%), is the live book at a different gross. No candidate, no memo. **WHAT PROTOCOL SHOULD CARRY:** a realised-mean-gross column beside every published arm. SURVIVORSHIP: U56/B136/SMALL439 are current constituents only, and the bias runs AGAINST the un-gated arm (it holds the names a delisting-aware panel would kill), so a survivorship-free panel would make the gates look better, not worse — stated, not adjusted.

The plateau test gives a median **2 of 17** arms within 0.02 Sharpe of the cell argmax, spanning a median 0.44 flips/tkr/yr. The one shape that survives is the pooled, level-differenced curve (each cell's 17 Sharpes minus that cell's own mean): the **<0.5 flips/tkr/yr bucket is the WORST in 4 of 4 (book x convention) pools** (-0.0034, -0.0402, -0.0418, -0.0518) and the curve is flat to within +/-0.05 above it. **Below about half a flip per ticker-year the gate is too slow to be a gate; above it, where the argmax lands is not information.** **(3) IT IS NOT A GROSS LADDER, and the check is exact.** Applying this morning's idea 277 control — re-reading every point against the un-gated constant-gross ladder at its OWN realised mean gross — leaves Spearman(flips, Sharpe) **unchanged to 4 decimal places in all 24 cells**, which is precisely idea 277's identity result (the ladder's Sharpe span is 0.0013-0.0039 and cannot re-rank a 0.109-0.295 range). Out of sample the speed relationship is gone entirely: mean Spearman(flips, OOS Sharpe) **+0.081**, negative in only 9/24; mean Spearman(IS, OOS) over the 17 arms +0.144. **(5) KEEP census: 4a 2/408** — both `ew-all/dg/BAND0.05` on SMALL439 where the live book is weak, not a real win — **4b 41/408** (U56 32, B136 9, SMALL439 0), binding bar over the 367 failures is **DD** (119 alone, 296 including it) then CAGR. The mechanism is **cash-day relocation at constant total premium**: full-sample cash days are flat (**16.0 / 17.4 / 17.5 / 17.4%**) while the H1/H2 split swings **13.8/18.2 -> 4.4/30.3**, so band 0.12 buys its H1 gain by sitting in cash 30% of H2, where it destroys **-5.82 pp** and **-0.518 of Sharpe**. Turnover confirms the flip count and not the P&L (3.49 -> 2.04 x/yr at near-flat gross 0.770 -> 0.747). KEEP paths over all 480 points: **4a 0/480**, 4b **18/480** — GATE=OFF 14/96 (idea 30's own ungated passes, reproduced), band 0.00 **0/96**, band 0.03 0/96, band 0.06 **4/96**, band 0.12 0/96; first-failing-bar census over the 462 failures H1+CAGR 116, DD 94, H2+OOS+DD+CAGR 72, H1+DD 42. **Rule 8** ((c, band) chosen on 2009-2016 by IS Sharpe, 2017-2026 read once, 4 cells): the chooser takes a non-zero band in **4/4 cells and always the WIDEST (c=0.80, band=0.12)**, and loses a mean **+0.4937 of OOS Sharpe against idea 30's own anchor** (+0.5036 against the OOS-best cell, which is the **RAW** gate at c=0.50) — the sharpest IS-chooser loss in this family, and unsurprising once the mechanism is named: 2009-2016 IS the decade a wide band keeps you invested through. One **PARK** by-product, not a KEEP: `band=0.06 / c=0.60 / q=1.00` (60% QQQ inside a +/-6% band + 40% sleeve) is **the family's first gated 4b pass** — 11.24%/0.9622/-18.86%, halves 1.012/0.931, OOS 1.035 at 10 bps and 10.84%/0.9314/-18.89%, OOS 1.007 at 25 bps, clearing all five bars on both panels at both rungs — but rule 8 does not select it, idea 30's **ungated** c=0.50 book beats it on Sharpe, drawdown AND OOS (13.04%/1.0405/-20.08%, OOS 1.038) with no gate at all, and it fails 4a on every bar. Panel degeneracy re-confirmed for this ETF-only book: over 240 matched cells **max |U56-B136| Sharpe 1.094e-04**, max |d CAGR| 1.082e-05. The statement to carry forward: **the 200d gate's H1 cost is the insurance premium itself, paid in a decade where the insurance was worthless; a band can move that premium between halves but not reduce it.** SURVIVORSHIP: both universes are current-constituent lists; QQQ's 2009-2017 run is the best large-cap decade in the sample and the entire H1 recovery is "stay invested in it". research/backtests/2026-09-07_does-a-BAND-recover-what-the-raw-200d-gate-burns-in-H1_cloud.py

No RULES change, no book promoted, no KEEP claimed; RULES.md, scan.py, bot.py, baseline.py and PROTOCOL.md untouched.** 96 known-null arms (3 panels x 4 target on-shares x 8 replicates of idea 191's episodic-Bernoulli zero-information ON series, episode length 5.89 matched to the record's 41 real ON series) were each priced against a POOL of 200 of their own circular rotations, 19,296 backtests at 10 bps; because a uniformly random K-subset of a uniformly random D-subset is a uniformly random K-subset, every (band, K) size is then EXACT from the hypergeometric law rather than resampled. **(a) ARITHMETIC FIRST: a band at the r-th order statistic has exchangeability size (K+1-r)/(K+1), so 'Q95' means 0.0952 / 0.0588 / 0.0594 / 0.0547 at K=20/50/100/200 and MAX COLLAPSES 0.0476 -> 0.0196 -> 0.0099 -> 0.0050 — the label misstates the 5% target by 1.90x at K=20 before any data is seen, and band and K cannot be picked independently. (b) REALISED: Q95/K=100 on the Sharpe statistic is 0.0531 (se 0.0212, t +0.15 vs 5%), i.e. IT HOLDS; drawdown is 0.0874 (1.75x) but only t +1.48 and is reported as a direction, not a finding. (c) THE ONE DECISIVE DEVIATION IS THE PANEL: 0.0748 U56 / 0.0826 BROAD136 / 0.0020 SMALL439 (t -24.36 vs 5%, and the same on the OOS window) — on the small panel clause 11b is not a 5% test at all. (d) THE PREMISE IS INERT: rotation correlation is +0.3646 below 5 rebalances and gone beyond 10 (+0.0611, then -0.04..-0.01), a random subset of ~975 rotations never draws near-neighbours, and the real arm's rank inside its own pool is near-uniform (mean 0.4592 vs 0.500, sd 0.2909 vs 0.289, share>0.95 0.0417 vs 0.050).** Rule 8: the IS-calibrated order statistic moves r by 1-2 (19->20, 48->49, 95->97, 190->192), beats the nominal Q95 out of sample in **1 of 4 rungs**, and has a WORSE mean OOS size error (0.0207 vs 0.0160) — so 'clause 11b needs a calibrated quantile' is not supported. BOTH KEEP PATHS on the known-null books: a zero-information overlay clears **4a 0/96** and **4b 14/96**, 13 of the 14 on U56 whose untreated control clears 4b by itself, SMALL439 0/32 — the carrier result of the same day's idea 435, reproduced from an unrelated construction. Recommendation (proposed only): print (K+1-r)/(K+1) beside every verdict, publish the panel beside every rotation-null claim, do not adopt a calibrated quantile, and do not read the band on the drawdown statistic without more arms.

Timing share of the total edge on the 55 positive-total gate cells: median **104.5%**, >=90% in 35/55. The incumbent's OOS composition edge is +0.0534/+0.0568 (U56), +0.0262/+0.0294 (B136) and **-0.013/-0.015 (SMALL439)**. **4a 0 of 150.** SPY OOS 15.38% / 0.8786 / -33.72%. **WHAT IT CHANGES:** idea 247's memo point 6 ("beats its own matched-realised-gross control by +0.0975 ... not idea 244's gross channel") is true of the STATIC gross channel and **false of the timed one** — against a control that de-grosses on the same days to the same exposure the margin is **+0.0083 full sample** (+0.0534 OOS at 10 bps). No RULES change, no book promoted, no KEEP claimed; RULES.md, products/scan.py, products/bot/bot.py, research/baseline.py and PROTOCOL.md untouched.** Gate first: idea 259's rule-8 n-dial result reproduces on its own four panels, arms and saturation cap — 3 of 4 panels disagree, S_CAGR minus S_SHARPE **-0.0242** OOS Sharpe and **+2.56 pp** OOS CAGR against its published -0.0254 / +2.53, and the level ladder EWALL 0.8571 > FWD20 0.8426 > S_SHARPE 0.7813 > S_CAGR 0.7571 against 0.8577 / 0.8428 / 0.7815 / 0.7561. Design: five one-dimensional dials off one EWall(G) base book (n, cadence, gross, volgate, trim) x twelve panels (U56, B136, BSTK100, SMALL439 + eight pre-registered seeded sub-panels) = **60 cells, 348 arms, every point reported**; ONE tuned parameter, the dial value, chosen on IS 2009-2016 and OOS 2017+ read once; 10 bps, weekly base cadence, next-day execution. **Q1 (is the pair general?) NO — it is an n-dial phenomenon.** The two selectors disagree in **7 of 12 n cells (58.3%)** but in only 2/12 trim and 1/12 each on cadence, gross and volgate; pooled 12/60 = 20.0%. **Q2 (is the exchange rate a constant?) NO for the numerator, YES for the denominator.** Pooled it is **28.63 pp of CAGR per Sharpe point** against the n dial's **105.8**, and volgate (-13.21) and cadence (-17.94) carry the **wrong sign** — S_CAGR gives up CAGR *and* Sharpe there; within the n dial alone the per-cell rate spans **1.71 to 42.30 (25x)**. Permutation, 20,000 draws, with a **blocked** variant that shuffles dial labels within each panel (the exact null for this balanced 12x5 design): dOOS **CAGR** spread of per-dial means 1.8238, p **0.0010 unrestricted / 0.0001 blocked**; dOOS **Sharpe** spread 0.0474, p **0.2820 / 0.3081**; per-cell xr spread 1075.98, p 0.0832 / 0.3317. So the reportable invariant is that choosing on CAGR costs about **-0.014 of OOS Sharpe wherever you do it**, while what it buys is entirely dial-specific. **Q3 (is the sign reliable?) NO** — the +CAGR/-Sharpe shape holds in only **7 of the 12** disagreeing cells; 3 are a free lunch (S_CAGR better on both: B136/n, BSTK100/n, S5_M120/n) and 2 are both worse (S0_B60/cadence, S5_M120/volgate). **Q4 (does either selector earn its keep?) NO** — S_SHARPE minus DONOTHING **+0.0038 OOS Sharpe (t +0.31, wins 27/60)**, S_CAGR minus DONOTHING **-0.0098 (t -0.73, 25/60)**; mean OOS Sharpe S_SHARPE 0.7618 / DONOTHING 0.7580 / S_CAGR 0.7482, all below SPY **0.8817** and the live RULES v2 book **0.9196** (OOS CAGR 9.34% / 8.95% / 7.91% vs SPY 15.44%, RULES v2 7.01% at MaxDD -14.4%). Another idea-229 selection-loses instance. **Both KEEP paths over all 348 arms: 4a against the LIVE RULES v2 8, against the superseded v1 107 (13x, reproducing idea 482 on a fresh grid), 4b 22 — and the two sets DO NOT INTERSECT** (the 8 4a passers are all trim arms failing 4b on CAGR; the 22 4b passers all fail 4a). Among the 120 selected arms 4a 3 / 4b 5 against **4 of 60 for do-nothing**, so selection does not raise the pass rate, and all five 4b picks are already-known rows (U56 FWD20 = idea 2's construction; U56/B136 V1.00 = the plain above-MA equal-weight book with the vol gate switched off). No new KEEP-candidate, no memo. **Leg B, the queue's literal ask:** 2,162 committed CSVs scanned (1 skipped over 200k rows), idea 241's bar on replication and reporting axes applied, **73 files -> 6,956 menus**. It corroborates Leg A's sign and magnitude file-clustered (**dOOS Sharpe -0.0162, t -3.07, negative in 36/73; dOOS CAGR +0.63 pp, t +5.07, positive in 52/73; xr 38.74**) and reproduces the disagreement ordering (n 44.8%, trim 44.4%, gross 14.3%, cadence 9.9%), but it **cannot resolve dial-specificity**: family heterogeneity is p < 0.0001 menu-pooled and **p = 0.2757 (CAGR) / 0.3114 (Sharpe) once clustered on file**, because one file contributes 1,028 of the menus. Only the controlled grid, where every dial is measured on every panel, answers the question. Survivorship stated: B136/BSTK100 are current constituents, SMALL439 a current screen, and the seeded sub-panels inherit it. research/backtests/2026-09-09_is-S_CAGR-vs-S_SHARPE-a-general-selector-pair_B.result.md

Result: **302,043 fit calls at 244 distinct sites**, and the right statistic is **p/N** (an in-sample fit absorbs p/N of ANY regressor for free — verified by Monte Carlo at the record's own (N, p) pairs for a continuous design and for group indicators: 0.088 vs 0.090 predicted, 0.919 vs 0.920, 1.000 at p>=N). **THE CENSUS — agrees, and corrects.** The cloud run's static scan reported 70 files with a fit call, 5 wide, **3 wide-and-unfolded**; the runtime census confirms its conclusion (the >10-parameter regime is not the record: 64 of 244 sites are p=2, 111 are p<=10) but re-counts the exposed set: **134 sites clear p>10 in 7 scripts, and 116 of them are TWO-SIDED Frisch-Waugh within transforms** (`x` and `y` demeaned by the same cell means — a `groupby().transform("mean")` family the static scan did not see at all), where the in-sample fit IS the estimator and 'refit out of fold' is the wrong question. The remedy for that family is dof, not a fold split; the record's largest such site already uses cluster-robust SE. **RULE 8 + BOTH KEEP PATHS** on idea 78's committed 300 B136 books, parameters chosen on 2009-2016 and 2017-2026 read only to score the pick, 258 rows: **an in-sample fitted control is the incumbent selector in disguise — it picks the IS-Sharpe argmax on 19 of 21 cells (out of fold, 0-4 of 21)** — and **no fitted-control arm beats ranking on raw dispersion with no control at all** (RAW-sd OOS Sharpe 1.1163 / rank 8.0/50 vs CTRL-fit 0.998-1.088 and SD-resid 1.028-1.062). **4a 24/258 against the live RULES v2, 4b 110/258 against SPY, both 0/258** (binding 4b bars CAGR 97, H2 37, DD 26, OOS 11, H1 4) — nothing promotable, so no memo; this agrees with the cloud run that fixing the fit changes the inference, not the book. No RULES change, no book promoted, no KEEP claimed; RULES.md, PROTOCOL.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Gate first, and it is worth stating: averaging each panel's metrics does NOT reproduce idea 277's published EWall curve (max |dSharpe| 0.0579, |dMaxDD| 0.0339, the gap vanishing at s=1.000 where the rung is a single panel) because idea 277 built each rung by POOLING the six seed panels' return series into one portfolio; under its own aggregation the curve reproduces to max abs diff 2.2e-16 on Sharpe and 8.3e-17 on CAGR/MaxDD/OOS across 9/9 rungs. The decomposition is an exact log identity — log Sharpe = MEAN + VOL + DIV + const + TIMING + GROSS&COST, with rho defined so it closes — and its residual never exceeds 0.0064 over 27 grid points (3 gross modes x 3 cost rungs x 3 windows, all reported). At 10 bps the -0.4698 log fall from s=0 to s=1 splits MEAN -0.5220 (111%), VOL +0.3967 (-84%), DIVERSIFICATION +0.0177 (-4%, of which correlation +0.0206 and concentration -0.0026), TIMING -0.2856 (61%) and GROSS&COST -0.0813 (17%). So the two beta legs NET to -0.1253, about 27% of the fall — mean name return 19.76% -> 11.68% annualised against name vol 28.58% -> 19.21%, the numerator falling faster — while the single largest channel is TIMING, the weight-return covariation the 200d/vol gate produces, which the queue did not name. The BREADTH half is absent: k is fixed at 36, rho moves 0.342 -> 0.327 and is not even monotone (0.294 at s=0.25), N_eff moves 34.75 -> 33.97, and the concentration leg is worth 0.6% of the fall; idea 277's halving `disp` column has no channel into an un-ranked book's Sharpe except through H, which moves 0.0295 -> 0.0323. RULE 8: channel slopes fitted on 2009-2016 only and read on 2017-2026 untouched, the IS-fitted model beats the naive IS-constant 9/9 and the OOS-level flat line 9/9 (MAE 0.0962 vs 0.1224 vs 0.1467 at 10 bps), the largest-IS-slope channel is the largest-OOS-slope channel 9/9 (MEAN both times), it overpredicts (-0.4858 IS vs -0.4036 OOS), and the DIV leg's slope flips sign out of sample (+0.0578 -> -0.0251). The OOS curve is monotone 8/8 and the fall is 4.4x the within-share seed sd (0.3878 vs 0.0882). KEEP paths over the 441 rung books: 4a 0/441, 4b 57/441, both 0/441, binding bars CAGR 298 / H2 249 / DD 225 / H1 213 / OOS 213, and every 4b pass sits at s <= 0.625 with none at s >= 0.750 — the ETF share is an admissibility dial, not a book. - 2026-09-09 (cloud, idea 285 is-the-4b-footprint-a-monotone-function-of-cap-mix) — **ANSWERED; the queue's premise holds in DIRECTION and fails in FORM, and the substantive finding is that THERE IS NO SINGLE ADMISSIBILITY CURVE. No RULES change, no book promoted, no KEEP claimed; RULES.md, PROTOCOL.md, scan.py, bot.py and baseline.py untouched.** Idea 276's MIX construction rebuilt exactly as idea 286 rebuilt it — k=40 names per panel, share q from the 439-name sub-$2B panel (44 max_1d_move>=1.0 names dropped first) and 1-q from the 100-name non-ETF large-cap pool, all panels on ONE common window (2010-01-04..2026-09-04, 4,194 rows), SPY joined as a benchmark column only — at the finer resolution the queue asked for: **two tuned parameters, both reporting axes with every point published, q in {0.00,0.05,...,1.00} (21 rungs vs idea 276's 5) x n in {10,20,30}, 20 draws per rung (vs 8) = 420 panels and 1,680 arm-rows**, plus EWall as the un-ranked control and the live RULES v2 book as the 4a comparand on each panel; 10 bps, weekly, next-day execution, 260-day warm-up skip, 75% gross, seed 20260909. Gate first: the ladder reproduces and sharpens — mean gate breadth falls **0.6810 -> 0.3236 with Spearman(q, breadth) = -1.0000 exactly** against idea 286's -0.9801 on five rungs, and SPY is identical on every rung (0.8615 full, 0.8820 OOS) so nothing below is a benchmark artefact. **(1) NOT MONOTONE, BUT STEEP.** The joint 4b pass rate runs 0.35/0.10/0.70/0.50 at q=0 to 0.00 everywhere at q=1 (EWall/top10/top20/top30) with Spearman **-0.920 / -0.709 / -0.941 / -0.794**, yet **2 / 4 / 3 / 1 of the 20 q->q+0.05 transitions go the WRONG way**, and every one of the 24 (arm, bar) curves has between 1 and 7 wrong-way steps. 'Monotone' is a five-rung statement: at 8 draws x 5 rungs the noise is invisible, at 20 x 21 it is not. **160 of 1,680 arm-rows (9.5%) clear 4b and 5 (0.30%) clear 4a**, and one published boundary moves — the last q carrying any 4b pass is **0.60, not idea 276's 0.50** (top20 and EWall each on 1 of 20 draws there), so the 0.5 edge was a grid point. **(2) THE HEADLINE: THE BINDING ORDER REVERSES ACROSS BOOK SIZE.** First q whose bar pass rate drops below 50% — EWall H1 0.50 / H2 0.05 / OOS 0.25 / DDcap **0.00** / CAGRfloor 0.50; top10 0.40 / **0.00** / 0.05 / **0.00** / 0.50; top20 0.55 / **0.30** / 0.35 / 0.85 / 0.35; top30 0.55 / 0.20 / 0.35 / **never** / **0.05**. At n=30 the CAGR floor is gone by q=0.05 while the DD cap never binds at all (pass rate >= 0.60 at every rung, a 30-of-40-name book being barely concentrated); at n=10 and at EWall the DD cap is already binding at q=0 while the CAGR floor survives to q=0.50. **An 'admissibility q' is therefore a property of (cap mix, book size) JOINTLY, and the record's per-panel verdicts have been reading one off the other.** **(3) ONE BAR NEVER CUTS: the rule-8 OOS bar is the SOLE binding bar in 0 of 1,520 4b failures — 0.000 on all four arms.** Fails / sole-fails per arm: EWall H1 .539/.005, H2 .893/.003, OOS .815/.000, DDcap .961/.091, CAGR .641/.000; top10 .595/.002, .897/.010, .845/.000, .885/.081, .577/.000; top20 .635/.003, .942/.082, .815/.000, .322/.006, .888/.018; top30 .505/.000, .787/.003, .695/.000, .050/.000, .998/.193. The cutting bar is the **DD cap on diffuse books** (EWall, top10) and the **CAGR floor on wide ranked books** (top30), with H2 the most-failed bar everywhere. This is NOT a proposal to delete the OOS leg — it is a statement that the leg should stop being counted as an independent test on evidence like this. **(4) RULE 8 AND BOTH KEEP PATHS: n chosen per draw on IS Sharpe (<= 2016-12-31) and read once on 2017..2026-09-04 at all 21 rungs.** Median OOS Sharpe falls **1.032 at q=0 to 0.215 at q=1** (EWall control 1.005 -> 0.147; RULES v2 on the same panel 1.112 -> 0.520; SPY 0.882 flat), median OOS CAGR 10.9% -> 1.7%, median OOS MaxDD -16.1% -> -28.0%. **Pooled over 420 draws the chooser beats the live RULES v2 book OOS on 16.7% and SPY OOS on 32.4%; its picks clear 4b on 10.2% and 4a on 0.5%.** The median OOS Sharpe crosses SPY between q=0.30 and q=0.35 while the SHARE of draws beating SPY crosses 50% between q=0.40 and q=0.45 — two different 'where it stops working' answers from one grid, the same level-vs-rate distinction the binding curve makes. **NO KEEP: top20's 70% 4b pass rate at q=0 is a 40-name large-cap random draw, i.e. idea 486's random-draw base rate restated on a different construction, not a new book.** Honest limits recorded in the result file: 20 draws per rung gives a pass-rate standard error of ~0.11 at 50%, which is the size of the wrong-way steps, so the non-monotonicity claim is a claim about what the record can RESOLVE; k is held at idea 276's 40 so the (q x k) interaction is untested; both ends of the ladder are current-constituent survivor sets so every LEVEL is optimistic and only the q-contrast is claimed; and the 4a leg is barely exercised at 5 passes in 1,680 rows. Rule 8 applied to the WINDOW itself: its width **ordering** transfers (Spearman IS vs full **+0.794**) but its **location** does not — the two windows overlap **346/346**, the full-sample window is **nested inside** the IS window in **215/346**, and the IS window's lower edge sits at or below the full one in **344/346** (mean 0.045 vs 0.173); the IS window is a **superset, not a forecast**, which is idea 128/138's own caveat (an IS drawdown cap is measured on a window that cannot express a deep drawdown) surfacing as window location.
